p-001.title: How preheating flask dey work
p-001.summary: If you first pour hot water inside flask to preheat am, di drink go stay hot for much longer time.
p-001.principle: Heat dey waste through conduction, convection and radiation. Di vacuum layer dey reduce conduction and convection, and di silver-coated wall dey reduce radiation. Di heat wey go first warm di container wall na $Q = mc\Delta T$.
p-001.example: To warm 500mL flask stainless steel wall (about 200g, $c\approx0.5\ \mathrm{J/g\cdot K}$) from 20°C go 90°C, e need about 7kJ. If you no preheat am, di drink go give dis heat, and e go cool about 3 to 4°C for di first moment.
p-001.actionItem: This morning, fill your flask with boiling water, leave am for 3 minutes, pour am comot, den put your drink inside.

p-002.title: Make hot food cool before you put am for fridge
p-002.summary: If you put hot soup inside fridge just like dat, e go warm other food too and electricity go cost pass.
p-002.principle: Fridge must pump out di heat $Q = mc\Delta T$ wey enter am through compressor. Shallow and wide bowl get bigger surface area, so e go cool faster through $P = hA\Delta T$.
p-002.example: To cool 3L soup (80°C) go 5°C, about $3000\times4.18\times75\approx940\ \mathrm{kJ}$ go become fridge work. If you first cool am for room temperature reach 40°C, you don remove almost half of dat one.
p-002.actionItem: Today, share di food wey you cook inside shallow bowls, make e cool reach 30 to 40°C, den put am for fridge within 2 hours.

p-003.title: Use bubble wrap insulate window
p-003.summary: If you stick air-cap (bubble wrap) for window, di still air layer go reduce heat loss well well.
p-003.principle: Thermal conductivity of still air na about $0.026\ \mathrm{W/m\cdot K}$, wey be 1/40 of glass ($1.0$). For heat loss $Q = UA\Delta T$, di $U$ go reduce.
p-003.example: For single window of 2 $\mathrm{m^2}$, with 20°C difference between inside and outside, if $U\approx5.8$, na 232W loss. If air-cap bring am down to $U\approx3.5$, e go be 140W, so you save about 90W.
p-003.actionItem: Today, spray water for glass according to di window size, den stick di flat side of di air-cap for di glass.

p-004.title: Electric blanket vs boiler
p-004.summary: If na only you dey for house, electric blanket wey dey warm only your body area dey more efficient pass to warm di whole room.
p-004.principle: Heating energy dey proportional to di size of di space wey you wan warm, as $E = Pt$. If you warm only di small space between your body and blanket, di heat wey you need small.
p-004.example: If you use 50W electric blanket for 8 hours, na 0.4kWh. If you warm whole room with 4kW heating for 8 hours, e fit reach 32kWh, so di difference na many times.
p-004.actionItem: Tonight, reduce boiler setting by 1 to 2°C and put electric blanket for low temperature make you try am.

p-005.title: Rice cooker warm vs freeze small portions
p-005.summary: To freeze rice for small portions and reheat am dey use less electricity than to leave rice cooker for warm mode pass 12 hours.
p-005.principle: Warm mode must keep replacing heat loss $P = UA\Delta T$ through di wall. Microwave reheat dey use $E = Pt$ only for di moment wey e need am.
p-005.example: If you leave about 60W warm mode for 24 hours, na 1.44kWh. To reheat one bowl (200g) with 700W for 2 minutes, na about 0.023kWh.
p-005.actionItem: Today, wrap di rice wey remain for plastic wrap one bowl by one bowl, freeze am, and off di warm button.

p-006.title: Smartphone battery for cold
p-006.summary: Di reason why phone dey suddenly off for below-zero weather na say di chemical reaction inside battery don slow down.
p-006.principle: Ion movement speed dey follow Arrhenius equation $k = Ae^{-E_a/RT}$, so e dey drop sharply as temperature low, internal resistance go increase and voltage go fall.
p-006.example: Lithium-ion battery fit lose to about 70 to 80% usable capacity for 0°C, and less than dat for -10°C. Phone wey be 100% fit show 30% outside, den e off.
p-006.actionItem: When you dey go out, put your phone for inside pocket, and if e off, warm am with your body before you on am again.

p-007.title: Check car battery for winter before jump start
p-007.summary: Di reason why car no dey start for below-zero weather na say battery power reduce and engine oil don thick.
p-007.principle: Battery output na $P = V I$ and for low temperature, internal resistance $r$ go increase, so terminal voltage $V = \varepsilon - Ir$ go drop.
p-007.example: If starting current na 400A and internal resistance increase from 0.01Ω go 0.02Ω, voltage drop go increase from 4V go 8V, and 12V battery go struggle to start di car.
p-007.actionItem: Today, off headlights and heater before you start di car, and if di battery don pass 3 years, go check am.

p-008.title: How to walk for icy road
p-008.summary: For ice, to reduce your step and put your whole foot flat na di way to use di most friction.
p-008.principle: Di condition to no slip na horizontal force $F \le \mu N$. For ice, $\mu\approx0.05\text{-}0.1$ na about 1/10 of dry asphalt ($\approx0.7$).
p-008.example: For walking, if di ratio of horizontal part of front foot to di vertical force $\tan\theta$ pass $\mu$, you go slip. If you cut your step in half, $\theta$ go small and e go enter safe range.
p-008.actionItem: Today, when snow dey fall, reduce your step to half of normal and comot your hands from pocket.

p-009.title: Leave middle empty for microwave
p-009.summary: If you arrange food for di edge like donut shape, microwave go heat am more evenly.
p-009.principle: Microwave dey heat with 2.45GHz standing wave, and hot and cold spots go form according to wavelength $\lambda = c/f \approx 12.2\ \mathrm{cm}$.
p-009.example: Di centre of di plate dey often cold because microwaves dey weak there. If you arrange food round di edge and stir am once for middle, temperature difference fit reduce by more than 20°C.
p-009.actionItem: Today, for food wey you wan warm, leave di middle empty, put am for di edge, and stir am once when half of di time reach.

p-010.title: Boil with lid on
p-010.summary: If you just cover pot with lid, gas bill go reduce noticeably.
p-010.principle: When water evaporate, latent heat of vaporization $L \approx 2260\ \mathrm{J/g}$ go escape. Di lid dey stop steam and convection loss, so with di same heat e go boil faster.
p-010.example: To heat 1L water from 20°C go 100°C need $Q = 1000\times4.18\times80\approx334\ \mathrm{kJ}$. If you cover am with lid, time and gas usually reduce by about 20 to 30%.
p-010.actionItem: Today, when you dey boil noodles and soup, cover di pot from di start.

p-011.title: Fill freezer, leave fridge section empty
p-011.summary: If freezer full, temperature no go rise too much when you open di door, but di fridge section need air to move.
p-011.principle: Ice and food wey get big heat capacity $C = mc$ dey store coldness and reduce di heat change $\Delta T = Q/C$. Di fridge section need cold air circulation.
p-011.example: If you open di door for 10 seconds, about 100L of freezer air go change, and empty place go rise about 5°C, but full freezer go recover faster because di food dey buffer am.
p-011.actionItem: Today, freeze some water bottles and fill di empty places for your freezer.

p-012.title: Reflector behind radiator
p-012.summary: If you stick aluminium foil for di wall behind radiator, di heat go return inside di room.
p-012.principle: Radiant heat na $P = \varepsilon\sigma A T^4$, and shiny aluminium get low emissivity and high reflectivity, so e dey reflect infrared go di room side.
p-012.example: Part of di heat from radiator wey face outer wall dey enter di wall. If reflector return am, with di same heating, heat loss for di wall side go reduce and di room go warm faster.
p-012.actionItem: Today, stick thick foil reflector behind radiator wey dey outer wall.

p-013.title: Hunt standby power
p-013.summary: Appliances wey look like say dem off still dey chop electricity if dem dey plug for socket.
p-013.principle: Energy na $E = Pt$. 5W standby look small, but e dey pile up for 24 hours a day, 8760 hours a year.
p-013.example: If total standby power na 20W, e be $0.02\times8760 \approx 175\ \mathrm{kWh}$, and if one kWh na 200 won, e be 35,000 won per year.
p-013.actionItem: Today, tie TV, set-top box and chargers for one switch power strip and off am before you sleep.

p-014.title: Lower heating by 1°C
p-014.summary: Even if you lower room temperature by just 1°C, heating energy go reduce noticeably.
p-014.principle: Heat loss na $Q = UA\Delta T$, e dey proportional to di inside-outside temperature difference $\Delta T$.
p-014.example: If outside na 0°C and you lower inside from 22°C go 21°C, $\Delta T$ go reduce from 22 go 21, about 4.5%, and heating energy go reduce by almost di same amount.
p-014.actionItem: Today, lower your heating setting by 1°C and wear cardigan.

p-015.title: Curtain length and window heat loss
p-015.summary: Thick curtain wey reach di floor dey stop di cold air circulation near di window.
p-015.principle: Air near cold glass dey denser, e dey go down and convection dey form. Curtain dey reduce di convection coefficient $Q = hA\Delta T$ for heat loss $h$.
p-015.example: If you close thick curtain from window frame reach floor, heat loss for di window area dey usually reduce by 10 to 25%. If gap dey for di curtain, cold air go flow out like chimney.
p-015.actionItem: Tonight when sun set, draw di curtain fully and check say di bottom edge touch di floor.

p-016.title: Block draft for door gap
p-016.summary: 1mm gap for door dey chop your winter heating bill.
p-016.principle: Air wey dey enter through di gap, you must warm am by volume flow $\dot V$, and na $P = \rho c \dot V \Delta T$. Air $\rho c \approx 1.2\ \mathrm{kJ/m^3K}$.
p-016.example: If gap draft na 20 $\mathrm{m^3/h}$, $\Delta T=20$°C, e be $P \approx 1.2\times20\times20/3.6\approx133\ \mathrm{W}$. If you block half with weatherstrip, you go save about 66W.
p-016.actionItem: Today, stick weatherstrip for di gap under di door and around di edges of windows.

p-017.title: Tyre pressure for winter
p-017.summary: When temperature drop, tyre pressure also dey drop.
p-017.principle: For ideal gas with constant volume, $P/T = \text{const}$. As absolute temperature $T$ reduce, pressure $P$ dey reduce proportionally too.
p-017.example: Tyre wey be 35psi for 20°C (293K) go drop about 3.6psi to $35\times263/293\approx31.4\ \mathrm{psi}$ for -10°C (263K).
p-017.actionItem: This morning, measure tyre pressure when e still cold and fill am reach di recommended value.

p-018.title: Why mittens dey warmer
p-018.summary: Mittens wey fingers join together dey warmer pass gloves.
p-018.principle: Heat loss na $Q = hA\Delta T$, e dey proportional to exposed surface area $A$. If you put fingers together, surface area reduce and dem dey share heat.
p-018.example: Mittens get about 20 to 30% less exposed surface area than gloves wey wrap five fingers separately, so with di same insulation, heat loss dey reduce by di same amount.
p-018.actionItem: Today, for very cold day, wear mittens on top gloves.

p-019.title: Air layers for layered clothing
p-019.summary: Many thin clothes fit warm pass one thick cloth.
p-019.principle: Still air between clothes dey insulate. Total thermal resistance $R = \sum d_i/k_i$ dey increase as layers dey increase.
p-019.example: One 5mm layer of still air dey add $R = 0.005/0.026\approx0.19\ \mathrm{m^2K/W}$. If you dey hot, remove one layer so say sweat no go cool you down.
p-019.actionItem: Today, when you dey go out, try wear 3 layers: brushed inner wear, shirt, then windbreaker.

p-020.title: Dry clothes indoors and ventilation
p-020.summary: If you leave space between indoor clothes and use dehumidifier or ventilate, dem go dry faster.
p-020.principle: Evaporation rate na $\dot m \propto A(p_s - p_a)$, e dey proportional to surface area and vapour pressure difference.
p-020.example: If about 500g of water from 1kg wet laundry evaporate, e go take about $500\times2.26\approx1130\ \mathrm{kJ}$. If you spread clothes out, drying time fit nearly reduce to half.
p-020.actionItem: Today, hang clothes with space between each one and put fan for low.

p-021.title: How to prevent hot glass from breaking
p-021.summary: If you suddenly pour hot water inside glass, e fit break.
p-021.principle: Temperature difference dey cause different expansion, so thermal stress $\sigma = E\alpha\Delta T$ dey form. Ordinary soda-lime glass no dey resist am well.
p-021.example: If $E\approx70\ \mathrm{GPa}$, $\alpha\approx9\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$ and di temperature difference na $\Delta T=70$°C, $\sigma\approx44\ \mathrm{MPa}$ fit cause surface fracture.
p-021.actionItem: Today, for cold glass, first warm am with warm water before you pour hot drink.

p-022.title: Match induction pot bottom
p-022.summary: Induction dey work well when di pot bottom flat and di size correct.
p-022.principle: Induction heating dey produce heat of $P = I^2R$ direct for di pot bottom through eddy current. Di pot must be magnetic material, and di better di contact, di higher di efficiency.
p-022.example: If pot diameter small pass di coil, heat go reduce and e go take longer time. Efficiency na about 85 to 90%, wey high pass gas (about 40 to 50%).
p-022.actionItem: Today, put magnet for your pot bottom to check if e dey stick.

p-023.title: Use air fryer convection well
p-023.summary: Air fryer need space between food before e go crisp.
p-023.principle: For forced convection wey dey circulate hot air fast, $Q = hA\Delta T$ dey increase for $h$. If you stack food, di $A$ wey air dey touch go reduce.
p-023.example: Oven convection $h\approx10\ \mathrm{W/m^2K}$, fan convection $h\approx30\text{-}50$, so e dey 3 to 5 times faster. If you spread am for one layer, e fit even cut 10 minutes.
p-023.actionItem: Today, spread food for one layer for di air fryer basket, no let dem overlap.

p-024.title: Clean dryer filter
p-024.summary: If you empty dryer lint filter, drying time go short.
p-024.principle: When filter block, air flow rate $\dot V$ dey reduce and moisture removal rate $\dot m = \dot V\Delta\omega\rho$ dey drop.
p-024.example: Blocked filter fit increase drying time by 20 to 30%. If one cycle wey be 80 minutes become 100 minutes, e go cost extra 0.4kWh (for 2kW).
p-024.actionItem: Today, open your dryer lint filter and remove di lint.

p-025.title: Reduce static electricity for winter
p-025.summary: Di reason why door handle dey shock you for winter na say charge no fit escape from dry air.
p-025.principle: Charge $Q$ wey build up from friction dey behave like capacitor $V = Q/C$, voltage dey rise, and if air dry, discharge slow and e fit reach thousands of V.
p-025.example: If human body $C\approx100\ \mathrm{pF}$ get $Q=0.3\ \mu\mathrm{C}$, e be $V = 3000\ \mathrm{V}$. If you raise humidity to 40% or more, di charge go leak out gradually.
p-025.actionItem: Today, before you hold door handle, first touch key or wall to discharge.

p-026.title: Prevent power strip overload
p-026.summary: If you plug many big heaters inside one power strip, e get risk of overheating and fire.
p-026.principle: Power $P = VI$, so for 220V, na $I = P/V$, and heat dey proportional to square of current as $P_\text{heat} = I^2R$.
p-026.example: 1500W heater + 1000W electric kettle na $2500/220\approx11.4\ \mathrm{A}$, wey pass common 10A power strip. Even if current increase by just 10%, heat go increase by 21%.
p-026.actionItem: Today, check di rating of your power strip (e.g. 10A) and plug heaters direct for wall socket.

p-027.title: Charge battery 20 to 80%
p-027.summary: If you use smartphone between 20 to 80%, di battery go last longer.
p-027.principle: High charging voltage dey speed up electrolyte breakdown. Degradation rate dey sensitive to temperature as $k\propto e^{-E_a/RT}$.
p-027.example: E dey known say if you avoid 100% charge and heat exposure, di cycles wey battery fit keep 80% capacity fit increase from about 500 by some hundreds more.
p-027.actionItem: Today, turn on 'optimised charging' or 80% limit for your phone.

p-028.title: How much you go save if you change to LED
p-028.summary: Even if bulbs give di same brightness, LED dey use far less electricity.
p-028.principle: We dey compare am with luminous efficacy $\eta = \Phi/P$ (lm/W). Incandescent na about 13 lm/W, LED na about 100 lm/W or more.
p-028.example: For 800 lm bulb, incandescent na 60W, LED na 8W. If e dey on 5 hours a day, you go save $0.052\times5\times365\approx95\ \mathrm{kWh}$ per year.
p-028.actionItem: Today, change one bulb for di room wey dey on di longest to LED.

p-029.title: Why iron handle dey colder
p-029.summary: Even for di same temperature, metal dey feel far colder pass wood.
p-029.principle: Contact heat flux dey proportional to thermal effusivity $e = \sqrt{k\rho c}$. If heat escape quickly, you go feel say e cold.
p-029.example: Metal $e\approx10{,}000\text{-}20{,}000$, wood $e\approx400$ (SI), so di difference na many times. Even for di same 0°C, iron go feel far colder.
p-029.actionItem: Today, when you dey go out for winter, hold metal handle with gloves on or wrap am with cloth.

p-030.title: How to prevent frozen pipe burst
p-030.summary: If temperature drop below zero, water for pipe go freeze, volume go increase, and pipe fit burst.
p-030.principle: When water freeze, volume dey increase by about 9%. For closed pipe, pressure dey rise a lot and di pipe go break through $\Delta P = K\Delta V/V$.
p-030.example: If you calculate with bulk modulus $K\approx2\ \mathrm{GPa}$, e dey reach hundreds of MPa in theory, so e go burst. If small water dey flow, e no dey easily freeze.
p-030.actionItem: Today, if forecast show below zero, open tap very small and wrap insulation round di meter.

p-031.title: Make you off or on heating when you go out
p-031.summary: For short outing, keep di heating; for long one, e better to lower am.
p-031.principle: Heat loss rate na $P = UA(T_\text{in}-T_\text{out})$ and di lower di temperature, di less di loss. Energy to reheat na heat capacity $C\Delta T$.
p-031.example: If you go out 12 hours, lower di room from 22°C to 17°C, loss go reduce by about 25%, and reheat heat small pass dat, so na net gain. For 2 to 3 hours, di gain small.
p-031.actionItem: Today, if you go dey out for 6 hours or more, put am for away mode to lower am, and for short outing, leave am as e be.

p-032.title: Braking distance for snowy road
p-032.summary: For snowy road, braking distance dey increase to many times of dry road.
p-032.principle: Braking distance na $d = v^2/(2\mu g)$. E dey proportional to square of speed and inversely proportional to friction coefficient.
p-032.example: For 50km/h (13.9m/s), dry road $\mu=0.7$ na $d\approx14\ \mathrm{m}$, snowy road $\mu=0.2$ na $d\approx49\ \mathrm{m}$. If you reduce speed to 30km/h, e be about 18m.
p-032.actionItem: Today, for snowy road, reduce your speed to half of normal and increase di gap between cars.

p-033.title: Protect your back when you dey shovel snow
p-033.summary: When you dey scoop snow, if you hold di shovel handle long and use your body, di load for your back go reduce.
p-033.principle: Lever torque na $\tau = Fd$. Di farther di load from your waist, di bigger di moment for your waist.
p-033.example: If you lift 5kg of snow with arm stretched out 0.6m from your waist, e be $\tau\approx5\times9.8\times0.6\approx29\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$; if you bring am close to your body for 0.2m, e be about 10N·m, wey be 1/3.
p-033.actionItem: Today, when you dey scoop snow, lift small small often, near your body, and use your legs instead of your back.

p-034.title: How to open bottle cap easily
p-034.summary: Tight bottle cap go open if you increase di radius of your hand to increase torque.
p-034.principle: Torque na $\tau = Fr$. Even with di same force, if you increase di radius $r$, torque go increase proportionally.
p-034.example: If cap diameter na 3cm ($r=1.5\ \mathrm{cm}$) and di torque wey you need na 3N·m, e be $F=200\ \mathrm{N}$. With opener, if $r=6\ \mathrm{cm}$, e be $F=50\ \mathrm{N}$, wey be 1/4.
p-034.actionItem: Today, wrap rubber glove or towel round di cap to grip am, or use bottle opener tool.

p-035.title: Before you climb on top chair
p-035.summary: When you dey climb chair, di centre of gravity must dey above di base so you no go fall.
p-035.principle: Object dey stable when di vertical line from di centre of gravity dey inside di base. Tilt limit na $\tan\theta = b/h$.
p-035.example: For base wey wide $b=20\ \mathrm{cm}$, if person centre of gravity height na $h=100\ \mathrm{cm}$, e go fall once e tilt only $\theta=\arctan0.2\approx11^\circ$.
p-035.actionItem: Today, for high places, use stable step ladder instead of chair.

p-036.title: Put ladder at 75 degrees
p-036.summary: If ladder too upright, e go fall back; if you lay am down too much, e go slip.
p-036.principle: Di condition so ladder no go slip na $\tan\theta \ge 1/(2\mu)$ (ignore wall friction).
p-036.example: If floor $\mu=0.4$, then $\tan\theta \ge 1.25$, that is $\theta\ge51^\circ$. Safety standard of about 75° (put di base out by 1/4 of di length) dey recommended.
p-036.actionItem: Today, set up ladder with di base 1/4 of di ladder length away from di wall.

p-037.title: Bathroom mirror fog
p-037.summary: Di reason why mirror dey blur after shower na say water vapour dey condense below dew point.
p-037.principle: If surface temperature dey below dew point $T_d$, condensation go happen. Approximation na $T_d \approx T - (100-RH)/5$.
p-037.example: If bathroom na 30°C and humidity 90%, e be $T_d\approx28$°C. If mirror na 25°C, e go condense. If you use exhaust fan reduce humidity to 60%, e be $T_d\approx14$°C.
p-037.actionItem: Today, on di exhaust fan when you dey bath and leave am for 10 minutes more after you finish.

p-038.title: No drag heavy furniture
p-038.summary: For heavy furniture, e easier to lift one side, put cloth under am and move am than to push am.
p-038.principle: Static friction force na $f = \mu_s N$. If you put cloth, $\mu$ go reduce and e go prevent floor damage too.
p-038.example: For 50kg wardrobe, if $\mu=0.5$, e be $f=0.5\times50\times9.8\approx245\ \mathrm{N}$. If furniture pad make $\mu=0.2$, e go be 98N, wey reduce by 60%.
p-038.actionItem: Today, put felt pad or towel under furniture legs and slide am to move am.

p-039.title: Measure electric kettle water
p-039.summary: If you boil only wetin you go drink, electricity and time go reduce by di same amount.
p-039.principle: Heat to boil na $Q = mc\Delta T$, e dey proportional to di mass of water $m$.
p-039.example: To boil 1L from 20°C to 100°C need 334kJ ≈ 0.093kWh. For one cup (250mL), e be 0.023kWh, wey be 1/4.
p-039.actionItem: Today, look di cup mark and put only di water wey you need to boil.

p-040.title: Leave space behind fridge
p-040.summary: If you push fridge against wall, heat no go fit comot and electricity go cost more.
p-040.principle: Heat from compressor dey comot through natural convection from di back heat sink. If air circulation block for $Q = hA\Delta T$, $h$ go reduce.
p-040.example: If heat dissipation block and condenser temperature rise by 10°C, efficiency (COP) go drop and power consumption fit increase by about 10 to 15%. For 400kWh per year, e be 40 to 60kWh.
p-040.actionItem: Today, move di back and side of your fridge 5 to 10cm from di wall and wipe di dust.

p-041.title: Reduce washing machine spin vibration
p-041.summary: If clothes move to one side, washing machine go shake well well during spin.
p-041.principle: If unbalanced mass $m$ dey spin for radius $r$, centrifugal force $F = m\omega^2 r$ go form, and e dey proportional to square of angular velocity.
p-041.example: For 1000 rpm ($\omega\approx105\ \mathrm{rad/s}$), unbalance of 1kg, if $r=0.2\ \mathrm{m}$, e be $F\approx2200\ \mathrm{N}$. If you balance am, dis force almost disappear.
p-041.actionItem: Today, when you put big laundry like duvet, add small clothes together and spread dem evenly.

p-042.title: Restore vacuum suction power
p-042.summary: If you empty vacuum cleaner filter and dust bin, di suction power go almost return to how e be at first.
p-042.principle: Suction pressure difference $\Delta P$ multiplied by air flow rate $Q$ na suction power $P = \Delta P\cdot Q$. When e block, flow go reduce well well.
p-042.example: If filter half block, flow fit reduce by about 30 to 50%. Even with di same motor, di dust suction power go reduce by di same amount, so cleaning time go increase.
p-042.actionItem: Today, empty your vacuum dust bin and shake di filter or wash am with water and dry am.

p-043.title: Latent heat of ice pack
p-043.summary: To keep thing cold, na to use di latent heat wey ice dey absorb when e melt dey most efficient.
p-043.principle: When ice melt, e dey absorb heat of $Q = mL$ through $L=334\ \mathrm{J/g}$ while temperature stay for 0°C.
p-043.example: 500g ice pack go absorb $500\times334\approx167\ \mathrm{kJ}$ to melt. Dis one na 16 times di heat (10kJ) wey di same amount of 0°C water need to rise 5°C.
p-043.actionItem: Today, when you go market, put ice pack and put frozen food last for di bag.

p-044.title: Snow load for roof
p-044.summary: Wet snow heavy many times pass dry snow, so e fit make roof and plastic greenhouse collapse.
p-044.principle: Load na $P = \rho g h$. Dry snow $\rho\approx100\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, wet snow $\rho\approx400\text{-}500$.
p-044.example: Wet snow wey 30cm deep ($\rho=400$) na $400\times9.8\times0.3\approx1180\ \mathrm{Pa}$, wey be 4 times of dry snow (about 300Pa).
p-044.actionItem: Today, if plenty snow fall, sweep di snow comot for plastic greenhouse and awning from safe place.

p-045.title: Heat pump air conditioner heating efficiency
p-045.summary: Air conditioner heating dey produce more heat with di same electricity pass electric heater.
p-045.principle: Heat pump dey move heat, so $\mathrm{COP} = Q_h/W$ dey bigger than 1. Electric heater na $\mathrm{COP}=1$.
p-045.example: If COP na 3, 1kWh go produce 3kWh heat. For 3kW heating for 5 hours, electric heater na 15kWh, heat pump na 5kWh, so you save 10kWh.
p-045.actionItem: Today, instead of electric heater, try use air conditioner heating mode for 20°C.

p-046.title: Why wet gloves dey cold pass
p-046.summary: Wet gloves dey take heat comot far faster pass dry gloves.
p-046.principle: Thermal conductivity of water na about $0.6\ \mathrm{W/m\cdot K}$, wey be about 23 times of air ($0.026$), and evaporation heat dey add, so $Q = kA\Delta T/d$ dey bigger.
p-046.example: Even with di same thickness, heat loss for water-soaked gloves dey many times more, so hands dey cold quickly. For every 1g of evaporation, extra 2.26kJ dey escape.
p-046.actionItem: Today, dry di gloves wey you use touch snow immediately and carry one extra pair.

p-047.title: Icicles for eaves na sign say heat dey leak go roof
p-047.summary: If snow for roof melt from di bottom and freeze again for di eaves, e fit be evidence say indoor heat dey leak go di roof.
p-047.principle: Heat loss rate na $\dot Q=UA\,\Delta T$. If insulation bad, $U$ go big, roof surface temperature go rise above 0°C and di snow go melt.
p-047.example: For roof wey get 100m² area, if $U$ reduce from 0.5 go 0.25 $\mathrm{W/(m^2\,K)}$, when $\Delta T=20$ K, di loss go reduce from $0.5\times100\times20=1{,}000$ W go 500W, half.
p-047.actionItem: Today, check if icicles dey for eaves or balcony ceiling (no stand under dem), and if dem plenty, check ceiling and attic insulation.

p-048.title: One layer of soap film to stop glasses from fogging
p-048.summary: Even if you wear mask, glasses dey blur because lens surface cold pass di dew point of your exhaled breath. If you put thin soap film for di lens, e go form transparent water film instead of droplets and your vision go clear.
p-048.principle: If surface temperature $T_s$ low pass dew point $T_d$, water vapour go condense. Surfactant dey reduce contact angle so small droplets go spread and form transparent film.
p-048.example: Di dew point of 34℃ and 100% humidity exhaled breath na about 34℃, but di lens surface na about 20℃, so e condense immediately. If you spread one drop of neutral detergent thin for lens and let am dry, di droplets go spread over di whole lens and fogging go reduce well.
p-048.actionItem: Today, spread just one drop of neutral detergent for both sides of di lens, no wipe am, let am dry naturally, and press di nose wire of your mask so exhaled breath no go leak up.

p-049.title: How to identify real polarised sunglasses
p-049.summary: Reflected light from water surface and wet road dey mostly horizontally polarised, so polarised lenses dey filter am and reduce glare and eye strain. Fake one fit be just lens wey dark for colour, so check am yourself.
p-049.principle: Light intensity wey pass polariser dey follow Malus law $I=I_0\cos^2\theta$, and reflection from water surface dey almost completely polarised near Brewster angle $\theta_B=\arctan(n)\approx 53^\circ$.
p-049.example: If polarisation direction and lens axis na $90^\circ$, e be $\cos^2 90^\circ=0$, so reflected light almost dey blocked. But if you overlap two lenses with $90^\circ$, e go dark, and na dis way you fit check whether e real. Even if e polarised, UV protection (UV400) different thing, so check di label.
p-049.actionItem: Look smartphone screen through di lens, rotate di lens $90^\circ$ and check if di screen go dark, and also look for UV400 mark.

p-050.title: Why road for bridge dey freeze first
p-050.summary: Bridge dey touch cold air from up and down, so e dey freeze before ordinary road, and black ice wey hard to see dey form easily.
p-050.principle: Road for ground get heat from di earth wey dey rise, so e dey cool less, but for bridge, air dey under too, so no heat supply. Braking distance na $d=\dfrac{v^2}{2\mu g}$.
p-050.example: For 50km/h ($v\approx13.9$ m/s), if dry road $\mu\approx0.7$ be about 14m, ice $\mu\approx0.1$ be about 99m, e go increase nearly 7 times.
p-050.actionItem: For early morning and night wey temperature dey 3°C or below, reduce speed early before bridges, tunnel entrances and shaded areas.

p-051.title: Why 2 to 3 times magnification enough for makeup mirror
p-051.summary: For magnifying mirror, higher magnification no mean better. If focal length short, you go need put your face very close, and di range wey you fit see go narrow.
p-051.principle: Concave mirror $\dfrac1f=\dfrac1{d_o}+\dfrac1{d_i}$, magnification $m=-\dfrac{d_i}{d_o}$. If object dey inside di focal point, upright magnified virtual image go form.
p-051.example: For mirror wey get focal length $f=20$ cm, if you put your face for $d_o=10$ cm, e go appear for $d_i=-20$ cm, $m=2$ times. 10x mirror wey get 5cm focal length need you put your face inside 5cm, so you go see only one eye at a time. If you go farther pass di focal point, di image go turn upside down.
p-051.actionItem: When you wan buy mirror, measure di distance wey you dey usually stay from your face, and choose one wey get focal length of about 2 times of dat distance (2 to 3x magnification).

p-052.title: Use pressure cooker reduce cooking time and gas bill
p-052.summary: Pressure cooker dey raise internal pressure and boiling point of water to about 120℃, so e dey reduce cooking time to 1/3 or less.
p-052.principle: Boiling point dey rise with pressure (Clausius-Clapeyron). Reaction rate na roughly 2 times for every $10^\circ$C, so e go be $2^{(120-100)/10}=4$ times faster.
p-052.example: For gauge pressure of 1atm (about 2atm absolute), boiling point na about 120℃. Braised ribs wey need 60 minutes for ordinary pot go finish for about 20 minutes, and you fit save about 1kWh on 1.5kW induction. Never open di lid before pressure fully release.
p-052.actionItem: Tonight, cook something wey need long boiling (boiled pork, beans, steamed dish) with pressure cooker, and instead of extra heating, off di fire and let di remaining pressure finish am.

p-053.title: 1% door gap reduce soundproofing from 30dB to 20dB
p-053.summary: Even thick door, if gap dey under am, soundproofing performance go drop well well. Door draft tape wey cost few thousand won dey reduce noise and draft together.
p-053.principle: Combined transmittance $\tau=\dfrac{\sum S_i\tau_i}{\sum S_i}$, transmission loss $TL=-10\log_{10}\tau$.
p-053.example: If door get 30dB sound insulation (τ=0.001) and 1% area gap (τ≈1), with $\tau=0.99\times0.001+0.01=0.011$, TL na about 19.6dB, so e drop sharply from 30 to 20dB. If you block di gap with draft tape (about 3,000 won), winter draft go reduce too and e go help your heating bill.
p-053.actionItem: Close di door and check if light dey leak from di gap under and beside di door, den stick silicone weatherstrip or door sweep.

p-054.title: Just changing Wi-Fi router position fit change speed
p-054.summary: Every time distance double, signal go weaken by 4 times (6dB), and every wall dey remove extra 3 to 10dB. If you put router for open space for di centre of di house, speed go improve.
p-054.example: For 2.4GHz, 10m na about 60.0dB, 20m na about 66.0dB, so double distance na +6dB. If concrete wall dey between, 5 to 10dB more go lose, so speed for di end room go drop a lot.
p-054.actionItem: Take di router comot from behind TV or inside drawer or floor, move am to open shelf for 1 to 1.5m height for di centre of di house, and compare speed for di end room before and after.

p-055.title: Every 3dB for earphone volume, safe time dey half
p-055.summary: Every time sound intensity rise by 3dB, energy go double and di time wey you fit safely listen go be half. Even if you lower volume small, di time wey you dey protect your ear go increase well.
p-055.principle: Sound pressure level $L=10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_0}$ ($I_0=10^{-12}$ W/m²). Exposure recommendation: 8 hours at 85dB, and every 3dB rise, time go half.
p-055.example: 85dB for 8 hours, 88dB for 4 hours, 91dB for 2 hours, 94dB for 1 hour, 100dB for 15 minutes. If you raise volume because of subway noise and e reach 95dB or more, even 30 minutes too much.
p-055.actionItem: Today, turn on di headphone safety and volume limit setting for your smartphone and limit di maximum volume to about 60%.

p-056.title: Hydroplaning for spring rain, reduce speed by only 20%
p-056.summary: For wet road, if speed high, di water wey dey front of di tyre no fit comot, e go form wedge and lift di tyre. When hydroplaning happen, steering and braking almost impossible.
p-056.principle: When di dynamic pressure of water $q=\tfrac12\rho v^2$ near di contact pressure $p$, water film go lift di tyre. Critical speed $v\approx\sqrt{2p/\rho}$ (simple estimate).
p-056.example: If contact pressure na about 220kPa, $v\approx\sqrt{2\times220000/1000}\approx21$ m/s, wey be about 76km/h. If di grooves wear out, drainage no go work and e fit happen even for lower speed, so for 100km/h zone, e safer to reduce am to 80km/h.
p-056.actionItem: Check whether di tread wear indicator (TWI) between di tyre grooves don reach di same height as di groove depth, and for rainy day drive at 80% of your normal speed.

p-057.title: No trust earplug NRR number just like dat
p-057.summary: Di NRR wey dem write for di packaging na laboratory maximum, so di actual reduction go small well. For concert and construction earplugs, you must compare with adjusted value.
p-057.principle: Actual attenuation estimate $\mathrm{NRR}_{\text{actual}}\approx\dfrac{\mathrm{NRR}-7}{2}$ dB (apply 50% after A-weighting correction).
p-057.example: Di actual reduction of foam earplug wey get NRR 33 na $(33-7)/2=13$ dB. For 100dB concert, e reduce to 87dB, wey still small high for di 85dB standard. To wear am correctly dey more important than di number.
p-057.actionItem: Roll di foam earplug thin, pull your ear up and back, put am inside, and press am with your finger for 30 seconds make e expand.

p-058.title: Wireless charging, coil position dey decide efficiency
p-058.summary: Wireless charging get more loss than wired charging, so if position no align, e go heat up and use more power. Even if you just align am well, you fit reduce loss and battery degradation.
p-058.principle: Inductive coupling efficiency dey depend on coupling coefficient $k$ and $\eta=\dfrac{k^2Q_1Q_2}{\left(1+\sqrt{1+k^2Q_1Q_2}\right)^2}$. If e misalign, $k$ go drop sharply.
p-058.example: When you charge 5000 mAh, 3.85V (about 19.3Wh) phone, wired 90% na 21.4Wh, wireless 70% na 27.5Wh, and misaligned 50% na 38.5Wh. If you charge once every day, aligned na about 2kWh extra per year, misaligned na about 6kWh extra per year.
p-058.actionItem: Put your phone exactly for di centre of di coil mark for di charging pad, and remove thick case, cards or metal plate before you charge.

p-059.title: Take your foot off accelerator early before signal
p-059.summary: If you press brake when you see stop signal, di car kinetic energy go waste as heat. If you take your foot off di pedal early, di car go roll with fuel cut and save fuel.
p-059.principle: Kinetic energy $E_k=\tfrac12mv^2$. Di energy wey brake dey waste dey proportional to square of speed.
p-059.example: If 1,500kg car dey run 60km/h (16.7m/s), e be $E_k\approx208$ kJ. If you take effective energy of 1L petrol as about 8.5MJ, each stop na about 25mL worth. If you respond early to 10 signals, you go save tens to hundreds of mL per day.
p-059.actionItem: Today, when you dey drive and di signal ahead red, take your foot off di pedal about 150m before, let di car roll by itself, and use di brake lightly only when you need am.

p-060.title: Move water with siphon without pump
p-060.summary: To change aquarium water or empty rain barrel, you only need hose and height difference. Once you fill di hose with water, water go keep flowing to di lower side.
p-060.principle: If di outlet low pass di water surface by $\Delta h$, water go flow because of pressure difference $\Delta P=\rho g\Delta h$, and ideal flow speed na $v=\sqrt{2g\Delta h}$.
p-060.example: If height difference na 0.5m, ideal speed na 3.1m/s, but because of hose friction, di real one na about 1m/s. For 10mm diameter hose, $Q\approx0.08$ L/s, so 20L go move in about 4 minutes.
p-060.actionItem: Submerge di hose in water to fill am full, block one end, and move am go bucket for lower position. Never suck chemical liquid with your mouth.

p-061.title: For snowy day, UV dey come from top and bottom
p-061.summary: Fresh snow dey reflect plenty UV, so for snowfield for winter, your eyes and face dey burn from sun more easily than you think.
p-061.principle: Reflectance (albedo) na $\alpha=I_r/I_0$, and total UV exposure na roughly $I_0(1+\alpha)$. UV albedo of fresh snow na about 0.8 to 0.9, grass na about 0.03.
p-061.example: If direct UV na 1, for grass e be about 1.03, and for fresh snow e be about 1.8 to 1.9, almost double.
p-061.actionItem: When you dey go for snowy day or snowfield, carry UV-blocking sunglasses (goggles) and sunscreen.

p-062.title: Why your ear dey block when plane dey land
p-062.summary: Di air pressure inside plane dey like about 2,400m above sea level, so di air inside your ear go expand afta take-off and e go press back when plane dey go down. If you open your ears from di time wey landing start, e no go pain you.
p-062.example: If ground pressure na 101kPa and cabin pressure for cruise na about 75kPa, di air inside your ear go grow $101/75\approx1.35$ times, wey be 35% bigger. For landing e go shrink back, so eardrum go pull inside. If your nose block for cold, di tube for ear no go easily open.
p-062.actionItem: When dem announce say plane wan land, chew gum or yawn and swallow spit again and again, and no sleep, stay wake.

p-063.title: Binoculars number 8x42, how to read even di brightness
p-063.summary: Di numbers for binoculars na magnification × lens diameter. If you wan use am for early morning or evening, di exit pupil must big so e go bright, but if na only daytime you dey use am, small light one better.
p-063.example: 8x42 na $42/8=5.25$ mm, so relative brightness na about 27.6, while 10x25 na 2.5mm and e be about 6.3, so for dark place di first one bright pass by more than 4 times. Person pupil for dark na 5 to 7mm, so for early morning bird watching exit pupil of 4mm or more better.
p-063.actionItem: If you dey use am for early morning or evening bird watching, pick one wey get $D/M\ge4$ mm; if na only daytime walk, pick light small one and go try am for hand yourself.

p-064.title: If you wrap hot water pipe, heat go leak small
p-064.summary: Bare hot water pipe wey dey go from boiler to tap dey lose heat without rest. If you put insulation on top, di loss go reduce well well.
p-064.principle: Heat loss for pipe na $\dot Q\propto \Delta T/R$, and insulation dey increase thermal resistance $R$. If $R$ double, di loss for di same $\Delta T$ go half.
p-064.example: If we assume say 10m of bare hot water pipe get 25K difference from room and e dey lose about 25W per metre, e be 250W. If insulation bring am down to about 60W, you go save about 1.9kWh if e run 10 hours every day.
p-064.actionItem: Measure how long di bare hot water pipe be for boiler room or under sink, then plan to buy foam insulation and wrap am.

p-065.title: Roof box, comot am for spring
p-065.summary: If you leave di roof box wey you use carry ski things for winter, di air resistance for high speed go increase and fuel go waste.
p-065.principle: Air resistance power $P=\tfrac12\rho C_dAv^3$ (e dey follow cube of speed).
p-065.example: If car with $C_dA=0.69\,\mathrm{m^2}$ dey run 100km per hour (27.8m/s), e be about 8.9kW, but if roof box increase $C_dA$ by 20%, e go be about 10.7kW, wey be 1.8kW more. For 100km drive, e mean say you dey use about 0.8L extra.
p-065.actionItem: Check di roof box and di crossbars on di roof rack, and if e empty, remove am today and keep am for garage.

p-066.title: Adhesive hook, no pull am up, stretch am long to comot am
p-066.summary: Adhesive hook strong against pull wey dey go down (shear), but e weak against force wey dey pull am straight comot from wall (peel).
p-066.principle: For shear, di whole sticky surface share di force, but for peel di force gather for one line for di edge, so $F_{	ext{peel}}\ll F_{	ext{shear}}$.
p-066.example: For example, hook wey fit carry 2 kgf for shear fit drop at 0.2 to 0.5 kgf for peel. So weight wey dey hang down fine, but if you lift am up, e go easily drop.
p-066.actionItem: When you wan stick hook, clean dust and water from di surface and press am hard for more than 1 minute. When you wan remove am, pull am slowly and long, parallel to di wall.

p-067.title: Use noise cancelling cut volume by 6dB
p-067.summary: Noise cancelling dey make sound wey get opposite phase to di noise to cancel am. For train, you no need to turn volume up well well, so e dey protect your ears.
p-067.principle: Destructive interference: $A\sin\omega t+A\sin(\omega t+\pi)=0$. E dey work well for low-frequency steady sound (about 1kHz or below).
p-067.example: If subway noise na 80dB and noise cancelling reduce di low noise by about 20dB, you fit hear di same music for 6dB lower volume (for example 91dB to 85dB), and safe listening time go increase by 4 times, from 2 hours to 8 hours.
p-067.actionItem: For train or bus, turn on noise cancelling and reduce di volume by 2 or 3 steps, then try am.

p-068.title: Curve for spring rain, na dis be di speed limit
p-068.summary: Di highest speed wey you fit safely turn for curve depend on road friction coefficient and radius. When e wet, di limit go drop well well.
p-068.principle: Limit speed $v=\sqrt{\mu g r}$ (centripetal force = friction force).
p-068.example: For curve wey get 50m radius, dry road ($\mu=0.7$) na about 67km/h, wet road (0.4) na about 50km/h, and snow road (0.2) na about 36km/h. Di speed for sign board na for dry road, so if rain dey fall, reduce more.
p-068.actionItem: Slow down for straight road before you enter di curve, and for inside di curve no do sudden brake or sharp steering.

p-069.title: TV size, distance matter pass resolution
p-069.summary: Human eye resolution na about 1 arcminute. If you sit far, your eye no fit tell di difference between 4K and full HD, so e better to spend money on screen size instead of resolution.
p-069.principle: Eye resolution $\theta\approx1'\approx2.9\times10^{-4}$ rad, and if pixel spacing be $p$, di farthest distance wey you fit still see di difference na $d=\dfrac{p}{\theta}$.
p-069.example: 55-inch 4K pixel spacing na about 0.32mm, so you fit see pixel difference only if you dey inside $d\approx1.1$ m. If your sofa dey 3m away, even full HD no go show pixels reach 75 inches, so look size and picture quality (contrast, HDR) instead of 4K premium.
p-069.actionItem: Use tape measure measure di distance from where you wan put TV go your sofa, then decide di screen size based on dat distance.

p-070.title: Di thicker di frost for freezer, di more light e dey chop
p-070.summary: Frost get plenty air between ice crystals, so e dey act like insulation and e dey block cold from passing, so di compressor go run longer.
p-070.principle: Thermal resistance na $R=d/k$ and e dey follow thickness $d$. Frost $k$ na about 0.2 to 0.5 $\mathrm{W/(m\,K)}$, wey small pass pure ice (about 2.2).
p-070.example: If $k=0.3$, 5mm frost get $R=0.005/0.3\approx0.017\ \mathrm{m^2K/W}$, wey be 5 times of when e be 1mm. Cooling efficiency go drop by dat much.
p-070.actionItem: If frost pass 3 to 5mm, switch off di power and let am thaw by itself. No scrape am with knife or sharp tool.

p-071.title: 200L rainwater, free water for spring garden
p-071.summary: If you gather spring rain wey fall for roof, you fit water your garden without tap water. If you put di barrel high, water pressure go let you connect hose.
p-071.principle: Water pressure $P=\rho g h$, amount collected $V=A\times R$ (area × rainfall).
p-071.example: If 20mm rain fall for 10m² roof, $10\times20=200$ L go gather. If you raise di barrel by 1m, e go get 9.8kPa (about 0.1bar) pressure, so water go flow by gravity with hose go lower flower beds.
p-071.actionItem: Put di rain barrel on stand wey pass 50cm high, and cover am with lid and net so mosquito no go breed.

p-072.title: Microphone feedback howl, reduce 3dB and e go stop
p-072.summary: If microphone dey pick speaker sound again and amplify am, you go hear "eeee" howl. You fit stop am easily by only adjusting distance and volume.
p-072.principle: Loop gain $G=g_{amp}\cdot g_{path}\ge1$, and if di phase match, e go start to oscillate.
p-072.example: If you double di distance between microphone and speaker, path loss go increase by 6dB, so you fit raise volume by dat much. But if you reduce volume by only 3dB, loop gain go half and di howl go disappear.
p-072.actionItem: No put speaker for di direction wey di microphone dey face, point am towards di audience, and reduce di microphone input volume by 3dB (one or two steps).

p-073.title: Use shadow to know how strong UV be
p-073.summary: If your shadow short pass your height, e mean say sun dey higher than 45 degrees and UV strong. By end of March, afternoon shadow don already short pass your height.
p-073.principle: UV amount dey follow $\sin\alpha$ of sun elevation $\alpha$, and shadow length na $L=\dfrac{h}{\tan\alpha}$.
p-073.example: For latitude 37 degrees, noon sun elevation for spring equinox (around 20 March) na $90^\circ-37^\circ=53^\circ$, and shadow na $1/\tan53^\circ=0.75$ times your height. For early February (elevation about 38 degrees), e be 1.28 times.
p-073.actionItem: Check your shadow around noon today, and if e short pass your height, wear sunscreen of SPF30 or more and put on hat.

p-074.title: Section speed enforcement, even if you drive fast, you only gain 2 minutes
p-074.summary: Section speed enforcement dey check average speed. Di time wey you gain from sudden speeding small well, but energy and danger go increase plenty.
p-074.principle: Average speed $\bar v=\dfrac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$, air resistance power $\propto v^3$.
p-074.example: If you drive 20km section for 100km/h e take 12 minutes, and for 120km/h e take 10 minutes, so na 2 minutes difference, but air resistance power na $1.2^3=1.73$ times (+73%) and kinetic energy go increase by 44%. Di speeding for di front section you go need to recover for di back, so no profit dey.
p-074.actionItem: For section enforcement area, set cruise control to speed limit and drive steady.

p-075.title: For speaker, look sensitivity (dB) pass watt
p-075.summary: 3dB difference for sensitivity to produce di same loudness na double amplifier output. Big watt number no mean say sound go loud.
p-075.example: To get 85dB at 3m, you need about 94.5dB converted to 1m. Speaker wey get 90dB sensitivity need about 2.8W, while 84dB speaker need about 11.2W, wey be 4 times difference.
p-075.actionItem: For di speaker wey you wan buy, check di sensitivity (dB/1W/1m) for specification sheet and pick di one wey get higher sensitivity.

p-076.title: Reduce fan speed by just 20% and power go half
p-076.summary: Fan power consumption dey follow cube of rotation speed. If e no matter say wind small weak, you fit save plenty electricity.
p-076.principle: Fan affinity law: airflow $Q\propto N$, power consumption $P\propto N^3$.
p-076.example: If you reduce speed to 80%, airflow go be 80%, and power go be $0.8^3=0.51$, wey be half. If na 40W fan, e go reduce to about 20W, and if you use am 8 hours a day, you go save about 4.7kWh every month.
p-076.actionItem: Today, set your fan or ventilation fan to 'medium' instead of 'high' and check if di breeze still enough for you.

p-077.title: Garden hose with one nozzle fit save 40% water
p-077.summary: If you squeeze di end of hose, water jet go quick pass for di same flow and e go reach far, and shut-off nozzle dey stop wastage when you dey move.
p-077.example: If 10L/min (0.167L/s) dey flow inside 15mm diameter hose, di speed na about 0.94m/s, and if you put 5mm nozzle, e go be about 8.5m/s, 9 times faster, and e need about 36kPa pressure. If you use shut-off nozzle to stop di water when you dey move, 50L wey you for use for 5 minutes fit reduce to about 30L.
p-077.actionItem: Put hand-grip shut-off nozzle for di end of hose and water only di root side of di plants.

p-078.title: Di 'bang' sound when you close tap, na water hammer
p-078.summary: If you close am quick, water wey dey flow go stop suddenly and shock wave go form inside di pipe, so you go hear 'bang' and di pipe fit spoil.
p-078.principle: Joukowsky equation $\Delta p=\rho c\,\Delta v$ (c: speed of sound inside pipe).
p-078.example: For copper pipe wey get flow speed 2m/s and $c\approx1200$ m/s, if you shut am suddenly, $\Delta p\approx2.4$ MPa (24bar), wey be 6 times di normal water pressure of 3 to 4bar. If closing time pass $2L/c$ (about 17 ms for 10m pipe), di shock go reduce well well.
p-078.actionItem: Close lever taps and washing machine valve slowly, and if e dey repeat, ask about installing water hammer arrestor.

p-079.title: When to change running shoes, look impact force
p-079.summary: When cushion don wear, di time wey your foot take stop go short and di force wey dey enter your knee and ankle go increase. Check dem every 500 to 800km.
p-079.principle: Impulse $F\,\Delta t=\Delta p$, so average impact force $F=\dfrac{m\Delta v}{\Delta t}$.
p-079.example: If we simplify say person wey weigh 70kg dey reduce 70N·s momentum when e land, if e stop for 0.035 second e be 2,000N, but if cushion wear and e stop for 0.02 second, e be 3,500N (about 5 times body weight), wey be 75% increase.
p-079.actionItem: Check today whether di sole of your running shoe don press and wrinkle, and write down di distance wey you don run since di last time you change am.

p-080.title: Night driving, if you fast pass low-beam range, e dey dangerous
p-080.summary: Di distance wey low beam dey light na about 40m, but stopping distance at 80km/h pass dat. E be like say you dey rush enter where you no fit see.
p-080.example: For 80km/h (22.2m/s), 1 second reaction and $\mu=0.7$, $22.2+36=58$ m, wey pass 40m. 60km/h na $16.7+20=37$ m, wey safe. Fog or oil film for inside di windscreen dey scatter light and e dey reduce your sight more.
p-080.actionItem: Before you start, clean di inside of windscreen and headlights, and for dark small roads drive 60km/h or below.

p-081.title: Bicycle helmet, di thickness wey dey absorb shock na di main thing
p-081.summary: Helmet dey increase di distance wey your head take stop, so e dey reduce impact force. Certification and good fit pass price or design.
p-081.example: If 5kg head hit at 6m/s, $E_k=90$ J. Without helmet, stopping distance of 2mm go give about 45kN, but with 20mm EPS foam e be about 4.5kN, wey be one-tenth. Once EPS don press from one impact, e no work again.
p-081.actionItem: Check for KC, CPSC or EN1078 certification mark, and adjust am so e fit two fingers height above your eyebrow and di chin strap form Y under di ear.

p-082.title: Solar garden light, if you tilt am 35 degrees facing south, e go get 25% more
p-082.summary: Solar panel dey receive di most when e face di sun straight. If you tilt di garden light to match your latitude, e go charge more.
p-082.principle: Light received $\propto\cos\theta$ ($\theta$: angle of incidence). Best tilt $\approx$ latitude.
p-082.example: For latitude 37 degrees, with noon sun elevation 53 degrees for spring equinox, horizontal panel na $\sin53^\circ=0.80$, panel wey dey vertical for wall na $\cos53^\circ=0.60$, and panel wey tilt 37 degrees na 1.0. E dey get about 25% more than horizontal and about 67% more than vertical.
p-082.actionItem: Make di garden light panel face south and tilt am 35 to 40 degrees, and remove shadow and dust.

p-083.title: Desk lamp, if you pull am 30cm closer, power go reduce to one quarter
p-083.summary: Light brightness dey reduce with square of distance. If you put lamp close, even weaker bulb fit give you di same brightness.
p-083.example: If you move di lamp from 60cm to 30cm, illuminance go be 4 times. To get 500 lux at 60cm, you need 12W LED, but at 30cm 3W go do, so if you use am 4 hours daily, you go save about 13kWh every year.
p-083.actionItem: Put di lamp about 30cm from your book, for di opposite side of di hand wey you dey write with, and change am to lower-watt bulb.

p-084.title: Why phone call dey cut for elevator
p-084.summary: Metal box na Faraday cage wey dey block electromagnetic waves, so signal no fit enter. If you prepare before signal cut, you fit protect important call.
p-084.principle: Skin depth $\delta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\pi f\mu\sigma}}$ (di depth wey radio wave dey reduce inside conductor).
p-084.example: For aluminium ($\sigma=3.8\times10^7$ S/m), di skin depth of 1.8GHz wave na only about 1.9µm, so even thin metal plate fit block signal. E mean say you dey depend on small signal wey dey leak enter through door gap and vent.
p-084.actionItem: Finish important calls before you enter elevator or turn on Wi-Fi calling, and download di files wey you need before you enter underground parking.

p-085.title: Spring big cleaning, no sweep dust, wipe am
p-085.summary: Fine dust dey stay inside air for different times depending on size. If you sweep, di dust wey don settle go fly up again and enter your breathing system.
p-085.example: 10µm diameter dust go settle 1m for about 3 minutes at about 6mm/s, but 2.5µm get speed $1/16$ times, 0.38mm/s, so e go take about 44 minutes. Small particles dey stay for air for long even after cleaning.
p-085.actionItem: Today, instead of sweeping, use wet mop or wet cloth clean am, and afta you finish, open window and ventilate for 1 hour.

p-086.title: 2-second rule for safe distance for highway
p-086.summary: If you brake from di same distance as di car for front, di gap wey you need na driver reaction distance. If you keep 2 seconds, you go get about 56m at 100km/h.
p-086.example: At 100km/h (27.8m/s) with 1.5 seconds reaction, you need $41.7$ m, and 2-second rule give 55.6m, so you get extra space. For rainy day, increase am to 3 to 4 seconds.
p-086.actionItem: When di car for front pass road sign or street light, count 'one, two' and check whether you finish counting before you reach dat point.

p-087.title: Di bigger di wheel for suitcase and stroller, di better e dey pass over kerb
p-087.summary: Big diameter wheel dey climb di same kerb with gentler angle, so e need less force.
p-087.principle: When wheel wey get radius $R$ dey climb kerb wey get height $h$, di horizontal force wey dey push di axle na $F=mg\,\dfrac{\sqrt{2Rh-h^2}}{R-h}$.
p-087.example: If weight on wheel $mg=100$ N and kerb height $h=1$ cm, 6cm diameter need about 112N, 10cm need about 75N, and 16cm need about 55N.
p-087.actionItem: When you dey choose suitcase or stroller, check di wheel diameter and material (rubber or urethane), and for kerb lift di front wheel small.

p-088.title: Why fast charging dey lose less when voltage high
p-088.summary: Heat wey dey disappear inside cable resistance dey follow square of current. Even for di same power, if you charge with higher voltage and lower current, di loss go reduce.
p-088.example: If you send 18W at 5V, e be 3.6A, so 2.6W (14%) go disappear inside 0.2Ω cable, but if you send am at 9V, e be 2A and only 0.8W (4.4%) go disappear. Thin and long cable dey lose more.
p-088.actionItem: Use thick and short cable wey support di same standard as di charger (like PD), and change old cables.

p-089.title: Dry cloth with spring sun and wind
p-089.summary: E need plenty energy to evaporate water from wet cloth. Sun and wind dey give dis energy free.
p-089.principle: Latent heat of evaporation $Q=mL$ ($L=2.26\times10^6$ J/kg), evaporation rate $E\propto(a+bu)(e_s-e_a)$ (e dey increase as wind $u$ big).
p-089.example: To evaporate 1kg water from cloth, e need $2.26$ MJ $\approx0.63$ kWh. If you spin am for 1,000 rpm or more and hang am for 2m/s wind, e go dry far faster than inside house, and you go save about 2 to 3kWh wey one dryer cycle dey use. For day wey get heavy pollen, use inside house.
p-089.actionItem: After spinning, shake di cloth and spread am, space dem so wind fit pass, and hang dem for where sun dey reach.

p-090.title: Spring tyre change, wheel nut wey no dey loosen
p-090.summary: Di reason why nut no dey move when you dey change from winter tyre to normal tyre na say di torque wey need dey big. Long wrench dey reduce di force.
p-090.example: If you use 0.3m wrench to loosen wheel nut wey get 110N·m specified torque, you need about 370N force, and with 0.6m wrench e be about 183N, wey be half. But when you dey tighten am, no add pipe to over-tighten, use torque wrench and follow di specified value.
p-090.actionItem: Before you lift di car with jack, first loosen di nuts half turn while di tyre still touch di ground, and always work for flat place.

p-091.title: Hiking backpack, put heavy load close to your back
p-091.summary: Di farther di backpack from your body, di bigger di turning force wey dey press your waist and shoulder. If you put heavy things close to your back and transfer di load to di waist belt, tiredness go reduce.
p-091.principle: Torque $\tau=mgd$ ($d$: distance from body axis to centre of gravity of load).
p-091.example: If you put 6kg load 25cm from your body, $\tau=6\times9.8\times0.25=14.7$ N·m, and if you bring am close to 10cm e be 5.9N·m, about 60% reduction. Make di waist belt carry 70% of di load go your hips.
p-091.actionItem: Put heavy things like water bottle or lunch box inside di backpack for di middle height for your back side, tighten di waist belt well and then start.

p-092.title: Cross ventilation for 10 minutes
p-092.summary: If you open two windows wey face each other instead of one window, di air inside di room go change far faster.
p-092.principle: Air flow dey follow Bernoulli equation $p+\tfrac{1}{2}\rho v^2=\mathrm{const}$ and flow rate $Q=Av$. If entrance and exit dey, wind go pass and ventilation amount go big.
p-092.example: For 75m³ room, if 1m/s wind enter through 0.5m² opening, $Q=0.5\times1=0.5\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$ (1,800m³/h). For real life e dey change 5 to 10 times per hour, so 10 minutes enough, but if you open only one window e be 1 to 2 times.
p-092.actionItem: Today, open windows wey face each other (or front door and window) at di same time and ventilate for 10 minutes.

p-093.title: Bicycle tyre pressure and rolling resistance
p-093.summary: If tyre pressure low, even for di same speed e go be more difficult.
p-093.principle: Rolling resistance na $F_\mathrm{rr}=C_\mathrm{rr}\,mg$, and when air comot, di contact surface go wide, deformation loss go increase and $C_\mathrm{rr}$ go increase.
p-093.example: If total weight na 80kg and $C_\mathrm{rr}$ rise from 0.005 to 0.010, $F_\mathrm{rr}$ go double from about 3.9N to 7.8N, and at 20km/h (5.6m/s) e go increase from about 22W to 44W.
p-093.actionItem: Before you start, pump air to di recommended pressure (psi/bar) wey dem write for di tyre side.

p-094.title: Dust mask dey filter with static electricity
p-094.summary: KF mask no dey catch fine dust with tiny holes, e dey use static electricity, so if e touch water or alcohol, e no go work well again.
p-094.principle: Di filter fibre carry permanent charge and e dey pull particles with Coulomb force $F=k\dfrac{q_1q_2}{r^2}$. If water, alcohol or sweat touch am, di charge go disappear.
p-094.example: KF94 dey filter more than 94% of 0.4μm particles, but after alcohol spray e fit drop below 80%. Normally, one day (about 8 hours at most) use for one mask dey okay.
p-094.actionItem: No wash di mask or spray disinfectant on am, and if e wet or lose shape, change am to new one today.

p-095.title: Drip coffee and how water dey flow
p-095.summary: If you pour water thin and slow, extraction go even and you go get stronger taste from di same coffee beans.
p-095.principle: Narrow spout dey increase flow speed $v=Q/A$ and e dey cause turbulence wey dey mix di grounds evenly. Extraction depend on contact time and temperature.
p-095.example: Di standard na to pour 250mL water for 92 to 96°C for 15g coffee in parts within 2 minutes 30 seconds to 3 minutes. If you pour all di water at once within 30 seconds, di contact time go reduce to 1/5 and di coffee go weak and sour.
p-095.actionItem: This morning, pour your coffee water in 3 parts, slowly with thin stream, and try am.

p-096.title: If you reduce screen brightness, power go reduce too
p-096.summary: Di backlight power of LCD monitor dey almost follow brightness, so if you reduce brightness, electricity and eye strain go reduce together.
p-096.principle: Backlight power go be like $P\approx kB$, e dey follow brightness $B$, and di total na $P=P_0+kB$.
p-096.example: If backlight na 25W out of 40W total at 100% brightness, at 50% e go reduce 12.5W and you go save about 31%. If 8 hours a day, $0.0125\times8\times30\approx3$ kWh every month.
p-096.actionItem: Today, reduce your monitor or TV brightness to around 50% to match di brightness around you.

p-097.title: Induction pot must get flat bottom
p-097.summary: Induction dey make current for di bottom of pot to heat am, so if di bottom bend, heating efficiency go drop.
p-097.principle: Changing magnetic field dey cause eddy current for di pot bottom and e dey heat with Joule heating $P=I^2R$. Di bigger di gap between di bottom and di cooking zone, di weaker di coupling.
p-097.example: Induction efficiency na about 85 to 90%, higher than gas stove (about 40 to 50%). If di bottom lift 2mm or more, efficiency go drop noticeably and e go take few more minutes to boil.
p-097.actionItem: Check today whether your pot bottom sit flat on top flat surface without shaking or lifting.

p-098.title: Put heavy books close to di shelf support
p-098.summary: Even for di same weight, di farther from di support, di bigger di turning force (moment) wey di shelf receive, so e go bend or fall.
p-098.principle: Moment wey dey act for di support na $M=Fd$ and e dey follow distance $d$.
p-098.example: If you put 5kg book (about 49N) 5cm from di support, $M\approx2.5\ \mathrm{N\,m}$, and if you put am 25cm, $M\approx12\ \mathrm{N\,m}$, wey be 5 times.
p-098.actionItem: Today when you dey arrange shelf, put heavy things close to wall or support, and light things for outside.

p-099.title: No open fridge door for long
p-099.summary: If you open di door, cold air go pour out and warm air go enter, so di compressor go need to work again.
p-099.principle: Air dey convect because of density difference, and heat wey dey enter na $Q=mc\Delta T$. Air for 300L fridge na about 0.36kg.
p-099.example: If you open di door for 30 seconds, di inside temperature fit rise from 4°C to nearly 10°C, and e need 10 to 20 minutes of compressor running to cool am again. If you open am 20 times daily without need, monthly electricity fit increase by about 2 to 4%.
p-099.actionItem: Today, decide wetin you wan take out before you open di fridge door and close am within 10 seconds.

p-100.title: Noise dey reduce 6dB every time distance double
p-100.summary: Just to move far from di sound source dey reduce noise well well, e be di easiest way to protect your hearing.
p-100.principle: Point source intensity na $I\propto1/r^2$ and sound pressure level na $L=10\log_{10}(I/I_0)$. If distance double, $\Delta L=-20\log_{10}2\approx-6\ \mathrm{dB}$.
p-100.example: Speaker wey be 90dB at 1m go be 84dB at 2m and 78dB at 4m. 85dB for 8 hours and 91dB for 2 hours na di recommended exposure limits, so if you keep distance, safe time go long.
p-100.actionItem: Today for concert or construction site, stand twice farther from di speaker or noise source.

p-101.title: If speed double, braking distance go be four times
p-101.summary: If you reduce your driving speed small, braking distance go reduce a lot, so accident risk go reduce.
p-101.principle: Braking distance from kinetic energy $\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2=\mu mg\,d$ na $d=\dfrac{v^2}{2\mu g}$. E dey follow square of speed.
p-101.example: For dry road ($\mu\approx0.7$), 50km/h (13.9m/s) na about 14m, and 100km/h (27.8m/s) na about 56m, 4 times. For wet road ($\mu\approx0.4$) you need about 98m at 100km/h.
p-101.actionItem: For rainy day today, reduce your speed by 20% from speed limit and keep double distance from di car for front.

p-102.title: Weigh yourself on hard and flat floor
p-102.summary: If you stand on soft carpet or slanted floor, force no go enter di scale sensors evenly and di reading go shake.
p-102.principle: Scale dey measure with di sum of four corner sensors $W=\sum F_i$. If di floor slant or soft, di load for each sensor go change.
p-102.example: If person weigh 70kg, $mg\approx686$ N go divide to about 171N for each of di four sensors, but if one leg press inside soft floor, one sensor go carry more and error go enter.
p-102.actionItem: Choose hard and flat place like bathroom tile for your scale, and always weigh yourself for di same spot.

p-103.title: Suction hook go stick only if you comot di air
p-103.summary: Di force wey dey make bathroom suction hook stick no be glue, na di outside atmospheric pressure wey dey press am.
p-103.principle: Suction force na $F=\Delta P\cdot A$. If you comot di air inside, di difference with outside atmospheric pressure (about 101kPa) go press di plate.
p-103.example: Di area of plate wey get 5cm diameter na $A=\pi(0.025)^2\approx1.96\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, so di theoretical maximum force na $101{,}000\times1.96\times10^{-3}\approx198$ N. For real life e small pass dat one because air dey leak.
p-103.actionItem: Before you stick am, wipe water and dust from di tile or glass, press am hard to comot air, then hang weight wey no pass di allowed load wey dem write.

p-104.title: For daytime, use window light and off di lamp
p-104.summary: Natural light near window for clear spring day dey bright pass indoor light by many times, so for daytime many times e enough even if you off di lamp.
p-104.principle: Illuminance na $E=\Phi/A$ (unit lx). For clear day, near window na usually 1,000 lx or more, and di indoor illuminance wey dem recommend for office and reading na 300 to 500 lx.
p-104.example: If you off three 8W LED bulbs (24W) for living room for 6 hours for daytime, $0.024\times6\times30\approx4.3$ kWh every month go save.
p-104.actionItem: Today for daytime, open di curtain, move your desk or reading place close to window and off di lamp.

p-105.title: For fan, compare airflow (CMM) together with noise
p-105.summary: Even for di same diameter, di amount of wind different. Airflow na di product of blade area and wind speed.
p-105.principle: Airflow na $Q=Av$ (unit $\mathrm{m^3/min}$). Area of fan wey get diameter $D$ na $A=\pi D^2/4$.
p-105.example: If 0.3m fan ($A\approx0.071\ \mathrm{m^2}$) blow for average 3m/s, $Q\approx0.21\ \mathrm{m^3/s}\approx12.8\ \mathrm{m^3/min}$, and e fit mix di air for 30 $\mathrm{m^3}$ room one time every about 2 minutes 20 seconds.
p-105.actionItem: When you wan buy fan or circulator, compare airflow (CMM), noise (dB) and power consumption (W) for di product table together.

p-106.title: Di tighter di window net, di more e dey block insects but e dey reduce wind too
p-106.summary: If mesh number for window net increase, di holes go small and block small insects, but di area wey wind fit pass (open area ratio) go reduce too.
p-106.principle: Hole size na about $25.4/N-d$ mm ($N$: wires per inch, $d$: wire diameter) and open area ratio na $\varphi=\left(\dfrac{p-d}{p}\right)^2$ ($p=25.4/N$).
p-106.example: If wire diameter na 0.25mm, 18 mesh get hole about 1.16mm and open area about 68%, and 24 mesh get hole about 0.81mm and open area about 58%.
p-106.actionItem: Before you change di window net, decide di size of insect wey you wan block and how much ventilation you need, then pick di mesh number.

p-107.title: Di charger efficiency na di extra electricity wey you go pay for
p-107.summary: Di energy wey dey comot from di socket pass di energy wey enter phone battery. Di difference dey disappear as heat from di charger and battery.
p-107.example: 5,000 mAh·3.85V battery na about 19.3Wh. If charging efficiency na 85%, e go use $19.3/0.85\approx22.7$ Wh from di socket, and if you charge 300 times a year, e be about 6.8kWh.
p-107.actionItem: Today when you dey charge, use certified original-quality adapter and charge am for place wey get air, no inside blanket.

p-108.title: Di more you bow your head, di more load your neck dey carry
p-108.summary: Di farther di head weight go forward from di neck bones, di more force e need from neck muscle because of lever effect.
p-108.principle: If head weight $W$ dey forward by $d$ from di neck support point, moment $M=Wd$ go form, and di muscle must hold am.
p-108.example: Head weight na about 5 kgf, and research model estimate say if you bow your head 15°, neck load go be about 12 kgf, and at 60° e go be about 27 kgf.
p-108.actionItem: Today, raise your laptop or phone screen to eye level, and every 30 minutes lift your head and stretch your neck.

p-109.title: Table wey get four legs dey touch only three points and e dey shake
p-109.summary: Three points dey fix one plane, so if di fourth leg no dey for di same plane, one leg go always lift up and di table go shake.
p-109.principle: Equilibrium conditions na $\sum F=W$ and $\sum M=0$. Three-point support dey always stable, but four points go touch only if dem dey di same plane.
p-109.example: If one leg short by 1mm, dat leg go lift and di other three legs go share di load. One folded paper na usually 0.1 to 0.2mm, so you go need to fold some pieces to support am.
p-109.actionItem: Put folded paper or height adjuster pad under di shaking leg, and when e level, press am with hand to check say e no shake again.

p-110.title: When shower water flow don weak
p-110.summary: If limescale gather for shower holes, di holes go narrow and flow go reduce well well.
p-110.principle: Flow for narrow pipe follow Poiseuille law $Q=\dfrac{\pi r^4\Delta P}{8\eta L}$ and e dey follow radius to di power 4.
p-110.example: If hole radius reduce by 20%, flow go be $0.8^4\approx0.41$ times, wey be 59% reduction. If you soak di shower head for about 1:1 diluted vinegar water for 30 minutes, di limescale go dissolve.
p-110.actionItem: Today, remove di shower head, soak am for diluted vinegar for 30 minutes, and rinse am.

p-111.title: Tent water resistance mm na di height of water column
p-111.summary: Di water resistance of camping tent for rainy season mean di height (mm) of water column wey di cloth fit hold.
p-111.principle: Hydrostatic pressure na $P=\rho g h$. Water column of 1,000mm na about 9.8kPa.
p-111.example: Water resistance of 1,500mm mean cloth wey fit hold $1000\times9.8\times1.5=14.7$ kPa. For heavy rain and floor wey person weight dey press, higher value better.
p-111.actionItem: Before rainy season camping, check di water resistance for di tent label (1,500mm or more recommended for fly) and di seam sealing condition.

p-112.title: Check fridge door seal with one sheet of paper
p-112.summary: If di rubber seal for door loose, warm air go leak enter and di compressor go run longer.
p-112.principle: Heat wey dey enter through di gap na $\dot Q=\dot m c_p\Delta T$. Di bigger di gap area, di more air flow and heat go enter.
p-112.example: If average gap na 1mm and door perimeter na 3m, di gap area na $0.001\times3=3\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, wey be 30cm², like say hole wey be size of palm dey open.
p-112.actionItem: Put one sheet of paper for di door gap, close am, and pull am. If e easily comot for any place, clean or change di seal.

p-113.title: Di electricity wey appliance dey use go finally turn to heat inside di room
p-113.summary: Most of electrical energy dey finally turn to heat and e dey raise di room temperature. Di load for air conditioner go increase too.
p-113.principle: By conservation of energy, $Q=Pt$. Appliance power $P$ almost all become heat wey dey inside di room.
p-113.example: If you use 100W computer for 4 hours, $0.1\times4=0.4$ kWh, about 1.44MJ, remain as heat inside di room, wey be di same as 100W small heater.
p-113.actionItem: Today, off computer, lights and chargers wey you no dey use to reduce heat sources inside di room.

p-114.title: Compare energy efficiency label with yearly kWh
p-114.summary: No only look di grade, compare di yearly (or monthly) kWh wey dem write for di label so you go know di real electricity use.
p-114.principle: Energy na $E=Pt$ (kWh). If you multiply di yearly consumption difference by years of use, e become di total electricity use difference.
p-114.example: Fridge wey dey use 300kWh per year and one wey dey use 450kWh per year get 150kWh difference per year, and for 10 years e be 1,500kWh difference.
p-114.actionItem: When you dey buy appliance, compare di energy efficiency grade and di yearly kWh for di label together.

p-115.title: Choose air purifier by CADR and room volume
p-115.summary: For dust season, di purifier performance must match di room size. Di main thing na how many times per hour e dey filter di air.
p-115.principle: Air changes per hour na $\mathrm{ACH}=\mathrm{CADR}/V$. CADR na di amount of cleaned air ($\mathrm{m^3/h}$).
p-115.example: If you use CADR 300 $\mathrm{m^3/h}$ purifier for 25 $\mathrm{m^2}$ × 2.4m = 60 $\mathrm{m^3}$ room, e be $300/60=5$ times per hour.
p-115.actionItem: Today, multiply room area by ceiling height to get volume, and check whether di purifier CADR na about 5 times di volume or more.

p-116.title: Car glass fog na because of dew point
p-116.summary: If glass temperature drop below di dew point of di air inside di car, water vapour go condense and fog go form.
p-116.principle: Relative humidity $\mathrm{RH}$ and air temperature determine di dew point $T_d$, and Magnus formula na $T_d\approx\dfrac{243.12\,\gamma}{17.62-\gamma}$, $\gamma=\ln\mathrm{RH}+\dfrac{17.62\,T}{243.12+T}$.
p-116.example: For indoor 22°C and relative humidity 70%, di dew point na about 16.3°C. If glass temperature na 10°C, fog go form, and if you run air conditioner (dehumidify) together with warm air, humidity for di glass surface go reduce.
p-116.actionItem: If di windscreen fog up today, turn on di air conditioner button and change to fresh air circulation to dehumidify.

p-117.title: Cut thick things with di inner part of scissors blade
p-117.summary: Scissors na lever, so di closer to di pivot di inner part of di blade be, di bigger di cutting force wey di same hand force go give.
p-117.principle: Lever balance na $F_{\text{cutting}}\,d_c=F_{\text{hand}}\,d_h$. Di closer di cutting point to di pivot, di smaller $d_c$ go be and di bigger $F_{\text{cutting}}$ go be.
p-117.example: If distance from hand to pivot $d_h=10$ cm, if di cutting point na 3cm from di pivot, 50N hand force go increase to $50\times10/3\approx167$ N. If na di tip (10cm), e remain 50N.
p-117.actionItem: Today when you dey cut thick packaging or cardboard, put am deep inside di scissors blade and cut.

p-118.title: Climbing stairs na good exercise even if you count am by power
p-118.summary: If you walk up one floor, you dey do work to lift your body, so you dey produce quite big power even for short time.
p-118.principle: Power for climbing na $P=\dfrac{mgh}{t}$. Na di increase for potential energy $mgh$ divide by di time wey e take.
p-118.example: If person wey weigh 70kg climb one floor (3m) for 15 seconds, $P=70\times9.8\times3/15\approx137$ W. Di potential energy for one floor na about 2.1kJ, and if we assume muscle efficiency of 25%, di metabolic energy na about 2kcal.
p-118.actionItem: Today, instead of elevator, climb just 2 floors with stairs, and hold di handrail to walk safely.

p-119.title: For travel adapter, look voltage and current, no be only plug shape
p-119.summary: No be say if di plug fit, you fit use am. If voltage for different countries different, current and device safety go change.
p-119.principle: Power na $P=VI$, so for di same power, if voltage low, current $I=P/V$ go big.
p-119.example: 1,500W device na $I\approx6.8$ A for 220V, but if you use am with transformer for 110V country e go be $I\approx13.6$ A, wey fit easily pass di adapter rating.
p-119.actionItem: Before you travel, check di voltage for your destination and di input voltage for your device label (for example 100-240V) and check di allowed current for di adapter.

p-120.title: For bus wey dey stop sudden, bend your knees and spread your feet
p-120.summary: If bus brake suddenly, your body go lean forward because of inertia. Your posture and foot friction go stop you from falling.
p-120.principle: Inertial force na $F=ma$, and for your foot not to slide, friction coefficient must be $\mu\ge a/g$.
p-120.example: If deceleration $a=3\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ (about 0.3g), person wey weigh 60kg go get about 180N force forward, and shoe-floor friction must be $\mu\ge0.31$ before e no go slide.
p-120.actionItem: Today, if you dey stand for bus or train, spread your feet for di direction wey e dey go and hold di handle.

p-121.title: Sharp knife need less force
p-121.summary: If di blade sharp, di contact area small, so even with di same force, pressure go be much bigger and di material go split easily.
p-121.principle: Pressure na $P=\dfrac{F}{A}$. Di smaller di blade tip area $A$, di bigger $P$ go be for di same $F$.
p-121.example: If blade tip width for 1cm length na 0.02mm, $A=2\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, and at 20N $P=10\ \mathrm{MPa}$. If e dull to 0.2mm, e become 1MPa, one-tenth, so you go need to press harder and risk of slipping and injury go increase.
p-121.actionItem: Test di knife wey you dey use today whether e fit easily cut one sheet of paper, and if e dull, sharpen di blade with whetstone or sharpener.

p-122.title: Inverter air conditioner, no dey off and on am
