p-122.summary: Inverter air conditioner dey adjust compressor speed to maintain set temperature, so e dey more efficient to leave am on.
p-122.principle: Cooling coefficient of performance $\mathrm{COP}=\dfrac{Q_c}{W}$ go higher for partial load because di heat exchanger relatively bigger and di temperature difference go reduce.
p-122.example: If fixed-speed type dey use average 480W (0.8kW × 60% running rate), and inverter dey use about 300W, for 6 hours per day na 2.88 versus 1.8kWh, and for 30 days you go save about 32kWh.
p-122.actionItem: Today, set di air conditioner to 26 to 28°C and leave am on.

p-123.title: Make shade for di AC outdoor unit
p-123.summary: Di cooler di air dey around di outdoor unit, di less di compressor go work, so e fit give di same cooling with less power.
p-123.principle: Di ideal cooling performance na Carnot $\mathrm{COP}_\mathrm{max}=\dfrac{T_c}{T_h-T_c}$. E dey bigger as di condensing temperature $T_h$ dey lower.
p-123.example: If di evaporating temperature $T_c=280\ \mathrm{K}$, e be 7.4 wen $T_h=318\ \mathrm{K}$ and 10 wen $308\ \mathrm{K}$, wey be about 35% higher. For real machine, if you lower di intake air temperature by 3 to 5°C, di power go reduce by 5 to 10%.
p-123.actionItem: Today, put sunshade above di outdoor unit, but no block di airflow for di front and back wey dey 30cm or more.

p-124.title: Use AC and fan together
p-124.summary: Wen you use fan blow wind, di temperature wey you feel go reduce by 2 to 3°C, so you fit raise di AC setting.
p-124.principle: Di heat wey skin dey lose by convection na $Q=hA(T_s-T_a)$, and as wind speed dey increase, di heat transfer coefficient $h$ dey bigger.
p-124.example: If skin na 33°C, room na 28°C, area na 1.8m², for no wind $h\approx5$ na 45W, but with wind 1m/s $h\approx10$ and you go lose about 90W, so you go feel cool. If you raise di setting by 1°C, di power go reduce by about 5 to 10%.
p-124.actionItem: Today, raise di AC to 28°C and run fan for low speed together to try am.

p-125.title: Cool canned drink quick with wet kitchen towel
p-125.summary: Na di principle say water dey take heat wen e dey evaporate. If you wrap wet tissue and put am for wind, di drink go cool by few degrees.
p-125.principle: Evaporation need heat $Q=mL_v$, and for water $L_v\approx2.4\ \mathrm{kJ/g}$. Dis heat dey come from di drink.
p-125.example: If 10g of water evaporate, e go absorb about 24kJ, so for 355mL drink, theoretically e go drop $\Delta T=24/(0.355\times4.0)\approx17\ \mathrm{K}$. For real life, e be about 5 to 8°C for 10 minutes under wind.
p-125.actionItem: Today, wrap lukewarm can with wet kitchen towel and put am before fan for 10 minutes.

p-126.title: Sunshade work better wen e block from outside di glass
p-126.summary: If you cover di sunlight after e don pass through di glass, di heat don already enter inside di room. Outside shade work far better.
p-126.principle: Di solar heat wey dey enter through window na $Q=\mathrm{SHGC}\times A\times I$. Wen you put shade, di effective SHGC go reduce.
p-126.example: For 2m² window and sunlight 600W/m², clear glass (SHGC 0.8) na 960W, indoor blind (0.5) na 600W, and outside shade (0.15) na about 180W, wey be reduction of about 80%.
p-126.actionItem: Today, check which sunshade (awning, bamboo blind, roller screen) fit install for di outside of di window.

p-127.title: Inside parked car dey hot sharp sharp
p-127.summary: Under sun, inside car dey trap heat like greenhouse, so e dey dangerous to leave child or pet inside even for short time.
p-127.principle: Glass dey allow short-wave sunlight pass and e dey trap di long-wave (infrared) wey di heated inside dey give out. Di absorbed heat $Q=\alpha IA$ pass di convection and conduction loss.
p-127.example: For 30°C outside, inside di car fit reach about 50°C inside 30 minutes, and di dashboard fit pass 70°C. Even if you open window small, di temperature rise no dey reduce well.
p-127.actionItem: Today, every time wey you dey comot from car, check di back seat, and never leave child or pet inside.

p-128.title: Set bicycle seat height make di knee bend small
p-128.summary: If di seat low too much, e dey put heavy load on di knee, and if e high too much, di hip go dey shake and e fit hurt di waist and knee.
p-128.principle: Common approximate formula na seat height $\approx0.883\times$ (leg length from floor to crotch). Wen di pedal dey for di lowest position, di knee dey bend 25 to 35°.
p-128.example: If leg length na 80cm, di seat height na $0.883\times80\approx70.6$ cm (from di pedal axle to di top of di seat).
p-128.actionItem: Today, before you ride, measure di seat height, put di pedal for di lowest position and put your heel on am, den check say di knee almost straight.

p-129.title: If you lower shower water temperature by 2 to 4°C, energy go reduce
p-129.summary: Even if you use di same amount of hot water, to heat di water to higher temperature need more energy.
p-129.principle: Di heat to warm water na $Q=mc\Delta T$. Di specific heat of water na $c=4.18\ \mathrm{kJ/(kg\,K)}$.
p-129.example: If tap water na 15°C and you heat 40L of shower water to 42°C, e be $40\times4.18\times27\approx4{,}514$ kJ (1.25kWh), and for 38°C na about 3,846kJ (1.07kWh), wey be difference of 0.19kWh per shower and about 68kWh for one year.
p-129.actionItem: Today, try lower your shower water temperature by 2 to 4°C, and if cold dey catch you, first think about reducing di shower time.

p-130.title: Try reduce only 10km/h for highway
p-130.summary: Air resistance dey increase with di square of speed, so even if you reduce speed small, you go save fuel well.
p-130.principle: Di air resistance force na $F_d=\tfrac{1}{2}C_d\rho A v^2$ and di power wey e dey use na $P=\tfrac{1}{2}C_d\rho A v^3$.
p-130.example: If $C_dA=0.7\ \mathrm{m^2}$, 110km/h (30.6m/s) na about 12.0kW and 100km/h na about 9.0kW, wey be 25% less. Energy per distance become $(100/110)^2\approx0.83$ times, 17% less, and di time for 100km go only increase by 5 minutes.
p-130.actionItem: Today, for highway, reduce 10km/h within di speed limit and drive for steady speed.

p-131.title: Check life jacket weight range and buoyancy (N)
p-131.summary: Swimming tube no be life jacket. Life jacket dey give enough buoyancy to keep your face above water.
p-131.principle: Buoyancy na $F_b=\rho V g$. If e push away 1L of water, e dey receive about 9.8N of force.
p-131.example: Life jacket wey get 50N buoyancy rating equal to di buoyancy of pushing away about 5L of water (about 5.1 kgf). Child and adult need different buoyancy, so di product must match di weight range.
p-131.actionItem: Before you go water play, check di weight range and certification mark for di life jacket label, and after you wear am, tighten di chin strap well.

p-132.title: If you ride bicycle behind person, e go dey less stress
p-132.summary: Because of slipstream, di person for front dey block di wind, so you fit ride di same speed with far less effort.
p-132.principle: Air resistance power na $P=\tfrac{1}{2}C_d\rho A v^3$. If you ride behind, di effective $C_d$ go reduce.
p-132.example: For flat road 30km/h (8.3m/s), if $C_dA=0.35\ \mathrm{m^2}$ then $P\approx0.5\times0.35\times1.2\times8.3^3\approx120\ \mathrm{W}$, and if you dey directly behind, e reduce 30 to 40% to about 75 to 85W.
p-132.actionItem: Today for group ride, keep 1 to 2m distance behind di person for front, but make sure say di front wheels no overlap.

p-133.title: For fast charger, check certification and heat
p-133.summary: As di charging power dey bigger, di heat dey increase too, so certified charger and ventilation dey decide safety and battery life.
p-133.principle: Power na $P=VI$ and conversion loss na $P_\mathrm{loss}=(1-\eta)P$. If efficiency $\eta=0.88$, 20W charger go turn about 2.4W to heat.
p-133.example: Di heat from 5W charger na about 0.6W, and 65W charger na about 7.8W. If heat no fit comot like inside blanket, di battery go pass 35°C, charging go slow and di life go reduce.
p-133.actionItem: Today, check di charger for certification mark like KC and di W rating wey match your device, and no charge under blanket.

p-134.title: If you go stand pass 10 seconds, better turn off di engine
p-134.summary: Engine wey dey idle dey keep burning fuel even if e no dey move. Di longer you dey stand, di bigger di waste.
p-134.principle: Fuel consumption na $V_f=\dot V_f\,t$ and di idling fuel consumption rate $\dot V_f$ for passenger car na usually about 0.6 to 1L/h.
p-134.example: If $\dot V_f=0.8$ L/h, 5 minutes (300 s) idling na $0.8/3600\times300\approx0.067$ L, and if you do am once a day for 365 days e be about 24L.
p-134.actionItem: Wen you dey wait for person or for parking lot, turn off di engine (if your car get auto stop for traffic light, just use am as e be).

p-135.title: Even same body weight fit make narrow heel pressure plenty times bigger
p-135.summary: Wen body weight concentrate for one point, pressure go increase and e dey hard for both di foot and di ground.
p-135.principle: Pressure na $P=F/A$. Even with di same force, if di contact area $A$ small, pressure dey bigger.
p-135.example: If 60 kgf (about 588N) body weight dey on one foot, heel wey get 1cm² contact area na about 5.9MPa and wide heel wey get 20cm² na about 0.29MPa, wey be difference of about 20 times.
p-135.actionItem: For day wey you go walk long, wear shoes wey get wide contact surface to reduce load on your foot and knee.

p-136.title: For noise between floors, you need mass and sound absorption
p-136.summary: To block sound, heavy and thick material dey work well, and if you reduce di impact with mat or pad, e go help.
p-136.principle: According to di mass law, transmission loss na $TL\approx20\log_{10}(mf)-47\ \mathrm{dB}$ ($m$: kg/m², $f$: Hz), and if di mass double, e go increase by about 6dB.
p-136.example: 10dB reduction na di level wey sound dey feel half as loud. If you stick felt pad to chair legs, di noise wen you drag am fit reduce by about 5 to 10dB, and thick mat dey reduce di impact sound of jumping.
p-136.actionItem: Today, stick felt pads to chair legs and spread thick mat for places wey you dey walk plenty.

p-137.title: If you use stick wen you dey go down mountain, your knee go dey comfortable
p-137.summary: Stick dey share part of di load with your arms and e dey reduce di load on di knee for downhill.
p-137.principle: For downhill, di knee dey receive about 3 times body weight force as shock absorption, and if di stick share di support force $F_s$, di knee force go reduce to $F_k=3mg-F_s$.
p-137.example: If body weight na 70kg, di weight na 686N and di knee force na about 2,060N. If di stick carry about 20% of am, e go reduce about 410N.
p-137.actionItem: Today for hiking, set di stick length so di elbow be 90 degrees and extend am longer for downhill.

p-138.title: If you thaw frozen food inside fridge, you recover di cold
p-138.summary: Because ice dey absorb heat wen e dey melt, if you thaw inside di fridge compartment, dat cold go dey use cool di fridge.
p-138.principle: For ice to melt, e need $Q=mL_f$ and $L_f\approx334\ \mathrm{kJ/kg}$.
p-138.example: If 1kg of frozen meat get about 70% ice, e go absorb $0.7\times334\approx234$ kJ (about 0.065kWh) to thaw. Di fridge go work less by dat much.
p-138.actionItem: Today, move your dinner ingredients from freezer to fridge di night before. Avoid to thaw for room temperature because of hygiene.

p-139.title: Di tighter di clothesline, di bigger di force wey di line and hook dey carry
p-139.summary: If you pull di line tight to hang clothes, di sag go reduce, but di tension wey dey on di line and anchor points go increase plenty.
p-139.principle: If weight $W$ hang for di middle of horizontal line and di line make angle $\theta$ with di horizontal, di tension na $T=\dfrac{W}{2\sin\theta}$.
p-139.example: For 5kg of laundry (about 49N), if di sag angle na 30° then $T=49\text{ N}$, but for 5° $T\approx281$ N (about 29 kgf), wey be about 6 times.
p-139.actionItem: Today, wen you dey set up clothesline or drying rack, no pull am too tight, and leave di line sag at about 5 to 10% of di line length.

p-140.title: Use feels-like temperature (heat index) to judge di heat
p-140.summary: Even if di air temperature be di same, if humidity high, sweat no go dry and e go hot and dangerous pass.
p-140.principle: Heat index na function of air temperature and relative humidity $HI = f(T, RH)$, and as evaporative cooling dey reduce, di feels-like temperature go rise.
p-140.example: For air temperature 32°C and humidity 40%, e feel like about 32°C, but if humidity na 70%, e feel like about 41°C, wey be zone wey you must watch out for heat illness.
p-140.actionItem: Before you go out for rainy season, check humidity, no be only air temperature, and adjust di time wey you go do outdoor activity.

p-141.title: Di pitch of ambulance sound fit tell you if e dey come near
p-141.summary: Wen siren dey come near, e dey sound high, and wen e dey go far, e dey sound low. Na Doppler effect.
p-141.principle: If sound source dey move with speed $v_s$, di frequency wey you hear na $f'=f\,\dfrac{v}{v\mp v_s}$ ($-$ wen e dey come near, $+$ wen e dey go far).
p-141.example: If car wey get 1,000Hz siren dey come near at 20m/s, you go hear $1000\times343/323\approx1{,}062$ Hz, and wen e dey go far, $1000\times343/363\approx945$ Hz.
p-141.actionItem: Today, if siren sound dey get louder and higher, check around you and make way.

p-142.title: Choose AC capacity by room size
p-142.summary: AC no be say big na good. E must match di room cooling load before e go efficient.
p-142.principle: Choose di capacity to match di cooling load $Q \approx q_0 A$ (about 150 to 200W/m² per area). If e big too much, e go dey on and off in short cycles.
p-142.example: 15m² room suit about 2.3 to 3.0kW (about 8,000 to 10,000 BTU/h). If di capacity too big, di short cycling go reduce efficiency.
p-142.actionItem: Before you choose AC, write down di room area, whether west-facing window dey, and di floor level, and compare di capacity with di seller.

p-143.title: If you raise AC setting by 1 to 2°C, di cooling load go reduce
p-143.summary: Di smaller di temperature difference between outside and inside, di less heat go enter through wall and window, so AC go work less.
p-143.principle: Di heat wey dey enter by conduction na $\dot Q=UA\,\Delta T$, wey proportional to di temperature difference $\Delta T$.
p-143.example: For outside 33°C, if you raise di room from 24°C to 26°C, $\Delta T$ go reduce from 9K to 7K, and di conduction heat inflow go reduce by about 22%.
p-143.actionItem: Today, raise di AC setting to 26°C and use fan for low speed together.

p-144.title: If flame pass di bottom of di pot, gas go waste
p-144.summary: Flame wey big pass di pot bottom dey leak to di side and e only dey heat di air. If you fit di flame inside di bottom, di heat go enter di pot better.
p-144.principle: Di heat wey dem transfer to di pot na $Q=\eta E_{\text{fuel}}$. Di higher di thermal efficiency $\eta$, di less fuel di same heating go need.
p-144.example: To heat 1L of water from 20°C to 100°C need 334kJ, and if $\eta$ na 40%, e use 835kJ of fuel, and if 50%, e use 668kJ. For dis assumption, you go save 20%.
p-144.actionItem: Today, wen you dey cook, reduce di flame so e no touch di edge of di pot bottom.

p-145.title: Water-repellent coating of umbrella and contact angle
p-145.summary: Umbrella dey bounce off water drops because di contact angle of di surface big, and you fit renew di coating after washing.
p-145.principle: Young equation: $\cos\theta = \frac{\gamma_{sv} - \gamma_{sl}}{\gamma_{lv}}$. If di contact angle $\theta > 90^\circ$, e be hydrophobic.
p-145.example: Umbrella cloth wey get water-repellent treatment get contact angle of about 110 to 120°, so water drops dey roll like beads. If friction wear dey reduce dis angle to below about 70°, e go start to wet.
p-145.actionItem: Open wet umbrella wide and dry am for shade, and if water drops start to soak in, spray water-repellent spray on am.

p-146.title: Measure distance with di gap between lightning and thunder
p-146.summary: If you count di seconds from di flash to di thunder, you fit know how close di lightning be.
p-146.principle: Sound speed na about $v \approx 343\ \mathrm{m/s}$ and light reach almost immediately, so distance $d = vt$.
p-146.example: If you hear thunder 9 seconds after di flash, $d \approx 343 \times 9 \approx 3.1\ \mathrm{km}$. If e dey within about 10 seconds (3.4km), you don already dey for lightning strike danger zone.
p-146.actionItem: For rainy season, if you hear thunder, stop outdoor activity and enter inside building or car.

p-147.title: For bicycle braking, use front and back brakes together, with more for di front
p-147.summary: Wen you brake, weight dey shift to di front wheel, so di front wheel fit give bigger braking force.
p-147.principle: Di load wey dey move to di front wheel during braking na $\Delta N=\dfrac{m a h}{L}$ ($h$: height of centre of gravity, $L$: wheelbase).
p-147.example: If mass na 80kg, $h=1.0$ m, $L=1.0$ m, deceleration $a=4\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, then $\Delta N=320$ N. Di static load front 314N and back 470N change to front 634N and back 150N.
p-147.actionItem: Today wen you ride bicycle, no use only di back brake, hold front and back together smoothly. If you suddenly hold only di front, you fit fall.

p-148.title: For non-contact thermometer, check distance and emissivity
p-148.summary: Infrared thermometer dey read temperature from di radiant heat wey di object dey give out, so di value dey change with di surface condition and distance.
p-148.principle: Radiation intensity na $P=\varepsilon\sigma T^4$. Shiny surface wey get low emissivity $\varepsilon$ go read lower than di real value.
p-148.example: Skin emissivity na about 0.98 so e dey accurate, but shiny metal na 0.1 to 0.3 so di error dey big. If di distance ratio na 12:1, for 1.2m distance e dey average di area of 10cm diameter.
p-148.actionItem: Wen you dey buy thermometer, check di use distance and di part wey you go measure, and today follow di distance wey dem write for di manual (usually few cm) to measure.

p-149.title: For small cooking, small toaster oven dey use less heat
p-149.summary: Big oven get plenty air and metal wey need heating, so for one or two person portion, small oven dey enough with far less heat.
p-149.principle: Di heat to heat something na $Q=\sum m c\,\Delta T$. Di smaller di mass wey you go heat, di less heat e need.
p-149.example: To raise tray and inside metal of 5kg ($c\approx0.45$ kJ/(kg·K)) by 180K need about 405kJ, but 1kg need about 81kJ. Heating 60L of air na small, about 13kJ.
p-149.actionItem: Today, if di amount wey you go bake small, use toaster oven or air fryer instead of big oven.

p-150.title: Turn off di fire small early and finish with residual heat
p-150.summary: Di water and ingredients inside di pot dey store heat, so if you cover di lid and leave am, cooking go continue even without fire.
p-150.principle: Di stored heat na $Q=mc\Delta T$, and if lid dey, heat loss small so di temperature dey fall slowly.
p-150.example: For 3kW burner (assuming gas thermal efficiency 40%), if you turn off 2 minutes early, e save $3\times120=360$ kJ of fuel heat. 1.5L of water wey get lid fit keep above 90°C for few minutes.
p-150.actionItem: Today wen you dey cook noodles, soup or steamed food, turn off di fire 1 to 2 minutes early and cover di lid to finish with residual heat.

p-151.title: Wind earphone wire for figure-8 shape so e no go tangle
p-151.summary: If you wind di wire for one direction only, di wire go build up twist and e go tangle wen you open am. If you wind am for figure-8, di twist go cancel.
p-151.principle: Every time you turn di wire one round, twist angle $\theta=2\pi$ dey build up, and di torsional moment na $\tau=\dfrac{GJ}{L}\theta$.
p-151.example: If you wind 1m wire for di same direction 10 turns, 10 twists go build up, but if you wind 5 turns + and 5 turns − (figure-8), di total go be 0 so e go almost no tangle wen you open am.
p-151.actionItem: Today wen you dey arrange earphones or charging cable, no wrap dem around your finger, fold dem for figure-8 shape to store.

p-152.title: Water wey enter ear no dey comot because of surface tension
p-152.summary: Water drop inside di narrow ear canal dey trapped by di pressure wey surface tension dey create, so e no dey flow out easily.
p-152.principle: Laplace pressure na $\Delta P=\dfrac{2\gamma}{r}$ and for water $\gamma\approx0.072$ N/m. Di smaller di radius $r$, di bigger di pressure.
p-152.example: If $r=3$ mm, $\Delta P=2\times0.072/0.003=48$ Pa, so e hard to comot by gravity alone.
p-152.actionItem: After you play for water, tilt your head, gently pull di outer ear and hop on one leg. No use cotton bud, and if pain or discharge dey, go hospital.

p-153.title: Drive tent pegs slant for di opposite side of di rope
p-153.summary: If di peg drive nearly perpendicular to di rope direction, di soil go resist di pulling-out force best.
p-153.principle: Di rope tension $T$ dey split into horizontal $T\cos\theta$ and vertical $T\sin\theta$, and di vertical component dey pull di peg up.
p-153.example: If tension na 100N and rope angle na 45°, horizontal na 71N and di pulling-up force na 71N. If you drive di peg slanted about 45 to 60° opposite to di rope direction, di soil go resist am.
p-153.actionItem: Today for camping or picnic, drive di pegs slanted nearly perpendicular to di rope direction and pull di rope at about 45° angle.

p-154.title: Choose ice box by thickness, lid seal and amount of ice
p-154.summary: Di time wey ice box dey keep things cold depend on di insulation thickness and di amount of ice.
p-154.principle: Heat inflow through di wall na $\dot Q=\dfrac{kA\Delta T}{d}$, and di heat to melt ice na $Q=mL_f$, $L_f\approx334$ kJ/kg.
p-154.example: If heat inflow na 10W, 2kg of ice (668kJ) go last $668{,}000/10\approx18.6$ hours, and if 20W, about 9.3 hours.
p-154.actionItem: If you get outing plan today, fill di box with 2kg or more of ice and drinks wey you don chill before, without gaps, and no open di lid often.

p-155.title: For rainy season, part of AC power dey go for condensing moisture
p-155.summary: For humid day, energy dey go not only to cool di air but also to turn water vapour to water.
p-155.principle: Wen water vapour turn to water, heat of $Q=mL_v$ dey come out, and for water $L_v\approx2{,}260\ \mathrm{kJ/kg}$.
p-155.example: For 60 $\mathrm{m^3}$ room (air about 72kg), if you reduce 2g of water vapour per 1kg of air, di cooler go handle $0.144\times2{,}260\approx325$ kJ (about 0.09kWh).
p-155.actionItem: For humid day today, use di AC dry mode or 26 to 28°C for low wind, and close doors and windows so moisture no go enter.

p-156.title: Electric kettle dey more energy efficient than gas stove
p-156.summary: Wen you dey boil water, electric kettle wey no dey leak heat dey use less energy to boil di same water.
p-156.principle: Efficiency $\eta = \frac{mc\Delta T}{E_{in}}$. To heat 1L of water from 20°C to 100°C need $1 \times 4.18 \times 80 = 334\ \mathrm{kJ}$ ($\approx 0.093\ \mathrm{kWh}$).
p-156.example: Electric kettle wey get about 90% efficiency use about 0.103kWh, and gas fire wey get about 40% use about 0.23kWh of energy.
p-156.actionItem: Wen you wan boil water, measure only di amount wey you need and boil am with electric kettle.

p-157.title: You fit decide di time to warm one cup by calculation
p-157.summary: If you decide microwave time by feeling, e easy to run am too long and waste energy.
p-157.principle: Di heat to warm water na $Q=mc\Delta T$, and di time wey you need na $t=Q/P_{\text{output}}$.
p-157.example: To heat 250g of water from 20°C to 90°C need $0.25\times4.18\times70\approx73$ kJ, and if di output na 700W, e be about 104 seconds (1 minute 44 seconds).
p-157.actionItem: Today wen you dey warm drink, first run am for about 1 minute 30 seconds, and if e no reach, add 20 seconds at a time.

p-158.title: If rain dey fall only from above, you go wet less if you run
p-158.summary: If you run for rain, di time wey rain hit your head and shoulders go reduce, but di amount of rain wey hit di front of your body depend on di distance.
p-158.principle: For rain wey dey fall vertically, di amount wey hit di top na $W_{\text{top}}\propto t=L/v$, inversely proportional to speed, and di amount wey hit di front proportional only to di distance $L$.
p-158.example: If you walk 100m (1.4m/s) e be about 71 seconds, and if you run (3.5m/s) about 29 seconds, so di time wey di top dey wet reduce by 59%. If wind dey blow, di result go change.
p-158.actionItem: Today if rain fall, for short stretch wey you no get umbrella, walk fast within di range wey no go harm safety, and be careful for slippery floor.

p-159.title: 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look 6m away for 20 seconds
p-159.summary: Di longer you look close screen, di more di lens of your eye go keep getting thick and tiredness go build up.
p-159.principle: For di lens formula $\dfrac1f=\dfrac1{d_o}+\dfrac1{d_i}$, di closer di object, di bigger di refractive power (dioptre) $D=1/d_o$ wey you need.
p-159.example: Screen wey dey 40cm distance need about 2.5 D of accommodation, but 6m distance need about 0.17 D, wey reduce di strain by nearly 15 times.
p-159.actionItem: Today, set timer for 20 minutes, and every time e ring, look far place wey dey 6m or more for 20 seconds.

p-160.title: If rip current carry you, swim parallel to di shore
p-160.summary: Rip current na narrow, fast water path wey dey go from di shore toward di sea, and if you swim against am, you go tire.
p-160.principle: According to di continuity equation $A_1v_1=A_2v_2$, if water squeeze enter narrow channel, di flow speed go increase.
p-160.example: Di speed of rip current fit reach up to about 2m/s, wey faster than human swimming speed (about 1m/s), and di width na usually few tens of metres, so if you move sideways 20 to 30m, you fit escape.
p-160.actionItem: If you get beach plan today, play for place wey lifeguard dey, and if rip current carry you, save your strength, swim parallel to di shore and wave your hand to ask for rescue.

p-161.title: Di best parasol na di one wey bright outside and dark inside
p-161.summary: Di white outside dey reflect sunlight, and di dark colour inside dey absorb di reflected light wey dey come up from di ground.
p-161.principle: Di radiation wey di surface dey absorb na $q=(1-\alpha)I$. $\alpha$ na di reflectance.
p-161.example: For noon sunlight 800 $\mathrm{W/m^2}$, white wey get reflectance 0.7 dey absorb 240 $\mathrm{W/m^2}$, and black wey get reflectance 0.05 dey absorb 760 $\mathrm{W/m^2}$ (assumed values).
p-161.actionItem: Wen you dey buy parasol, check di outside colour and UV protection mark like UPF 50+.

p-162.title: Why big fan dey more efficient
p-162.summary: For di same wind, big blade fan wey run for low speed dey use far less energy.
p-162.principle: Air kinetic energy power $P = \frac{1}{2}\rho A v^3 = \frac{\rho Q^3}{2A^2}$ ($Q = Av$ airflow).
p-162.example: For airflow 0.5m³/s, 30cm diameter get theoretical power of about 15W and 60cm diameter about 1W. If di area na 4 times, di power na 1/16.
p-162.actionItem: Wen you dey buy fan, compare di blade diameter and use big one for low speed.

p-163.title: For 5km, bicycle dey use far less energy than car
p-163.summary: If you go near place with bicycle instead of car, you fit reduce fuel and energy well well.
p-163.principle: Dem calculate exercise energy with work $W=Pt$ and efficiency. 1L of petrol get about 9kWh of chemical energy.
p-163.example: Bicycle 5km (15km/h, 100W, 20 minutes) na 33Wh, and even if you consider muscle efficiency 25%, na about 0.13kWh. Passenger car wey get fuel economy 12km/L use about 3.7kWh for 5km, wey be difference of about 28 times.
p-163.actionItem: Today, for outing within 5km, try walk or use bicycle.

p-164.title: If you water flower pot from below, water go soak in by capillary action
p-164.summary: Di narrow gaps between soil grains dey pull water up, so even if you pour water inside di saucer (bottom watering), di water go reach di roots.
p-164.principle: Di capillary rise height na $h=\dfrac{2\gamma\cos\theta}{\rho g r}$. Di smaller di gap radius $r$, di higher e rise.
p-164.actionItem: Today, pour water inside di flower pot saucer, leave am for 20 minutes, den throw away di remaining water. Standing water dey cause root rot and mosquitoes.

p-165.title: Measure blood pressure with your arm for heart level
p-165.summary: If di arm dey lower than di heart, di weight of blood (hydrostatic pressure) go add and di blood pressure go read higher than di real value.
p-165.principle: Di hydrostatic pressure difference na $\Delta P=\rho g h$. Blood density na about 1,060 $\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ and 1kPa na about 7.5mmHg.
p-165.example: If di arm dey 20cm lower than di heart, $\Delta P=1060\times9.8\times0.2\approx2.08$ kPa, dat means about 15.6mmHg higher dey measure.
p-165.actionItem: Wen you dey measure blood pressure, sit for chair, lean your back and rest di arm wey get cuff on di desk to match di heart level.

p-166.title: Luggage inside car dey fly forward with big force during sudden braking
p-166.summary: Luggage wey dem no fix dey try to keep moving even wen di car stop, so e become big impact force during sudden braking.
p-166.principle: Di force wey dey act on di luggage as di car dey decelerate na $F=ma$ and $a=v/\Delta t$.
p-166.example: If 10kg luggage stop from 50km/h (13.9m/s) in 0.1 second, $a\approx139\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, $F\approx1{,}390$ N (about 140 kgf).
p-166.actionItem: Today wen you dey load luggage for car, put am for di boot floor and secure am, and no put heavy things for di back seat shelf or on top of di seat.

p-167.title: Waterproof rating IPX number mean di condition wey water touch
p-167.summary: IPX4 mean e fit resist splashing water and IPX7 mean e fit resist immersion 1m deep for 30 minutes, so bigger number no dey always better.
p-167.principle: Water pressure na $P=\rho g h$. Di pressure for 1m depth na about 9.8kPa.
p-167.example: IPX4 dem test am with water wey dey splash from all sides, and IPX7 dem test am under di condition of 1m depth for up to 30 minutes, and plenty times dem no guarantee for seawater, soapy water or hot water.
p-167.actionItem: Today, check di IPX number of your earphones or speaker, and if you wan use am for rainy day, check say e na at least IPX4.

p-168.title: Dehumidifier: compressor type and Peltier type
p-168.summary: If di room wide, compressor type suit, and if na small place like wardrobe, Peltier type suit.
p-168.principle: Coefficient of performance $COP = \frac{Q_c}{W}$. Compressor type na about 3 and Peltier na about 0.5.
p-168.example: To condense 1kg of water need about 2.26MJ (0.63kWh). Compressor type use about 0.2kWh and Peltier about 1.3kWh.
p-168.actionItem: For rainy season, check di dehumidifying capacity wey match di room size and use compressor type to manage di living room.

p-169.title: Wen night air cool, ventilate to remove heat from di house
p-169.summary: Di heat wey build up for day fit comot without energy if you open window for night wen di outside air cooler.
p-169.principle: Di heat wey ventilation dey carry out na $\dot Q=\dot m c_p\Delta T$.
p-169.example: If di room na 28°C and di outside air for night na 22°C, if you ventilate at 600 $\mathrm{m^3/h}$ (air about 0.2kg/s), you fit remove $0.2\times1.005\times6\approx1.2$ kW of heat.
p-169.actionItem: Tonight, if di temperature drop below di room, open windows for cross ventilation and close dem early for morning.

p-170.title: Di reason why drain dey gurgle na change in air pressure
p-170.summary: Wen plenty water go down at once, di air pressure inside di pipe dey change and e dey suck di water for di trap, air dey go in and out and e dey make sound.
p-170.principle: Di pressure of water column na $P=\rho g h$, so negative pressure $\Delta P$ dey pull water by $h=\Delta P/(\rho g)$.
p-170.example: Negative pressure of 100Pa equal to water column of $100/(1000\times9.8)\approx10$ mm height. If di water seal depth of di trap na 50mm or more, e usually hold.
p-170.actionItem: Today if drain dey gurgle, pour water slowly, and if e repeat, ask di building management or plumber to check am.

p-171.title: Fan wind dey stop mosquito
p-171.summary: Mosquito dey fly slow, so e hard for dem to come near where fan wind dey.
p-171.principle: Di flight speed of mosquito na about 1.5m/s or less, so if wind speed $v_{wind} > v_{mosq}$, e hard for dem to come near, and di wind dey scatter di carbon dioxide plume too.
p-171.example: Fan wey get 3m/s wind speed na 2 times di maximum speed of mosquito. If you direct di wind to di leg side, di chance of dem to come bite go reduce.
p-171.actionItem: For balcony or outdoors, turn on fan pointing to leg height.

p-172.title: Wen you pass big vehicle for highway, prepare for crosswind
p-172.summary: If sudden crosswind blow near truck or for bridge, di car go push to one side.
p-172.principle: Di force wey wind apply on di car na $F=\tfrac12\rho C A v^2$, proportional to di square of wind speed $v$.
p-172.example: If wind speed na 20m/s (72km/h), side area 2.5 $\mathrm{m^2}$, $C\approx0.8$, then $F\approx0.5\times1.2\times0.8\times2.5\times400\approx480$ N.
p-172.actionItem: Today if rain or strong wind forecast dey, hold di steering wheel with two hands for bridge and tunnel exits and reduce speed.

p-173.title: Choose cooling fabric by di contact cooling value (Q-max)
p-173.summary: Cooling material dey take heat quick as e touch di skin so e dey feel cool, and dem dey show dat level as Q-max.
p-173.principle: Di heat flux for di moment of contact na $q\propto\dfrac{b\,\Delta T}{\sqrt{t}}$, and di bigger di thermal effusivity $b=\sqrt{k\rho c}$, di colder e go feel.
p-173.example: At di moment wey e touch with $\Delta T=5$ K, fabric wey get Q-max of 0.25 $\mathrm{W/cm^2}$ dey take heat about 1.7 times faster than fabric wey get 0.15 (example).
p-173.actionItem: Wen you dey choose summer clothes or bedding, check di Q-max value for di label (usually 0.2 or above dem dey mark as cooling).

p-174.title: Calculate electric bicycle range with battery Wh and consumption
p-174.summary: If you divide di battery capacity (Wh) by di power wey you dey use per 1km (Wh/km), you fit estimate di range.
p-174.principle: Range na $d=E/e$ and air resistance na $F\propto v^2$, so di faster you go, di bigger $e$.
p-174.example: If battery na 500Wh and consumption na 15Wh/km, e be about 33km. 25km/h get drag of $(25/20)^2\approx1.56$ times than 20km/h, so di distance go short.
p-174.actionItem: Today wen you ride electric bicycle, keep speed around 20km/h and check di tyre pressure.

p-175.title: 100kg of luggage for di boot dey burn more fuel for 100km
p-175.summary: Di heavier di car, di more energy rolling resistance and acceleration need, so if you dey carry things wey you no dey use, fuel go waste.
p-175.principle: Rolling resistance na $F_r=C_{rr}mg$ and work na $W=F_r d$.
p-175.example: If $C_{rr}=0.01$, $m=100$ kg, then $F_r\approx9.8$ N and for 100km $W\approx0.27$ kWh. If engine efficiency na 25% and petrol na 9kWh/L, e be about 0.12L, and acceleration energy na separate.
p-175.actionItem: Today, take out di things wey you no dey use from di boot.

p-176.title: Why wet bathroom floor dey slippery
p-176.summary: Water film dey reduce di friction coefficient plenty, so put anti-slip mat for bathroom.
p-176.principle: Static friction limit $F \le \mu N$. If di friction coefficient lower than wetin walking need (about 0.3 to 0.4), you go slip.
p-176.example: Dry tile $\mu \approx 0.6$, wet smooth tile $\mu \approx 0.2$, and rubber mat na about 0.6 even wen e wet.
p-176.actionItem: Put anti-slip mat for di bathroom floor and shower area.

p-177.title: Ultraviolet rays dey pass even for cloudy day
p-177.summary: Cloud dey reduce visible light but e dey allow plenty UV pass, so you need protection even for cloudy day.
p-177.principle: UV index $UVI = 40 \int E_\lambda\, s(\lambda)\, d\lambda$ (erythemal action spectrum $s$). Thin cloud no dey reduce UV well.
p-177.example: Thin cloud dey allow about 80 to 90% of UV pass. If UV index na 8 for June midday, skin fit burn within about 20 minutes.
p-177.actionItem: Even for cloudy day, check di UV index before you go out and apply sunscreen.

p-178.title: After you pass water puddle, press di brake lightly to dry am
p-178.summary: Wet brake pads and discs get less friction so braking slow. If you press lightly, di friction heat go evaporate di water.
p-178.principle: Braking distance na $d=\dfrac{v^2}{2\mu g}$. If braking friction reduce, $d$ go increase.
p-178.example: For 60km/h (16.7m/s), if $\mu=0.4$ e be about 35.5m, and if e wet and drop to $\mu=0.25$, e be about 56.7m, wey be about 1.6 times (assumed value).
p-178.actionItem: Today for rainy season, after you pass deep water puddle, wen di area safe, press di brake lightly few times to check di condition.

p-179.title: Choose pot by bottom thickness and material
p-179.summary: Pot wey get thick bottom and aluminium or copper layer dey spread heat evenly so food dey stick less.
p-179.principle: Fourier law $q = k\frac{\Delta T}{d}$. Stainless steel $k \approx 16$, aluminium $\approx 237$ W/(m·K).
p-179.example: For thickness 3mm and ΔT 10K, stainless steel na about 53kW/m² and aluminium na about 790kW/m², so about 15 times more heat dey flow.
p-179.actionItem: Wen you dey choose pot, check say di bottom flat and thick, and if na induction, make sure say di bottom magnetic.

p-180.title: Use sun to heat water bucket and save shower water
p-180.summary: Sunlight dey give up to about 1kW of energy per 1m², so you fit heat di water for black bucket for free.
p-180.principle: Di absorbed heat na $Q=\alpha I A t$ and di temperature rise of di water na $\Delta T=Q/(mc)$.
p-180.example: If we assume black 20L bucket (0.25 $\mathrm{m^2}$) with $I=700\ \mathrm{W/m^2}$ and absorptivity 0.9, e be $0.9\times700\times0.25\approx158$ W, and in 2 hours about 1.1MJ go enter and di water go rise by about 13°C.
p-180.actionItem: Today if sun strong, put water for black bucket or hose, leave am for sun for 2 to 3 hours, den use am for flower pots or washing car.

p-181.title: Creaking door, stick-slip friction
p-181.summary: Hinge dey creak because static friction bigger than kinetic friction so e dey break and slide.
p-181.principle: Stick-slip: $F_s = \mu_s N > F_k = \mu_k N$. Lubrication dey lower both $\mu$.
p-181.example: If dry metal $\mu \approx 0.5$ drop to about 0.1 after lubrication, friction go reduce by about 80% and di sound go disappear.
p-181.actionItem: Put one drop of silicone lubricant or oil on di hinge pin and wipe away di excess.

p-182.title: Noise add up to 3dB, two fans
p-182.summary: If you turn on two noise machines wey be di same, di sound no double, e only go up by 3dB. For sleep, low noise important.
p-182.example: Two 40dB fans na $10\log_{10}(2\times10^4) \approx 43\ \mathrm{dB}$. WHO recommend bedroom night noise of about 30dB or less.
p-182.actionItem: Compare di noise (dB) rating of bedroom appliances and use only di quietest one wen you dey sleep.

p-183.title: Barefoot for beach for midday, why dry sand dey hot and wet sand dey cool
p-183.summary: Dry sand for midday dey heat up easily and fit burn di sole of your foot, but wet sand wey hold water dey far less hot.
p-183.principle: Wen dem receive di same heat $Q$, temperature rise na $\Delta T=\frac{Q}{mc}$. Di specific heat of dry sand na $c\approx0.8\ \mathrm{kJ/(kg\cdot K)}$ and water na $4.18\ \mathrm{kJ/(kg\cdot K)}$, so water bigger well well and e rise less, and di water dey also take heat as e dey evaporate.
p-183.example: If 1kg of sand and 1kg of water each receive 50kJ, sand go rise about $+62\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and water about $+12\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. So even if di dry sand surface for midday reach 50 to 60°C, di wet sand wey wave touch dey stay around 30°C.
p-183.actionItem: For midday, wear sandals go, and den walk move on top di wet sand for di water edge.

p-184.title: Sea water dey carry body float pass fresh water
p-184.summary: Even di same person go float small higher for sea pass for swimming pool or river.
p-184.principle: Buoyant force na $F_b=\rho g V$ by di weight of di fluid wey object push away. Sea water na $\rho\approx1025\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, fresh water na $1000\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, so e big pass by about 2.5%.
p-184.example: For person wey get mass 70kg to float completely, e must push away 70L of water for fresh water, but only $70/1.025\approx68.3$ L for sea water. Di volume wey must dey under water go reduce by about 1.7L. For Dead Sea wey get more salt (about 1240kg/m³), you go float even more easy.
p-184.actionItem: Try float for sea by laying on your back, breathe in and relax. Do am only for shallow place, and keep your life jacket on.

p-185.title: Make snorkel tube short, no extend am pass 30cm
p-185.summary: If you extend snorkel tube long, breathing go hard sharply because of water pressure, and di air wey you breathe out go remain inside di tube, and na danger.
p-185.principle: Water pressure na $\Delta P=\rho g h$, e dey increase by about 0.1 atmosphere (about 9.8kPa) for every 1m depth. Your chest must overcome dis pressure to breathe air in, and di longer di tube, di bigger di dead space wey di exhaled air dey remain.
p-185.example: If di top of di tube touch di water surface, at 30cm depth e be $\Delta P\approx2.9\ \mathrm{kPa}$, but for 1m depth e be about 9.8kPa, wey near di maximum inhalation pressure range of person, so breathing almost impossible. Tube wey get inner diameter 18mm and length 30cm get dead space of about 75mL.
p-185.actionItem: Today check your snorkel length, and no use equipment wey dem extend pass standard or wey dem join hose to.

p-186.title: Swimming pool floor dey look shallow pass how e really be
p-186.summary: Di floor under water dey look like only about three-quarters of di depth wey you see, so di real depth deeper pass wetin you see.
p-186.principle: When light dey comot from water enter air, e dey refract, and di apparent depth go be $d'=\frac{d}{n}$. Di refractive index of water na $n\approx1.33$, so $d'\approx0.75\,d$.
p-186.example: For swimming pool wey real depth na 2.0m, e go look like $2.0/1.33\approx1.5$ m if you look am from above. 3m depth go look about 2.3m, wey be difference of 0.7m.
p-186.actionItem: Before you enter swimming pool, check di depth mark for di wall, and no dive head-first inside place wey you no sabi.

p-187.title: Why you dey suddenly meet cold water layer for sea
p-187.summary: For summer, sea and lake get warm water for top and cold water for under wey form layers, so even if you go few steps deeper, e fit suddenly turn cold.
p-187.principle: Surface water wey sun warm get small density $\rho(T)$, so e dey float for top, and cold water dey sink under to form stable layer (thermocline). If di layer stable, di water for top and bottom no dey mix well, so temperature dey change sharply for di boundary.
p-187.example: Water density na about 997.0 for 25°C and about 999.1kg/m³ for 15°C, so even difference of only about 0.2% fit keep di layers. For lake or sea, e common say water temperature go drop by 5 to 10°C within few metres, and if wind push di surface water, cold water go rise up and di beach water temperature go suddenly drop.
p-187.actionItem: Before you enter deep place, dip your feet and legs slowly to feel di water temperature change, and on days wey di water cold, no go far at once.

p-188.title: Diving entry speed: 3m height na about 28km per hour
p-188.summary: If you jump from 3m height, you go hit water at about 28km per hour, so to enter water without to check di depth dey dangerous.
p-188.principle: If you ignore air resistance, for fall height $h$ di speed from energy conservation na $v=\sqrt{2gh}$.
p-188.example: If $h=3\ \mathrm{m}$, then $v=\sqrt{2\times9.8\times3}\approx7.7\ \mathrm{m/s}\approx27.6\ \mathrm{km/h}$. For 10m height na about 14m/s (about 50km per hour), so if di height pass 3 times, di speed na about 1.8 times.
p-188.actionItem: Before you jump or dive, check di depth mark, and no enter water head-first if you no know di depth.

p-189.title: For summer clothes, look reflectance, no be colour
p-189.summary: For summer clothes, how much sunlight di cloth reflect and how well air fit pass go decide how cool you go feel, no be di colour name.
p-189.principle: Di energy wey di cloth absorb na $q=(1-\alpha)\,I$. $\alpha$ na reflectance (albedo), $I$ na solar radiation. Light colours get high visible light reflectance, so dem absorb less.
p-189.example: For solar radiation $I=1000\ \mathrm{W/m^2}$, white cloth wey get reflectance 0.7 go absorb about 300W/m², while black cloth wey get reflectance 0.1 go absorb about 900W/m², wey be 3 times difference. But sometimes dark fabrics dey block ultraviolet better, so check ultraviolet protection factor (UPF) too.
p-189.actionItem: When you dey buy summer clothes, look for light colour and fabric weave wey air dey pass well, and check di UPF mark for di label.

p-190.title: Transparent bottle wey get water and glass fish tank fit start fire
p-190.summary: Round transparent bottle or fish tank wey get water inside fit gather sunlight like lens and set fire to things wey fit burn.
p-190.principle: Convex lens follow $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{u}+\frac{1}{v}$, and light from far object like di sun ($u\to\infty$) dey gather for focus $v=f$. Di focal length of spherical container wey full of water na $f\approx\frac{nD}{4(n-1)}$.
p-190.example: Water bottle wey get diameter $D=8\ \mathrm{cm}$ na $f\approx1.33\times8/(4\times0.33)\approx8\ \mathrm{cm}$. For solar radiation 1000W/m², cross-section area of about 50cm² dey gather about 5W, and e dey concentrate for spot of few mm², wey fit reach temperature wey go burn paper or cloth.
p-190.actionItem: Move water bottles, fish tanks and glass decorations wey dey window side, balcony or inside car wey sun dey reach go shade, or cover dem with opaque cloth.

p-191.title: Choose watermelon by di sound wey e make when you knock am
p-191.summary: Watermelon wey don ripe well dey tend to make low and ringing sound, so you fit use di knocking sound as clue. But no decide with sound alone, check di weight and appearance too.
p-191.principle: Natural frequency of object na $f\propto\sqrt{k/m}$. As di flesh dey ripen, di stiffness $k$ dey reduce, so di frequency go low, and if e never ripe, e dey make high and hard sound.
p-191.example: If di mass dey di same and stiffness $k$ reduce by 36% to become $0.64k$, di frequency go be $\sqrt{0.64}=0.8$ times, wey mean 20% lower. If di sizes similar, choose di heavier one, and di one wey get yellow spot for di bottom.
p-191.actionItem: When you dey buy watermelon, knock am with hand to check say e get low and ringing sound, and choose di heavier one among di same size.

p-192.title: Inflate tube and beach ball to 80% only
p-192.summary: Under hot sun, air dey expand and tube or beach ball wey you fill full fit burst, so e safe to inflate am to about 80% only.
p-192.principle: For ideal gas $PV=nRT$, if pressure dey same then $V\propto T$ (Charles's law), and if volume fixed then $P\propto T$. Calculate temperature for absolute temperature (K).
p-192.example: If temperature rise from 25°C (298K) to 50°C (323K), di volume go be $323/298\approx1.084$ times, wey mean e increase by 8.4%. Even if you fill only 95%, e go pass di limit, and for car trunk wey be 60°C (333K), e go increase by about 12%.
p-192.actionItem: Inflate tube and beach ball to 80 to 90% only, and no leave dem for long time inside hot car or under direct sunlight.

p-193.title: Why raindrops no dey pain us, terminal velocity 9m/s
p-193.summary: Even raindrop wey fall from many km height no dey go faster pass around 30km per hour because of air resistance, so e no dey pain. But hailstone dey fast and dangerous.
p-193.principle: When gravity and air resistance equal, di speed go become constant, and terminal velocity na $mg=\tfrac{1}{2}\rho v^2C_dA$ for $v_t=\sqrt{\frac{2mg}{\rho C_dA}}$.
p-193.example: Raindrop wey get 5mm diameter get about 9m/s (32km per hour), and 2mm raindrop get about 6.5m/s. For vacuum e go reach about 140m/s from 1km. Hailstone wey get 2cm diameter dey about 20m/s (72km per hour) and fit scratch car.
p-193.actionItem: On days wey dem forecast hail, check weather forecast and park your car under roof.

p-194.title: Direct air conditioner wind go up
p-194.summary: When you dey cool, if you send di wind upward, di cold air go come down and di whole room go cool evenly.
p-194.principle: Density of ideal gas na $\rho=\frac{PM}{RT}$, e dey big when temperature low. Cold air dey heavy and sink, hot air dey rise, so natural convection dey form.
p-194.example: For 1 atmosphere, air for 18°C (291K) na about 1.21kg/m³, and for 28°C (301K) na about 1.17kg/m³, so cold air heavy by about 3.4%. If you send wind upward, e no go touch person directly, so even if you raise di set temperature by 1 to 2°C, e still go comfortable and energy go reduce.
p-194.actionItem: Today when you dey cool, set di wind direction louvre upward (or horizontal), and when you dey heat, set am downward.

p-195.title: Watching waves for breakwater: if wave height double, energy go be 4 times
p-195.summary: If wave height double, di energy wey di wave get go be 4 times, so to watch waves for breakwater or rocks dey much more dangerous than you think.
p-195.principle: Energy per unit area of regular wave na $E=\frac{1}{8}\rho g H^2$, e dey proportional to square of wave height $H$.
p-195.example: When $\rho=1025\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, wave height 1m na about 1.26kJ/m², and 2m na about 5.0kJ/m², wey be 4 times. Overtopping (when wave pass over breakwater) fit sweep person away at once.
p-195.actionItem: On days wey waves high, no climb breakwater or rocks, and before you comot, check di wave height with sea forecast.

p-196.title: Smartphone overheating for mid-summer: remove di case to protect e life
p-196.summary: High temperature dey quickly reduce battery life, so for mid-summer remove di case and avoid direct sunlight so heat go comot well.
p-196.principle: Conduction thermal resistance na $R=\frac{L}{kA}$, and when heat generation na $P$, temperature difference na $\Delta T=PR$. Insulating case wey thick $L$, wey big, dey increase $R$, so e hard for heat to escape.
p-196.example: If silicone case wey get thickness 2mm and thermal conductivity $k\approx0.2\ \mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$ cover area 70cm², e be $R\approx1.4\ \mathrm{K/W}$. If e dey produce 3W like navigation, di temperature go rise about 4°C more. Lithium-ion battery dey age quick above 35°C, and roughly every 10°C rise nearly double di ageing speed.
p-196.actionItem: When you dey use navigation or charge for sun, remove di case and put di phone for shade or place wey air dey pass.

p-197.title: Frisbee must spin to fly far and straight
p-197.summary: When you throw frisbee, if you give am spin with wrist snap, e go fly far and straight without wobbling, and throwing na light whole-body exercise too.
p-197.principle: If no external torque dey, angular momentum $L=I\omega$ dey conserved. Spinning frisbee dey keep stable position because of gyroscopic effect wey no easily change direction.
p-197.example: Frisbee wey you spin about 5 to 8 times per second fly stably for 30 to 40m, but if you throw am flat without spin, e go flip or fall within few metres. At di same speed, if spin rate double, $L$ go double too, so you need double torque to disturb di position.
p-197.actionItem: Throw frisbee with wrist snap for park for 10 minutes. Before you throw, loosen your shoulder and wrist lightly.

p-198.title: Water wey dem heat for microwave no look like say e dey boil, then e go suddenly burst out
p-198.summary: If you heat water for smooth cup inside microwave for long time, e fit pass boiling point without boiling, then e go suddenly boil up as you touch am, and you fit get burn.
p-198.principle: For bubbles to form, dem need scratch or particle to be nucleus, but smooth cup and clean water no get dis one, so di water go pass boiling point (100°C) and become superheated. If shock or powder enter, e go vaporize at once.
p-198.example: To heat 250mL from 20°C to 100°C need $Q=0.25\times4.18\times80\approx84\ \mathrm{kJ}$, and with 800W microwave e take about 105 seconds. If you increase di time more, some part fit pass 100°C, so even one spoon of powder go make foam overflow.
p-198.actionItem: When you dey heat water, put wooden chopstick or microwave stick inside, and after heating, leave am for 30 seconds before you take am out, and no put your face over di cup.

p-199.title: Preheat pan until water drops roll like beads
p-199.summary: If you preheat stainless steel pan only until water drops roll like beads, food go stick less, and you go save gas wey you for use to heat am more.
p-199.principle: If pan surface pass about 200°C, steam film go form under di water drop, so di water no go boil immediately but e go float and roll (Leidenfrost effect). Dis temperature na good preheat signal to add oil.
p-199.example: To heat 1.2kg stainless steel pan (specific heat about 0.5kJ/(kg·K)) from 20°C to 200°C need $Q=1.2\times0.5\times180\approx108\ \mathrm{kJ}$ (about 0.03kWh). If water drop vanish with sizzling sound immediately, e still dey about 150 to 190°C.
p-199.actionItem: Drop one drop of water for pan, if e roll like bead, add oil and reduce fire.

p-200.title: For plasterboard wall, spread di load with anchor
p-200.summary: Plasterboard weak, so if you only drive screw, e go easily come out, so you must spread di load over wide area with anchor wey dey open from behind.
p-200.principle: Bearing pressure na $p=\frac{F}{A}$. Di bigger di contact area $A$, di less di pressure on plasterboard for di same load. Wedge expansion or toggle anchors dey open from behind and increase di area.
p-200.example: If one screw carry 10kg ($F\approx98\ \mathrm{N}$) picture frame with about 1cm², e be about 0.98MPa, but if toggle anchor carry am with 8cm², e be about 0.12MPa, wey be 1/8. Each anchor get different allowed load, so check di product label.
p-200.actionItem: For heavy things, find di stud (frame) and drive am there, or choose anchor wey get enough allowed load.

p-201.title: Bulb colour temperature K: parlour 3000K, study room 5000K
p-201.summary: Di higher di bulb colour temperature, di bluer and colder di light. For rest space choose low K, and for study and work space choose high K.
p-201.principle: Wavelength wey hot black body emit strongest na Wien's law $\lambda_{max}=\frac{b}{T}$, $b=2.898\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m\cdot K}$. Di higher di temperature, di more e dey move toward blue, and bulb colour temperature na value wey dem give by comparing am with dis black body light colour.
p-201.example: Black body 3000K peak for about 966nm, 5000K for about 580nm, and 6500K for about 446nm, so di higher, di bluer e dey feel. Parlour normally na 2700 to 3000K (warm white), and study room na 4000 to 5000K (daylight).
p-201.actionItem: When you dey buy bulb, check di K mark for di package, and choose around 3000K for parlour and around 5000K for study room.

p-202.title: Check LED flicker with phone slow motion
p-202.summary: LED lights fit flicker without you seeing am, and di cheaper di product, di bigger di flicker, wey fit make your eyes tire. Slow motion recording dey easy way to check am.
p-202.principle: LED wey dem rectify from alternating current dey change brightness at 2 times di power frequency, so e flicker at 120Hz for 60Hz area and 100Hz for 50Hz area. Di period na $T=\frac{1}{f}$, and for 120Hz e be about 8.3 ms.
p-202.example: If you point phone for 240 fps slow motion at di light, di frame interval na about 4.2 ms, so about 2 frames dey inside one period, and you go see stripes or brightness change. Product wey flicker deep fit cause eye strain or headache for some people.
p-202.actionItem: Record your house light with slow motion, and if you see stripes, consider to change am to flicker-free product.

p-203.title: For downhill, use engine brake to prevent brake overheating
p-203.summary: For long downhill, if you only press brake, heat go gather and braking force go drop, so you must also use engine braking with low gear. Fuel cut-off fit save fuel too.
p-203.principle: Potential energy $mgh$ wey you lose from height and kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ wey reduce dey turn to heat for brake pads. If temperature rise too much, brake fade dey happen where friction drop sharply.
p-203.example: If 1500kg car go down 500m altitude, about $1500\times9.8\times500\approx7.4\ \mathrm{MJ}$ (about 2kWh) go become heat. Kinetic energy to stop from 100km per hour (27.8m/s) na about 580kJ. If you use low gear, engine resistance go share dis heat.
p-203.actionItem: Before long downhill start, shift to low gear so you go press brake only sometimes.

p-204.title: If you swing your arms when you dey walk, e dey use less energy
p-204.summary: If you walk with your arms swinging naturally, e dey use less energy than if you fix your arms, and your body dey shake less.
p-204.principle: Arm na pendulum wey dey swing for shoulder axis, wey get natural period $T=2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$. If step rhythm and arm swing resonate, e need less effort, and di swinging arm dey cancel di body twist wey di legs dey make.
p-204.example: If effective arm length $L\approx0.35\ \mathrm{m}$, then $T\approx1.2\ \mathrm{s}$ wey be similar to one step period (about 1.1 s). Research show say if you block arm swing, walking energy consumption go increase by about 10%.
p-204.actionItem: Today when you dey walk, relax your shoulder and swing your arms naturally for 10 minutes.

p-205.title: Why song dey sound good for shower room, reverberation
p-205.summary: For bathroom, tile and glass almost no dey absorb sound, so sound dey remain long and singing dey sound rich. For video call e fit turn echo and be inconvenient.
p-205.principle: Reverberation time na Sabine formula $T=\frac{0.161\,V}{A}$. $V$ na room volume (m³), $A$ na total absorption (m²), wey be sum of surface area times absorption coefficient.
p-205.example: If volume na 7.2m³, surface area about 23m², and tile absorption coefficient about 0.02, then $A\approx0.46\ \mathrm{m^2}$, $T\approx2.5\ \mathrm{s}$. Parlour wey get carpet and curtain na about 0.4 to 0.6 seconds, so sound dey vanish much faster.
p-205.actionItem: If you wan call or record inside bathroom, hang towel or mat to reduce di echo, or move go room wey get soft furniture.

p-206.title: Air conditioner drain hose must slope down to di end
p-206.summary: Air conditioner condensate dey flow by gravity only, so di drain hose must slope down to di end, and if e sag or bend for middle, e go block and water fit leak enter di room.
p-206.principle: Condensate dey flow from high place to low place by gravity, and di hose need downward slope of at least 1cm for every 1m length (slope 1/100 or more). If water gather, e go cause contamination, blockage and leak.
p-206.example: On humid days, air conditioner dey make about 1L of condensate per hour. For 5m hose, di end must low by at least 5cm than di start. If leak wet di wallpaper and floor, repair burden big.
p-206.actionItem: Check say di drain hose slope down to di end, no bend or sag, and di end no dey inside water.

p-207.title: E hard to know di direction of sound under water
p-207.summary: Under water, sound dey travel too fast so di time difference clue between di two ears dey disappear, so e hard to know which side boat or person dey come from.
p-207.principle: Speed of sound na about 343m/s for air and about 1500m/s for water. Direction dey judge by time difference $\Delta t=\frac{d\cos\theta}{v}$ wey sound take reach di two ears, and if $v$ big, $\Delta t$ go become very small.
p-207.example: If di distance between di ears na $d\approx0.2\ \mathrm{m}$, di maximum time difference for air na about 0.58 ms, but under water e be about 0.13 ms, wey be 1/4.4. Di brain hard to distinguish am, so you no fit know where di motor sound dey come from.
p-207.actionItem: When you dey play for water, swim only inside di assigned zone (inside di buoys), and always lift your head to look di boats around you with your own eyes.

p-208.title: Water gun go farthest if you shoot am at 45 degrees
p-208.summary: When air resistance small, water stream go farthest if you shoot am at 45 degrees. Try am when una dey compete for distance for water play.
p-208.principle: Range of projectile wey dem shoot from di same height na $R=\frac{v^2\sin2\theta}{g}$, and e dey maximum when $\sin2\theta$ reach maximum, for $\theta=45^\circ$. For real life, di best angle fit reduce small because of air resistance.
p-208.example: Water stream wey get 10m per second go be $R=10^2/9.8\approx10.2\ \mathrm{m}$ for 45 degrees, and for 30 or 60 degrees e be $\sin60^\circ\approx0.866$, about 8.8m, wey be 86% level.
p-208.actionItem: When you dey shoot water gun, try change di angle to find di angle wey go farthest, but no aim am for another person face and eyes.

p-209.title: Why ball dey curve na spin, Magnus force
p-209.summary: Ball wey dey fly with spin dey curve to one side because di spin dey make di air pressure for both sides of di ball different.
p-209.principle: When spinning ball dey move for air, force $\vec v$ go form wey dey perpendicular to both di velocity $\vec\omega$ and di spin axis $\vec F=S(\vec\omega\times\vec v)$ (Magnus force). Air for one side go faster, so pressure difference go form.
p-209.example: Football free kick wey dey go 108km per hour (30m/s) with about 8 rotations per second fit curve sideways about 3 to 4m as e travel 25m. If no spin dey, e go fly almost straight.
p-209.actionItem: When you dey kick ball for park, give am sidespin with di inside of your foot and observe how di curve direction dey change.

p-210.title: Di sea horizon na only about 4.7km away
p-210.summary: From eye height 1.7m, di distance to di sea horizon na only about 4.7km, so di far sea wey you see for beach near pass wetin you think.
p-210.principle: Because di Earth round, from eye height $h$ (m) di distance to di horizon na $d\approx3.57\sqrt{h}$ km. Dis value don already include di correction for atmospheric refraction.
p-210.example: If eye height na 1.7m, e be $d\approx3.57\times\sqrt{1.7}\approx4.65$ km, and from 10m height of beach building e be about 11.3km. Ship wey dey come from far fit lose di hull first and you go only see di mast.
p-210.actionItem: For beach, look ship for far sea and observe how di hull dey disappear beyond di horizon and only di mast remain.

p-211.title: Press earth leakage breaker test button every month for rainy season
p-211.summary: For rainy season wey get plenty moisture, electric leakage risk dey increase, so check every month with di test button say di earth leakage breaker dey work well.
p-211.principle: Earth leakage breaker dey detect di difference $I_\Delta=|I_{in}-I_{out}|$ between di current wey enter and di current wey comot, and normally if rated sensitivity na 30mA or more, e dey cut power within about 0.03 seconds. Di test button dey deliberately make dis difference to check say e dey work.
p-211.example: If leakage current na 30mA, e fit dey dangerous if person touch am, so e must cut immediately for dis level. When you press di test button, di lever must drop and di power must off, wey be normal.
p-211.actionItem: Save di file wey you dey work on, then press di earth leakage breaker test button to check say e dey cut, and if e no cut, ask electrician to check am.

p-212.title: Check air conditioner remote infrared with phone camera
p-212.summary: If di air conditioner no dey respond to di remote, use phone camera check say di remote dey send signal so you no go call repair person for nothing.
p-212.principle: Infrared LED of di remote dey send signal for about 940nm (wavelength wey eye no fit see), and di photon energy na $E=\frac{hc}{\lambda}\approx\frac{1240\ \mathrm{eV\cdot nm}}{940\ \mathrm{nm}}\approx1.32\ \mathrm{eV}$. Camera CMOS sensor dey detect dis light and show am as bright light for screen.
p-212.example: Point di remote at di camera lens and press button, if faint purple or white light dey flash for screen, di remote dey normal. If you no see am, replace battery (normally 2 AAA) or check di remote first. Some front cameras get weak infrared filter, so dem dey show am better.
p-212.actionItem: Turn on di front camera of your phone and press di remote button to check if you see light.

p-213.title: Why your body weight dey change when elevator start and stop
p-213.summary: When elevator start to go up, your body dey feel heavy, and when e stop, e dey feel light. Na no be say your weight dey change, na di force wey di floor dey push you dey different.
p-213.principle: For elevator wey dey move with upward acceleration $a$, di force wey di floor dey push person (normal force) na $N=m(g+a)$. Di scale dey read dis value, so di apparent weight dey change.
p-213.example: If person wey weigh 70kg accelerate upward by 1m/s², then $N=70\times(9.8+1)\approx756\ \mathrm{N}$, so di scale go show about 77kg. When e dey go up and stop, if downward acceleration na 1m/s², e go feel like about 63kg.
p-213.actionItem: When elevator start and stop, bend your knees small and hold di handle to keep your balance.

p-214.title: Di right side of typhoon direction na more dangerous
p-214.summary: For Northern Hemisphere, typhoon wind dey stronger for di right side of di direction wey e dey go, so for areas wey dey right side of di typhoon path, you must prepare for bigger damage.
p-214.principle: Typhoon get wind $v_{rot}$ wey dey turn anticlockwise and di moving speed $v_{move}$ of di typhoon itself, so for di right side of di direction, di two speeds dey add, and for di left side dem dey subtract: $v_{wind}=v_{rot}\pm v_{move}$.
p-214.example: If rotating wind na 40m/s and moving speed na 8m/s, right side na about 48m/s and left side na about 32m/s, and wind pressure dey proportional to square of speed, so e get $(48/32)^2=2.25$ times difference. Dem dey call dis right area di dangerous semicircle.
p-214.actionItem: During typhoon, check di forecast path from di weather agency, and if you dey di right side of di path, cancel or postpone going out and coastal trips.

p-215.title: Typhoon wind speed double, wind pressure go be 4 times
p-215.summary: If wind speed double, di force wey dey act on window and signboard go be 4 times, so you no suppose measure typhoon with di feeling of weak wind.
p-215.principle: Di force wey wind give to area $A$ na $F=\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2A$ (assuming drag coefficient about 1), wey dey proportional to square of speed. Air density na $\rho\approx1.225\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$.
p-215.example: For 1m² window, wind speed 20m/s na $F\approx245\ \mathrm{N}$, and 40m/s na about 980N (about 100 kgf), wey be 4 times. Big glass window dey receive much bigger force than dis.
p-215.actionItem: Before typhoon, check say your window locks dey okay, and during typhoon, stay away from window.

p-216.title: If window dey rattle for strong wind, use gap cushion
p-216.summary: Window dey rattle for wind because di shaking match di natural frequency of di window, so if you stick cushion for di gap, you fit reduce noise and gap draught together.
p-216.principle: Natural frequency of window frame na $f=\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$. If di fluctuating frequency of wind dey similar to $f$, e go resonate and shake big. Cushion dey add damping and change stiffness $k$ to avoid resonance.
p-216.example: If 8kg window sash dey supported with $k=80\ \mathrm{kN/m}$, then $f=\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{80000/8}\approx15.9\ \mathrm{Hz}$. If cushion make $k$ double, e go rise to about 22.5Hz and damping go increase too, so rattling go reduce. If you block di gap, winter draught go reduce too, and you go save heating energy.
p-216.actionItem: Stick weatherstrip cushion wey thick 5 to 10mm for window frame gap and check if di rattling sound reduce.

p-217.title: Why camping tarp dey flap for wind
p-217.summary: Wind wey dey pass fast over tarp dey reduce pressure and lift di cloth up, so how you fix di tarp for windy day na safety matter.
p-217.principle: For Bernoulli principle, where fluid speed fast, pressure low, di pressure difference between top and bottom na $\Delta P\approx\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2$. Dis pressure difference become di lift force wey dey lift di cloth.
p-217.example: At wind speed 10m/s, with $\Delta P\approx\frac{1}{2}\times1.225\times10^2\approx61\ \mathrm{Pa}$, force of up to about 980N (about 100 kgf) fit dey act on 4m × 4m (16m²) tarp. If wind speed na 20m/s, e be 4 times.
p-217.actionItem: When you dey buy tarp, check di number of eyelets and di reinforcement, and when you dey set am up, put di low side facing di wind direction and drive di pegs deep at angle.

p-218.title: Run fan mode for 10 minutes before you off air conditioner
p-218.summary: If you run am for fan mode about 10 minutes before you off di air conditioner, di moisture inside go dry and di mould smell go reduce, and di electricity bill burden almost nothing.
p-218.principle: After cooling, condensed water drops dey remain for di evaporator. Evaporation rate dey proportional to di difference $(p_s-p)$ between saturated vapour pressure and actual vapour pressure, so if fan push di humid air out, e go dry fast.
p-218.example: Fan mode power na about 40W, so 10 minutes na only $40\times\frac{10}{60}\approx6.7\ \mathrm{Wh}$. If moisture remain, mould and bacteria go grow and smell go come, and e fit lead to air conditioner cleaning cost and performance drop.
p-218.actionItem: Today before you off air conditioner, run fan or dry mode for 10 minutes, or if e get auto-dry function, turn am on.

p-219.title: Always fasten seat belt for turbulence for plane
p-219.summary: Turbulence dey come without warning, so to always fasten seat belt when you sit na di surest way to prevent injury.
p-219.principle: For Newton's second law $F=ma$, if plane suddenly accelerate vertically, di same acceleration go act on your body too. If vertical acceleration na $\pm1\,g$, your apparent weight go become 0 or 2 times.
p-219.example: Person wey weigh 70kg dey get force change of about $\pm0.5\,g$ even for medium turbulence of $0.5\times70\times9.8\approx343\ \mathrm{N}$. For strong turbulence above 1g, person wey no fasten belt fit float up from di seat and hit di ceiling.
p-219.actionItem: While you dey sit for plane during flight, fasten your seat belt well to fit your body, low across your pelvis.

p-220.title: Car wey dey inside water no dey open door
p-220.summary: Door of car wey dey under water no dey open because of water pressure, so you must escape quickly through window instead of door.
p-220.principle: Di force wey water apply on door na $F=\rho g\frac{h}{2}A$, wey be water pressure for average depth times di area. Until di water level inside and outside di door equal, you must open am against dis force.
p-220.example: If door width na 1.0m and water level na 0.5m (area 0.5m²), e be $F=1000\times9.8\times0.25\times0.5\approx1225\ \mathrm{N}$, about 125 kgf. Electric window fit stop to work soon. You must move immediately when e start to enter water, before water fill up.
p-220.actionItem: Keep emergency escape hammer (window-breaking tool) for car where your hand fit reach am, and never enter flooded road.

p-221.title: Unplug appliances when thunder dey
p-221.summary: During lightning, very high voltage (surge) dey instantly induce for wires and fit spoil TV and computer, so unplug before thunder start.
p-221.principle: When lightning current change sharply, voltage $V=-M\frac{dI}{dt}$ dey induce for nearby wire loop ($M$ na mutual inductance). Di bigger di rate of current change, di more kV dey form.
p-221.example: If $M=1\ \mathrm{\mu H}$ and $dI/dt=6\times10^9\ \mathrm{A/s}$, then $V\approx6\ \mathrm{kV}$, wey pass di about 1.5 to 2.5kV wey household 220V appliance fit survive. But when lightning dey strike directly over your head, no go near to unplug.
p-221.actionItem: Before storm come, unplug TV, computer and router or use surge protector power strip, and when thunder dey, no touch wires and devices.

p-222.title: Bring balcony pots inside before typhoon
p-222.summary: Flower pots wey typhoon blow or wey fall fit kill person below, so bring balcony pots and things inside before.
p-222.principle: Energy of object wey fall from height $h$ na $mgh$, and falling speed na $v=\sqrt{2gh}$ if you ignore air resistance. Di danger dey increase with weight and height.
p-222.example: If 5kg pot fall from about 30m height (10th floor), e be $v\approx24\ \mathrm{m/s}$ (about 87km per hour) and di energy na about $5\times9.8\times30\approx1470\ \mathrm{J}$. Dis energy dey similar to about 3.8kg object wey dey fly about 100km per hour.
p-222.actionItem: When typhoon forecast come out, bring inside di pots for balcony rail, clothes drying rack and small furniture, and lock di windows.

p-223.title: Seasickness dey less for di middle low deck of ship
p-223.summary: Di middle part of ship and low deck get di smallest shaking, so seasickness dey less, so choose here when you dey pick cabin or seat.
p-223.principle: Ship dey swing around axis near di centre, so di size of position movement dey proportional to distance from di rotation centre ($s\approx r\theta$). Seasickness dey happen when di movement wey eyes see no match di feeling of di vestibular organ for inner ear.
p-223.example: If side-to-side tilt na $\pm2^\circ$ (0.035 rad), di bow wey dey 40m from di centre go move about $\pm1.4\ \mathrm{m}$, and di middle wey dey 5m go move about $\pm0.17\ \mathrm{m}$, wey be 8 times difference. Di higher di deck, di bigger di shaking.
p-223.actionItem: When you dey book ship, choose cabin for di low deck for di middle of di hull, and after you board, look di horizon.

p-224.title: Shooting stars dey show after your eyes adapt to darkness for 20 minutes
p-224.summary: If you comot from bright place to watch shooting stars, e dey take about 20 to 30 minutes for your eyes to adapt to darkness, so before then you no go see faint meteors well.
p-224.principle: For dark place, rod cells dey become sensitive to light and photopigment dey regenerate, and di visual threshold light level dey drop greatly with time. Full adaptation of rod cells dey take about 20 to 30 minutes, and if phone screen light reach your eyes, di adaptation go break.
p-224.example: After you adapt to darkness, sensitivity to light go be about 10,000 times or more than for bright place. Perseid meteor shower dey peak around 12 to 13 August every year, and for place wey get less moonlight and city light, you fit see tens per hour.
p-224.actionItem: If you go out to watch meteor shower, stay for di darkest place you fit get for 20 minutes without looking at phone, and look wide across di sky.

p-225.title: Why screen no dey show for outdoor for midday, luminance and reflected light
p-225.summary: For bright outdoor, you no fit see screen no be because di screen dark, but because di sunlight wey di screen surface reflect dey cover di screen light.
p-225.principle: Contrast ratio na $CR=\frac{L+L_a}{L_a}$ where $L$ na screen luminance (nit) and $L_a=\frac{RE}{\pi}$ na luminance of ambient light wey di surface reflect ($R$ na reflectance, $E$ na illuminance). If reflected light big, di contrast ratio go near 1.
p-225.example: For direct sunlight $E=100{,}000\ \mathrm{lx}$ and reflectance $R=2\%$, e be $L_a\approx637\ \mathrm{nit}$. For 800 nit screen, $CR\approx(800+637)/637\approx2.3$:1 almost no visible, and for 300 lx indoor, e be $L_a\approx1.9\ \mathrm{nit}$ where $CR$ na hundreds.
p-225.actionItem: On strong sun days, set screen brightness to max or auto, and use your body or hand make shade over di screen.

p-226.title: Why map compass for travel place dey turn wrong
p-226.summary: Phone compass dey read weak Earth magnetic field, so e dey easily turn wrong direction because of magnet or iron near am.
p-226.principle: Earth magnetic field na about $50\ \mu\mathrm{T}$ (for Korea area) wey very weak, so if magnetic field $B_{int}$ wey magnetic object around make dey add, direction error of $\theta\approx\arctan\frac{B_{int}}{B_{earth}}$ go form.
p-226.example: Even if magnet case or car holder add only $10\ \mu\mathrm{T}$, di error na $\arctan(10/50)\approx11^\circ$. Also, Korea get declination where magnetic north and true north differ by about 8°, so you must consider di difference between grid north and magnetic north too.
p-226.actionItem: If map app dey show direction strange, calibrate di compass by moving di phone in figure-8, and stay away from magnet or iron.

p-227.title: Temperature dey drop by 0.65 degree every 100m wey you climb mountain
p-227.summary: High mountain dey much cooler than flat ground for di same day, so if you pack clothes by only looking di heat for flat ground, you go feel cold for di mountain top.
p-227.principle: Atmospheric temperature dey drop as altitude rise by average lapse rate $\Gamma\approx6.5\ ^\circ\mathrm{C/km}$. If altitude difference na $\Delta z$, temperature go change by $\Delta T=-\Gamma\Delta z$.
p-227.example: If start point sea level 100m na 30°C, Cheonwangbong peak of Jirisan (1915m) go be $30-0.65\times18.15\approx18.2\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. If wind dey, di feels-like temperature go be lower.
p-227.actionItem: Before you go mountain, check di forecast temperature for di summit altitude and put light windproof jacket for your backpack.

p-228.title: Tropical night: di wall dey release for night di heat wey e store for day
p-228.summary: Tropical night dey hot because di heat wey wall and floor store during di day dey come out again for night, so you must block sun for day and ventilate for night.
p-228.principle: Heat storage body like concrete dey store heat of $Q=mc\Delta T$ as temperature rise, and e dey release di heat when di room cool. If mass and specific heat big, di stored amount go big too.
p-228.example: If concrete wall wey thick 20cm and area 10m² (mass about 4800kg, specific heat about 0.88kJ/(kg·K)) rise by 5°C, e go store $Q\approx4800\times0.88\times5\approx21\ \mathrm{MJ}$ (about 5.9kWh). Dis heat go slowly come out enter di room all night.
p-228.actionItem: For day, close curtain or blind for window wey sun dey enter, and for night when outside temperature drop below inside, open window to ventilate, then set air conditioner to 26 to 27°C.

p-229.title: Take lukewarm shower 1 to 2 hours before sleep
p-229.summary: Warm shower 1 to 2 hours before sleep dey send di heat inside your body outside, and e dey create body temperature change wey make am easy to sleep.
p-229.principle: When warm water widen di peripheral blood vessels, heat dey escape through di skin and core body temperature go drop: $q = hA(T_s - T_a)$.
p-229.example: If you shower for 10 minutes with about 40°C water and lie down 1 to 2 hours later, studies report say time to fall asleep short by about 10 minutes on average.
p-229.actionItem: Today try take 10 minutes shower with about 40°C water 1 to 2 hours before you go bed.

p-230.title: Plunger dey unblock when you pull, no be when you push
p-230.summary: Plunger na tool wey you fit use press di cup tight under water and pull hard to shake out di blockage.
p-230.principle: Pressure difference between inside and outside of di cup dey create force: $F = \Delta P \cdot A$. You must fill am with water, no be air, so di pressure go transmit as e be.
p-230.example: If cup area $0.01\ \mathrm{m^2}$ and $\Delta P = 5\ \mathrm{kPa}$, force of about 50N (about 5 kgf) go act on di blocked place.
