p-230.actionItem: Today make di drain cup dey under water, press am tight, press lightly, then pull strongly, repeat 10 times (no use am with chemicals).

p-231.title: Screw wey get fine thread dey drive in with less force
p-231.summary: Di narrower di screw thread spacing (pitch), di tighter you fit drive am with di same force, so fine screw better for hard wood.
p-231.principle: Ideal mechanical advantage of screw na $MA = \dfrac{2\pi r}{p}$ ($r$: radius of screwdriver, $p$: pitch).
p-231.example: When $r = 2\ \mathrm{mm}$, pitch 1.0mm na $MA \approx 12.6$, and 0.5mm na $MA \approx 25$, so you need only half di force (ignore friction).
p-231.actionItem: Today for hard wood, choose screw wey get fine pitch, and drill pilot hole first.

p-232.title: Rubber band exercise: resistance dey differ by length
p-232.summary: Elastic band resistance dey increase almost in proportion to stretched length, so stretching am to di same length na di standard for exercise intensity.
p-232.principle: Hooke's law: $F = kx$ (rubber band dey nonlinear if you stretch am plenty, so na approximation).
p-232.example: $k = 100\ \mathrm{N/m}$ band dey give resistance of about 30N when you stretch am 0.3m, and about 60N when you stretch am 0.6m.
p-232.actionItem: Today when you dey do band exercise, mark your hand spacing so you go stretch am to di same length every time.

p-233.title: Cool wind just before rain shower na signal to take shelter
p-233.summary: Sudden cool wind just before storm na cold downdraft of thunderstorm, and na signal say lightning and gust go soon come.
p-233.principle: Cold air get big density so e dey sink and spread: $\rho = \dfrac{P}{R_s T}$.
p-233.example: For 1 atmosphere, air density na about $1.165\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$ at 30°C and about $1.204\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$ at 20°C, wey be about 3% heavier, and gust fit blow up to 60 to 90km per hour.
p-233.actionItem: Today if cool wind suddenly blow when you dey outside and you hear thunder, enter building or car immediately.

p-234.title: For car air conditioner, use outside air first, and when e cool, use recirculation
p-234.summary: Just after you enter di car, open window to let hot air comot, and when di inside cool, change to recirculation to reduce cooling load.
p-234.principle: Cooling load dey proportional to air flow rate and temperature difference: $\dot{Q} = \dot{m}\, c_p\, \Delta T$.
p-234.example: If $\dot{m} = 0.1\ \mathrm{kg/s}$ and $c_p = 1.005\ \mathrm{kJ/(kg\cdot K)}$, outside air 35°C→22°C na about 1.3kW, and recirculated air 25°C→22°C na about 0.3kW.
p-234.actionItem: Today when you enter car, open window 1 minute to ventilate, and when e cool, change to recirculation (for long trip, sometimes ventilate with outside air).

p-235.title: Night photo shake: use shutter 1/focal length rule
p-235.summary: When you dey shoot by hand, if you set shutter time shorter than reciprocal of lens focal length, you fit reduce hand shake blur plenty.
p-235.principle: Rule of thumb: $t \le \dfrac{1}{f}$ (for full-frame equivalent focal length $f$ mm, $t$ seconds).
p-235.example: 50mm lens about 1/50 second, 200mm lens about 1/200 second or less dey safe, and if e dark, raise ISO or steady your body.
p-235.actionItem: Today when you dey shoot night view, put your elbows against your body or lean on wall, and shoot with 2-second timer.

p-236.title: Campfire dey burn well if you stack firewood standing
p-236.summary: If you stack firewood standing and leaning at angle, chimney effect go suck air from below, so fire go catch well.
p-236.principle: Draught pressure wey hot gas column dey create: $\Delta P \approx \rho g h \dfrac{\Delta T}{T}$.
p-236.example: If height $h = 0.5\ \mathrm{m}$, flame side 600K, outside air 300K, e be $\Delta P \approx 1.2 \times 9.8 \times 0.5 \times \dfrac{300}{600} \approx 3\ \mathrm{Pa}$.
p-236.actionItem: Today for camping, stack firewood small tent-style standing, but keep water near and no make fire for place wey dem forbid fire.

p-237.title: If ice melt, di water for cup no go overflow
p-237.summary: Ice wey dey float for water, even if e melt, di water surface almost remain di same, so even full cup no go overflow.
p-237.principle: Floating ice dey push away water equal to e own weight: $V_{\mathrm{d}} = \dfrac{m}{\rho_w}$, and di volume of di melted water na $\dfrac{m}{\rho_w}$.
p-237.example: 90g ice dey push away 90mL water (only about $98\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ out of total volume about $8\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ dey come out above), and when e melt e become 90mL, so di water surface dey di same.
p-237.actionItem: Today fill cup full with ice and water and watch di water surface until all di ice melt (no press am with hand).

p-238.title: Check di green zone for fire extinguisher pressure gauge
p-238.summary: Pressurised fire extinguisher must get gauge needle for green zone (normal 0.7 to 0.98MPa) before you fit use am.
p-238.principle: Pressure na force per unit area: $P = \dfrac{F}{A}$. If gas leak, container pressure go drop and spraying force go weak.
p-238.example: Normal range 0.7 to 0.98MPa na about 7 to 9.8bar (7 to 10 times atmospheric pressure), and if di needle dey red zone or near 0, you must replace or refill am.
p-238.actionItem: Today check say di fire extinguisher gauge for your house or car dey green zone, and check di safety pin and hose condition too.

p-239.title: Seesaw balance if di heavier person sit near di centre
p-239.summary: Even two people wey get different weight go balance seesaw if di heavier one sit closer to di centre.
p-239.example: If 30kg child sit 2m from di centre and 60kg child sit 1m, e be $30 \times 2 = 60 \times 1$, so e balance.
p-239.actionItem: Today if you go playground with child, change where di two of una sit to find di balance point, and make dem come down safely one by one.

p-240.title: Why gap dey for summer bridge and road joints
p-240.summary: Metal and concrete dey expand when e hot, so bridges and roads dey leave expansion space for di joint gap.
p-240.example: If steel ($\alpha \approx 12 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{/K}$) 100m section change from -10°C to 40°C, e be $\Delta L \approx 0.06\ \mathrm{m}$, wey mean e go extend about 60mm.
p-240.actionItem: Today when you pass bridge or pavement joint, look for di gap, and no put stone or rubbish inside di gap.

p-241.title: Torch batteries: series dey brighter, parallel dey last longer
p-241.summary: If you connect batteries for series, voltage go increase and e go bright, and if you connect for parallel, voltage dey di same and capacity go add up so e go last long, but di total energy na di same.
p-241.principle: Series: $V = V_1 + V_2$, parallel: $Q = Q_1 + Q_2$. Energy $E = VQ$.
p-241.example: Two 1.5V · 2500 mAh batteries na 3V · 2.5 Ah for series and 1.5V · 5 Ah for parallel, and both na about 7.5Wh.
p-241.actionItem: Today replace torch batteries together, di same type and di same remaining charge, and no mix new and old.

p-242.title: Windshield cover to reduce wind noise for beach video
p-242.summary: Furry windshield cover for front of microphone dey scatter turbulence and reduce wind noise plenty.
p-242.principle: Di standard for when flow become turbulent na Reynolds number: $\mathrm{Re} = \dfrac{\rho v D}{\mu}$.
p-242.example: If wind speed na 5m/s and microphone diameter na 1cm, e be $\mathrm{Re} \approx 3{,}300$, and furry cover dey reduce wind noise by roughly 10 to 20dB.
p-242.actionItem: Today when you dey shoot video for beach, put furry windshield cover and point di microphone away from di wind.

p-243.title: Why touchscreen dey misbehave with wet hand
p-243.summary: Water drops dey conduct electricity and dey spread over di screen and change di capacitance of many electrodes, so ghost touch dey happen.
p-243.principle: Capacitance: $C = \dfrac{\varepsilon A}{d}$ (relative permittivity of water about 80, air about 1).
p-243.example: If water drop touch am, di sensor fit read capacitance change similar to finger, so e dey misbehave even when di screen no spoil.
p-243.actionItem: Today if di screen dey behave strange, first wipe di water from your hand and screen with dry cloth before you repair am.

p-244.title: Camping burner: use windshield but no cover di gas cylinder
p-244.summary: Windshield dey reduce heat loss from burner and pot, but if you cover di gas cylinder, e go overheat and na danger.
p-244.principle: Convective heat loss: $q = hA\Delta T$ (if wind strong, $h$ go big).
p-244.example: If pot surface $0.05\ \mathrm{m^2}$, and $\Delta T = 80\ \mathrm{K}$ from $h$ increase from 10 to 30 $\mathrm{W/(m^2\cdot K)}$, di loss go increase from 40W to 120W (example).
p-244.actionItem: Today when you dey cook outdoors, put windshield only around di pot and burner, and keep di gas cylinder outside (no use am indoors or inside tent).

p-245.title: Why fog dey form for clear autumn dawn
p-245.summary: For clear night wey no get wind, di ground dey cool by radiation, and wen di air reach dew point, fog go form.
p-245.principle: Dew point approximation: $T_d \approx T - \dfrac{100 - \mathrm{RH}}{5}$ (°C, RH na %).
p-245.example: If na 20°C and 70% humidity for afternoon, $T_d \approx 14$ °C, and if e drop to 12°C for dawn e go saturate and fog go form.
p-245.actionItem: Today, if you dey drive for foggy dawn, put on low beam and fog lamp and keep more distance from di car for front pass normal.

p-246.title: Set your bicycle gear by cadence, no be by force
p-246.summary: For di same power, gear wey you dey pedal light, about 70 to 90 times per minute, dey reduce di load on your knee.
p-246.principle: Power na torque times angular velocity: $P = \tau \omega$, $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi \cdot \mathrm{rpm}}{60}$.
p-246.example: To produce about 210W, at 60 rpm you need about 33N·m, and at 90 rpm about 22N·m of torque.
p-246.actionItem: Today for your ride, change gear and keep your pedalling at 70 to 90 times per minute.

p-247.title: Tidal flat dey open about 50 minutes late every day
p-247.summary: Moon dey take about 50 minutes more to go round Earth every day, so di tide time too dey late by about 50 minutes every day.
p-247.principle: Di lunar day na $T_{\mathrm{lunar}} \approx 24\ \mathrm{h}\ 50\ \mathrm{min}$, and high tide and low tide dey come two times a day, so di interval na about 12 hours 25 minutes.
p-247.example: If low tide today na 10:00, tomorrow na about 10:50, and after 6 days e go be about 15:00, wey be $6 \times 50 = 300$ minutes later.
p-247.actionItem: Today, before you go di tidal flat, check di tide table and decide di time wey you go comot before high tide come in.

p-248.title: Vacuum packer na di force wey atmospheric pressure dey press with
p-248.summary: Vacuum packer dey remove di air inside di bag, and di outside atmospheric pressure go press di food make e stick tight.
p-248.example: If di bag area na $0.03\ \mathrm{m^2}$ and di pressure difference na 80kPa, force of about 2.4kN (about 240 kgf) go spread across di whole thing.
p-248.actionItem: Today, vacuum-pack dry food or portions wey you wan freeze, but still keep food wey dey spoil easily inside fridge or freezer.

p-249.title: Steamer dey cook quick with di heat of condensation of steam
p-249.summary: Steam dey condense into water for di food surface and e dey release plenty latent heat, so e dey carry heat faster pass boiling water.
p-249.principle: Heat wey dem release for condensation: $Q = mL$ ($L \approx 2260\ \mathrm{kJ/kg}$).
p-249.example: If 50g of steam condense, e go release about 113kJ, wey be about 6.8 times more than wen 100°C water of 50g cool to 20°C (about 16.7kJ).
p-249.actionItem: Today wen you dey steam food, keep di lid closed, and wen you wan open am, lift di lid away from your face to avoid steam burn.

p-250.title: You fit guess temperature from cricket sound
p-250.summary: Cricket dey chirp faster wen e warm, so you fit roughly know di temperature from di number of chirps.
p-250.principle: Dolbear's law: $T_{\mathrm{F}} \approx 40 + \dfrac{N_{60}}{4}$ ($N_{60}$: number of chirps for 1 minute).
p-250.example: If na 100 chirps per minute e be about 65°F (about 18°C), and 160 chirps na about 80°F (about 27°C), na rough value wey fit get error depending on di species.
p-250.actionItem: Today evening, count cricket chirps for 15 seconds, multiply by 4, and estimate di temperature with di formula above.

p-251.title: Why sunset dey red
p-251.summary: Wen sun low, light dey pass through di atmosphere for longer distance, blue light dey scatter first and red light remain, so sunset dey red.
p-251.example: Blue (450nm) dey scatter $(700/450)^4 \approx 5.9$ times stronger than red (700nm), so e dey disappear first.
p-251.actionItem: Today, watch how di sky colour dey change for sunset, but no look di sun directly and no point camera or telescope at di sun.

p-252.title: Full moon look like size of one coin wey you put far
p-252.summary: Full moon small pass wetin you think, so small say if you stretch your arm, one grain of rice fit cover am.
p-252.example: If you put 24mm diameter coin about 2.7m away, e get di same angular size, and for arm length of about 60cm, object wey be about 5mm diameter go cover di moon.
p-252.actionItem: Today wen full moon rise, stretch your arm well and use one grain of rice cover di moon.

p-253.title: Traffic jam for festival journey dey start from one brake of di car for front
p-253.summary: For road wey get plenty cars, if one car press brake, di reaction delays of di cars for back go pile up and traffic wave go spread backward.
p-253.principle: Stopping distance: $d = v\,t_r + \dfrac{v^2}{2a}$, and traffic wave dey usually travel backward at about 15 to 20km/h.
p-253.example: For 100km/h (about 27.8m/s), if reaction na 1 second, you don run 27.8m anyhow in dat time, and if you keep 3 seconds gap and drive smoothly, you fit save about 5 to 10% fuel.
p-253.actionItem: Today for driving, keep 2 to 3 seconds gap from di car for front and lift your foot from accelerator early so you go use brake less.

p-254.title: Safe distance for grass trimmer wey dey throw stone na 15m or more
p-254.summary: Di tip of grass trimmer blade dey very fast, so stone dey fly like bullet, so nobody must dey inside 15m working radius.
p-254.principle: Blade tip speed: $v = \omega r$, flying range: $R = \dfrac{v^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$.
p-254.example: If blade radius na 0.115m and 6,500 rpm ($\omega \approx 681\ \mathrm{rad/s}$), e be $v \approx 78\ \mathrm{m/s}$, wey be about 280km/h.
p-254.actionItem: Today before you start trimming, check say nobody or vehicle no dey inside 15m radius and wear safety goggles and face guard.

p-255.title: For sleeping bag check di comfort temperature, for mat check di R-value
p-255.summary: For night cold, more heat dey escape to di ground pass di top, so check di comfort temperature of di sleeping bag and di R-value of di mat together.
p-255.example: For 2cm thick $k = 0.035\ \mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$ foam mat, e be $R \approx 0.57\ \mathrm{m^2K/W}$ (US R-value about 3.2), and for autumn camping, R-value of 3 or more na common standard.
p-255.actionItem: Today wen you dey choose camping gear, check say di sleeping bag comfort temperature dey at or below di lowest expected temperature, and di mat R-value na 3 or more.

p-256.title: You fit read altitude change with phone pressure sensor
p-256.summary: Plenty phones get pressure sensor, so you fit estimate di height wey you climb or come down from di change of pressure.
p-256.principle: $\Delta P \approx -\rho g\,\Delta h$, near sea level, drop of about 1hPa = rise of about 8m.
p-256.example: If $\rho = 1.2\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, then $1.2 \times 9.8 \times 8 \approx 94\ \mathrm{Pa} \approx 0.94\ \mathrm{hPa}$ for every 8m, so 30 floors (about 90m) go reduce di pressure by about 11hPa.
p-256.actionItem: Today, open barometer app and compare di value for ground floor and di upper floor of di stairs (weather change fit change di value too, so measure within short time).

p-257.title: Fix bookshelf and fridge to di wall to prepare for earthquake
p-257.summary: Furniture wey tall and narrow dey fall even with small shaking, so e safer if you fix am to di wall.
p-257.principle: Condition for falling: $mg\,\dfrac{b}{2} < m a\, h_c$, wey be $a > g\,\dfrac{b}{2 h_c}$ ($b$: width, $h_c$: height of centre of gravity).
p-257.example: Bookshelf wey be 1.8m high ($h_c = 0.9\ \mathrm{m}$) and 0.3m wide go fall at $a > 0.3/1.8\, g \approx 0.17\,g$.
p-257.actionItem: Today, fix tall furniture to wall stud with L-bracket and put heavy things for di lower shelves.

p-258.title: Why guitar pitch dey change wen day and night temperature differ well for change of season
p-258.summary: Wen temperature change, di tension of di string dey change and di pitch go change, so you must tune again before you play.
p-258.example: If tension drop by 1%, di frequency go drop by about 0.5%, so 440Hz note go drop by about 2.2Hz (about 9 cents), wey fit sound bad to di ear.
p-258.actionItem: Today before you play, tune di strings again with tuner (one more time wen di change don stabilize after you play).

p-259.title: For curved track for sports field, lean your body inside
p-259.summary: Wen you dey turn for curve, if you lean your body inside, friction force go provide di centripetal force so you go turn without slipping.
p-259.example: If you turn for curve of radius 20m at 14.4km/h (4m/s), $\tan\theta \approx 16/196 \approx 0.082$ so you lean about 4.7°.
p-259.actionItem: Today for curved section, reduce your speed early and lean slightly inside starting from di ankle as you turn.

p-260.title: If contrail dey stay for long time, e be sign say sky dey humid
p-260.summary: If aeroplane cloud no vanish quick and e spread, e mean say di high sky humid reach to supersaturate wit respect to ice.
p-260.principle: Relative humidity wit respect to ice: $\mathrm{RH}_i = \dfrac{e}{e_i} \times 100\%$, if $\mathrm{RH}_i > 100\%$ contrail go persist.
p-260.example: For about -40°C, di saturation vapour pressure wit respect to ice na about 68% of dat for water, so even if humidity wit respect to water na 70%, e go be $\mathrm{RH}_i > 100\%$.
p-260.actionItem: Today, look how long contrails for di sky dey stay, and if e spread long, take am only as reference sign say di upper air dey humid (e no be forecast).

p-261.title: If you put chopstick inside rice container, you fit lift di container
p-261.summary: If you pack rice well and put chopstick inside, di grains go grip di chopstick tight and you fit lift di whole rice container.
p-261.principle: Pressure between rice grains dey squeeze di chopstick and e create friction: $f = \mu N$.
p-261.example: For example, if sideways pressing force na $N = 50\ \mathrm{N}$, and $\mu = 0.4$, friction na about 20N, wey fit lift rice container of about 1kg (about 9.8N).
p-261.actionItem: Today, fill narrow glass bottle with rice, press am down to pack am, put chopstick deep inside, and lift am (do am for table so di bottle no go break).

p-262.title: Choose di heavier fruit wen dem get di same size
p-262.summary: If di size dey same, di heavier fruit usually get more water and no dry too much.
p-262.example: If two oranges of similar volume weigh 220g ($\rho \approx 1.10\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$) and 190g ($\rho \approx 0.95\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$), di heavier one usually get more juice.
p-262.actionItem: Today wen you dey buy fruit, hold fruits of similar size for both hands to compare weight, and check say bruise no dey.

p-263.title: For airport moving walkway, speed dey add up wen you walk
p-263.summary: If you walk on moving walkway, di walkway speed go add to your walking speed and you go move much faster.
p-263.principle: Composition of relative velocity: $v = v_1 + v_2$.
p-263.example: Moving walkway 0.75m/s plus walking 1.4m/s na 2.15m/s, so 200m take about 267 seconds if you stand and about 93 seconds if you walk, wey be about 3 minutes faster.
p-263.actionItem: Today wen you dey walk on moving walkway, stay to one side, hold di handrail, and keep your luggage close to your body.

p-264.title: Reflective sticker for bicycle dey send light back
p-264.summary: Retroreflective sticker dey send car light back di way e come from, so e make bicycle visible for dark road.
p-264.principle: Corner cube dey send light back for opposite direction with three mirrors wey perpendicular to each other: $\vec{r}_{out} = -\vec{r}_{in}$.
p-264.example: Reflective gear fit usually dey visible from about 150m away, but dark clothes dey often only visible within 30 to 50m.
p-264.actionItem: Today, put reflective stickers for your bicycle wheels, frame and pedals, and turn on both front and rear lights too.

p-265.title: No put hot soup inside blender straight
p-265.summary: If you put hot soup inside closed blender and run am, steam go expand and di lid go fly off and you fit burn.
p-265.principle: Ideal gas: $PV = nRT$. If 1g of water turn steam for 100°C and 1atm, di volume na about 1.7L.
p-265.example: If $n = \dfrac{1}{18} \approx 0.056\ \mathrm{mol}$, e be $V = \dfrac{nRT}{P} \approx 1.7\ \mathrm{L}$, so e swell to about 1,700 times di liquid volume.
p-265.actionItem: Today, cool hot soup for at least 10 minutes, fill only half of di capacity or less, open di lid vent, cover am with towel and blend.

p-266.title: Why day and night dey almost equal for autumn equinox
p-266.summary: For autumn equinox, di sun dey exactly over di equator, so everywhere for Earth day and night dey almost 12 hours each.
p-266.example: Declination na +23.4° for summer solstice (around June 21), 0° for autumn equinox (around September 22), and -23.4° for winter solstice (around December 21).
p-266.actionItem: Today, check di sunrise and sunset times and calculate if di day length na about 12 hours.

p-267.title: Bleed air from boiler and radiator for change of season
p-267.summary: If air fill di heating pipe, water no fit circulate well and di upper part of di radiator go cold. If you bleed di air, e go warm more with di same fuel.
p-267.principle: Heat supply dey proportional to circulation flow rate: $Q = \dot{m}\, c\, \Delta T$.
p-267.example: For 1kW radiator, if $\Delta T = 15\ \mathrm{K}$, water must flow about $1\ \mathrm{L/min}$ and di part wey air dey no fit produce heat.
p-267.actionItem: After you turn off di heating and e don cool, open di air valve of radiator wey di upper part cold to bleed di air, and check di boiler pressure as di manual say.

p-268.title: For slope parking, turn di wheels to lean on di curb
p-268.summary: Wen you park for slope, apart from handbrake and gear, if you set di wheel direction toward di curb, di curb go stop di car if e slip.
p-268.principle: Force along di slope: $F = mg\sin\theta$, friction: $f = \mu N$.
p-268.example: If 1,500kg car stand for 10% slope ($\theta \approx 5.7^\circ$), about 1.46kN (about 150 kgf) dey pull am down.
p-268.actionItem: Today, for downhill parking turn di wheels toward di curb, and for uphill curb parking turn am di other way, and engage handbrake and P (or 1st gear).

p-269.title: Nearby scenery for outside train window dey pass faster
p-269.summary: Even if you dey travel at di same speed, near objects dey pass fast because di line of sight dey turn quick, but far mountain dey look slow.
p-269.example: For 100km/h (27.8m/s), tree wey dey 20m away na $\omega \approx 1.39\ \mathrm{rad/s} \approx 80^\circ/\mathrm{s}$, and mountain wey dey 5km away na about $0.3^\circ/\mathrm{s}$.
p-269.actionItem: Today, if travel make you dizzy, look far mountain or sky instead of nearby scenery.

p-270.title: Na foot friction dey win tug-of-war, no be body weight
p-270.summary: For tug-of-war, di rope dey pull with di same force for both sides, and na di maximum friction force wey di ground dey support di feet with dey decide who win.
p-270.principle: Static friction: $f \le \mu N$ ($N = mg$), di tension for di rope dey di same for both sides (action-reaction).
p-270.example: For body weight of 70kg, for dry ground $\mu = 0.8$ e be about 550N maximum, and for slippery ground $\mu = 0.4$ about 270N.
p-270.actionItem: Today if you play tug-of-war or similar game, wear shoes wey get good grip and lower your body backward, but no wrap di rope round your arm.

p-271.title: If you cut meat in half, e go cook 4 times faster
p-271.summary: If you slice meat to half thickness, di time wey heat go take reach di centre go reduce to about one quarter and you go save fuel too.
p-271.principle: Thermal diffusion time: $t \propto \dfrac{L^2}{\alpha}$ ($L$: thickness, $\alpha$: thermal diffusivity).
p-271.example: If 6cm thick piece take about 60 minutes, 3cm go take about $60 \times \left(\dfrac{3}{6}\right)^2 = 15$ minutes, as estimate.
p-271.actionItem: Today, slice big meat thin to grill am, and check with thermometer say di core temperature na about 75°C or more.

p-272.title: Hit baseball with di sweet spot so your hand no go pain
p-272.summary: Bat get centre of percussion (sweet spot) wey if you hit with am, almost no shock go reach your hand.
p-272.principle: Distance of di centre of percussion from di handle: $q = \dfrac{I}{m d}$ ($I$: moment of inertia about di pivot, $d$: distance from di pivot to di centre of mass).
p-272.example: If you hold uniform rod of 0.84m from di end of di handle, e be $q = \dfrac{2}{3} L \approx 0.56\ \mathrm{m}$, but real bat dey heavy for di end so di position slightly different.
p-272.actionItem: Today for batting practice, try to hit di ball with di middle sweet spot, no di end of di bat.

p-273.title: If you wind rope three times round post, di force go reduce
p-273.summary: If you wind rope round post few turns, friction go increase and you fit hold heavy load with very small force.
p-273.example: $\mu = 0.3$, 3 turns ($\varphi = 6\pi \approx 18.85\ \mathrm{rad}$) e be $e^{5.65} \approx 285$ times, so you fit hold 1,000N load with about 3.5N (ideal value).
p-273.actionItem: Today wen you dey tie load, wind rope 2 to 3 turns round di post, but no wind di rope round your hand or body, and no use am for loads wey connect to life.

p-274.title: Honey and syrup dey flow more easily if you warm dem
p-274.summary: If temperature rise, viscosity of honey and syrup go drop well, so less go remain for di bottle.
p-274.principle: Temperature dependence of viscosity (Arrhenius type): $\eta = A\,e^{E/(RT)}$.
p-274.example: Honey wey get viscosity of about 10Pa·s for 20°C go dey thinner by 5 to 10 times to about 1 to 2Pa·s for 40°C.
p-274.actionItem: Today, soak closed honey jar for about 40°C warm water for 5 minutes before you use am, and avoid boiling water or microwave.

p-275.title: Keep kimjang for balcony shade inside Styrofoam box
p-275.summary: Styrofoam almost no dey conduct heat, and shade dey block radiant heat from sunlight. If you combine di two, kimjang kimchi go keep constant low temperature for long.
p-275.principle: Conduction heat loss na $q=\frac{kA\Delta T}{L}$, and di thermal conductivity of Styrofoam na $k\approx0.035\ \mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$ wey low pass wood (about $0.12$). Direct sunlight dey heat di container surface by radiation, so shade dey necessary.
p-275.example: For box wey get thickness $3\ \mathrm{cm}$ and area $1\ \mathrm{m^2}$, if di temperature difference between inside and outside na $10\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, e be $q=0.035\times1\times10/0.03\approx12\ \mathrm{W}$. Wood box of di same thickness dey leak about $40\ \mathrm{W}$, wey be more than 3 times.
p-275.actionItem: Today, put kimchi container inside Styrofoam box for di shady side of di balcony, fill di gaps with newspaper, and close di lid.

p-276.title: Clear leaves wey block drain before water overflow
p-276.summary: If leaves cover di drain area, di amount of water wey dey drain for di same rain go reduce well and e go cause backflow and flooding. One minute cleaning before rain na di cheapest prevention.
p-276.principle: Flow rate na $Q=Av$, so if di effective cross-section area $A$ wey water dey pass reduce, di drainage go reduce in proportion. Leaves dey block di gaps of di grate and dey reduce $A$ well.
p-276.example: Di area of drain wey get diameter $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ na about $79\ \mathrm{cm^2}$. If leaves cover half, e be $A\approx39\ \mathrm{cm^2}$, and if di flow speed dey di same, di drainage go drop to about $50\%$.
p-276.actionItem: Today, remove leaves from di drain covers for balcony, rooftop and front of di house with gloved hand or tongs.

p-277.title: 10 minutes of morning sun na tens of times brighter than indoor light
p-277.summary: Even outside for cloudy morning, e bright well pass indoor light, and dis bright light dey help set your body daily rhythm. Short walk for morning na di easiest lighting prescription.
p-277.principle: Illuminance na di amount of light wey dey enter per unit area $E=\frac{\Phi}{A}$, and di unit na lux ($\mathrm{lm/m^2}$). Outdoors for clear day na about $10{,}000\sim100{,}000\ \mathrm{lux}$, and normal indoor na $100\sim500\ \mathrm{lux}$.
p-277.example: Outdoors for clear morning at about $10{,}000\ \mathrm{lux}$ na about 20 times of office $500\ \mathrm{lux}$ and about 70 times of living room $150\ \mathrm{lux}$. Even cloudy day usually dey above $1{,}000\ \mathrm{lux}$, so e brighter than indoors.
p-277.actionItem: Today, walk outside for 10 minutes for morning, no dey look through window. Do not look at di sun directly.

p-278.title: For autumn mountain hike, because of mountain shadow, sun dey set earlier than di chart
p-278.summary: Sunset time table dey based on flat land horizon, so if ridge dey for west, di sun go dey blocked much earlier. For mountain, di time wey sun touch di ridge na di real sunset.
p-278.principle: If di blocking angle of di western ridge na $h$, di time wey sun go down to dat height na di real sunset, and di sun go dey blocked early by dat much, $\Delta t\approx\frac{h}{\omega}$. For mid-latitude autumn, di vertical descent speed of di sun na about $\omega\approx12^\circ/\mathrm{h}$.
p-278.example: If di western ridge blocking angle na $10^\circ$, shade go come $\Delta t\approx10^\circ/12^\circ\mathrm{/h}\approx50\ \mathrm{min}$ earlier. If you add di time wey e take dark after sunset, your time to descend go reduce by more than 1 hour.
p-278.actionItem: Today for your hike plan, set di time to finish descent 1.5 to 2 hours before di table sunset time and put headlamp for your backpack.

p-279.title: For down jacket, look di fill power number and fill weight together
p-279.summary: Fill power na di measure of how well di down dey loft to trap air. Higher number mean lighter for di same warmth, but total warmth dey depend on fill weight too.
p-279.principle: Fill power na $\mathrm{FP}=\frac{V\,(\mathrm{in^3})}{m\,(\mathrm{oz})}$, wey be di volume wey e dey puff up per unit weight. Warmth dey depend on di thickness of di trapped still air layer ($k\approx0.026\ \mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$), so di weight wey you need to fill di same volume na $m\propto\frac{1}{\mathrm{FP}}$.
p-279.example: To fill di same thickness, fill power 600 na $100\ \mathrm{g}$, and fill power 800 na $600/800\times100=75\ \mathrm{g}$ only. For di same warmth, e light by about $25\%$.
p-279.actionItem: Today wen you dey buy down jacket, check both di fill power and di fill weight (g) for di label and compare.

p-280.title: Solar calculator dey work even under indoor light
p-280.summary: Calculator dey use only few microwatts of power, so even indoor light wey weak pass sunlight fit run am well. Wetin matter na whether di photon energy pass di threshold, no be di light intensity.
p-280.principle: Photon energy na $E=h\nu=\frac{hc}{\lambda}\approx\frac{1240\ \mathrm{eV\cdot nm}}{\lambda}$. If e bigger than di semiconductor band gap, electrons go release and current go flow, and if di light weak, only di current go reduce.
p-280.example: Photon of visible light wey get wavelength $550\ \mathrm{nm}$ na $E\approx2.25\ \mathrm{eV}$ wey bigger than di band gap of amorphous silicon about $1.7\ \mathrm{eV}$. $500\ \mathrm{lux}$ indoor light na about $100{,}000\ \mathrm{lux}$ of di sunlight for clear day (about $1/200$), but e enough for calculator wey need few $\mu\mathrm{W}$.
p-280.actionItem: Today, turn on solar calculator under indoor light and cover di panel with your hand to check if di numbers dey fade.

p-281.title: For OLED phone, dark mode dey save battery
p-281.summary: OLED dey produce light by each pixel, so black pixels almost no dey use power. Di more dark background di screen get, di less screen power e go use.
p-281.principle: Screen power na di sum of pixel power $P=\sum_i P_i$, and black pixel na $P_i\approx0$. LCD wey get backlight wey dey always on get almost di same power no matter di screen content, so e no get effect.
p-281.example: If we assume screen power na $1.0\ \mathrm{W}$ for white background and $0.5\ \mathrm{W}$ for black background, for 3 hours a day e go save $0.5\ \mathrm{W}\times3\ \mathrm{h}=1.5\ \mathrm{Wh}$. Dat one na about $15\ \mathrm{Wh}$ of $10\%$ battery.
p-281.actionItem: Today, if your phone get OLED screen, turn on dark mode for settings. If na LCD phone, di effect small so reduce di brightness.

p-282.title: Drive in fog with low beam and fog lamp
p-282.summary: If you turn on high beam for fog, light go bounce back from water droplets and you go see worse. Low beam and fog lamp wey dey shine low dey give better visibility.
p-282.principle: Fog droplets (diameter about $1\sim20\ \mu\mathrm{m}$) dey similar to di wavelength of light, so Mie scattering dey scatter light strongly for all directions, especially front and back. Light dey attenuate as $I=I_0e^{-\beta x}$, and high beam light wey dey close to eye level dey bounce back and cause glare.
p-282.example: For fog wey visibility dey within $50\ \mathrm{m}$, according to road traffic law, you must reduce maximum speed by at least $50\%$, and if na $100\ \mathrm{km/h}$ limit road, e be $50\ \mathrm{km/h}$ or below.
p-282.actionItem: From today, wen fog dey, turn on low beam and fog lamp, turn off high beam, and keep wider distance from di car for front than normal.

p-283.title: Reading light must shine from di opposite side of your writing hand
p-283.summary: Because light dey travel straight, di shadow of hand and pen dey cover di letters. If light dey shine from front on di opposite side of your writing hand, di shadow go go behind your hand and your eyes go work less hard.
p-283.principle: If di height from point source na $H$, di object height na $h$ and di horizontal distance na $d$, di shadow go extend $s=\frac{dh}{H-h}$ behind di object. If di light source dey di same side as di writing hand, dis shadow go land on di letters.
p-283.example: If di lamp height na $H=40\ \mathrm{cm}$, hand height na $h=3\ \mathrm{cm}$ and horizontal distance na $d=30\ \mathrm{cm}$, shadow of $s=\frac{30\times3}{37}\approx2.4\ \mathrm{cm}$ go form. Di common reading illuminance na $300\sim500\ \mathrm{lux}$.
p-283.actionItem: Today, if you be right-handed, put di lamp for front left of di desk, and if you be left-handed, put am for front right.

p-284.title: Climb steep slope in zigzag
p-284.summary: If di height wey you climb na di same, di work na di same, but if you go around di path diagonally, di force for each step go reduce and you go breathe less hard. But di travel distance go increase.
p-284.principle: Di work wey you need on slope na $W=mgh$, e no depend on path, but di force along di slope na $F=mg\sin\theta=mg\frac{h}{L}$, so e reduce as di path length $L$ increase.
p-284.example: If person wey be $70\ \mathrm{kg}$ climb $100\ \mathrm{m}$, e be $W\approx69\ \mathrm{kJ}$. For $30^\circ$ direct climb, na $F\approx343\ \mathrm{N}$ for $200\ \mathrm{m}$, and for $15^\circ$ zigzag na about $F\approx178\ \mathrm{N}$ for $386\ \mathrm{m}$.
p-284.actionItem: Today, wen you meet steep section, choose to go diagonally inside di trail, and no cut across through shortcut.

p-285.title: Winter tyres dey keep soft below 7°C
p-285.summary: Rubber dey turn hard wen e cold and grip dey drop, but winter tyres dey use soft compound even for low temperature. Even if snow no dey, e dey make difference wen temperature dey around 7°C.
p-285.principle: Rubber dey keep elasticity above di glass transition temperature $T_g$ and e dey harden near am. Friction force na $F=\mu N$ and braking distance na $d=\frac{v^2}{2\mu g}$, so if $\mu$ drop, e go long.
p-285.example: If $80\ \mathrm{km/h}$ ($22.2\ \mathrm{m/s}$) at $\mu=0.8$ e be about $31\ \mathrm{m}$, and if di cooled tyre na $\mu=0.6$ e be about $42\ \mathrm{m}$. Di numbers na assumptions to help explain.
p-285.actionItem: Today, check for weather forecast whether di daily lowest temperature go continue to dey around 7°C, and schedule your winter tyre change.

p-286.title: Corridor sensor light dey see human body heat infrared
p-286.summary: Sensor light dey turn on wen e detect di change of infrared wey dey come from body temperature as person dey move. E dey turn on only wen necessary so e dey reduce corridor lighting power well.
p-286.principle: Di peak radiation wavelength of object na Wien's law $\lambda_{\max}=\frac{b}{T}$, $b\approx2898\ \mu\mathrm{m\cdot K}$. If skin na about $33\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ ($306\ \mathrm{K}$), e be $\lambda_{\max}\approx9.5\ \mu\mathrm{m}$, and PIR sensor dey watch di change of dis infrared.
p-286.example: If you keep $10\ \mathrm{W}$ corridor LED on for 24 hours, e be $240\ \mathrm{Wh}$. If sensor turn am on for only 2 hours a day and sensor standby power na $0.5\ \mathrm{W}$, e be $20+12=32\ \mathrm{Wh}$ and e reduce by about $87\%$.
p-286.actionItem: Today, change corridor or entrance light to sensor light, or set di sensor light on-time to 1 to 2 minutes.

p-287.title: Close di door of room wey you no dey use to reduce di heating volume
p-287.summary: If di air and wall area wey you must heat reduce, e go need less heat to reach di same temperature. But if you block am completely, condensation go form, so keep minimum temperature.
p-287.principle: Di heat to warm air na $Q=mc\Delta T$ and $m=\rho V$, so e dey proportional to di volume $V$ wey you go heat. Air na $\rho\approx1.2\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, $c\approx1005\ \mathrm{J/(kg\cdot K)}$.
p-287.example: To raise di air of empty room $25\ \mathrm{m^3}$ by $5\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ need $Q=1.2\times25\times1005\times5\approx151\ \mathrm{kJ}\approx0.04\ \mathrm{kWh}$. If you add di heat to warm walls and furniture and di heat wey dey leak continuously, di real amount go be many times more.
p-287.actionItem: Today, close di door of room wey you no dey use and reduce di heating valve of dat room to minimum temperature, no close am completely.

p-288.title: To avoid glare from oncoming headlights, look toward di right lane
p-288.summary: Di more you turn your eyes away from di light source, di faster di scattered light wey cover di view inside di retina dey reduce. If you put your gaze for di edge of di right lane, glare go reduce and you go still see di road.
p-288.principle: Veiling luminance wey scattered light inside di eye dey create na approximately $L_v\approx\frac{10E}{\theta^2}$. Here $E$ na di illuminance wey dey reach di eye ($\mathrm{lux}$), and $\theta$ na di angle between di light source and line of sight ($^\circ$).
p-288.example: Gaze wey dey $5^\circ$ away from di light source na $L_v\propto1/25$, and for $10^\circ$ away e be $1/100$, so di veiling luminance reduce to $1/4$. Di pupil too dey constrict for bright light so e help more.
p-288.actionItem: Tonight, wen you meet oncoming high beam, no close your eyes, put your gaze for di white line of di right lane and reduce your speed.

p-289.title: Why eyes dey tire if you turn on only screen for dark room
p-289.summary: For dark room, di pupil dey dilated but di screen very bright, so di eye must keep adjusting to di brightness difference. If you gently light di surroundings, di difference go reduce and di eyes go dey comfortable.
p-289.principle: Di pupil area na $A=\frac{\pi d^2}{4}$ and di diameter dey change by about $2\sim8\ \mathrm{mm}$, and retinal illuminance na $E_r\propto L\,A$. If di luminance ratio between screen and surroundings big, di eye must keep changing di adaptation state.
p-289.example: If di pupil diameter increase from $2\ \mathrm{mm}$ to $8\ \mathrm{mm}$, di area go be 16 times. If surroundings na $0.5\ \mathrm{cd/m^2}$ and screen na $200\ \mathrm{cd/m^2}$, di luminance ratio na $400:1$, wey far pass di about $3:1\sim10:1$ wey dem usually recommend.
p-289.actionItem: Tonight wen you dey look screen, turn on indirect light or small desk lamp behind di screen to gently light di surroundings.

p-290.title: Di safety line for subway platform dey because of train wind
p-290.summary: Wen fast train pass, di air beside di train dey fast and di pressure drop, and person fit get pulled toward di train. To stand behind di safety line na di surest preparation.
p-290.principle: According to Bernoulli's principle $p+\frac12\rho v^2=\mathrm{const}$, if air speed $v$ increase, pressure $p$ go drop. Di pressure drop na $\Delta p=\frac12\rho v^2$.
p-290.example: If air beside di train dey flow at $10\ \mathrm{m/s}$, e be $\Delta p=0.5\times1.2\times10^2=60\ \mathrm{Pa}$, and $0.6\ \mathrm{m^2}$ (about $F\approx36\ \mathrm{N}$) dey act on di side area of di body $3.7\ \mathrm{kgf}$. For real life, turbulence dey add and make am fluctuate.
p-290.actionItem: Today, wen train dey enter di platform, step back one more step behind di safety line.

p-291.title: Dark baking pan dey bake faster
p-291.summary: Black pan dey absorb more radiant heat from oven and silver pan dey reflect most of am. Even for di same recipe, di bottom dey brown faster depending on di colour of di pan.
p-291.principle: Di radiant energy wey surface absorb dey proportional to absorptivity (= emissivity) $\varepsilon$, and di emitted power na $P=\varepsilon\sigma AT^4$. Black surface na $\varepsilon\approx0.95$, and polished aluminium na about $0.1$.
p-291.example: For di same radiation environment, black pan dey absorb about $0.95/0.1\approx9$ times more radiant heat than polished silver pan. Dat one be why dem often recommend say make you lower di oven temperature by about $10\sim15\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ for dark pans.
p-291.actionItem: Today wen you dey bake with dark pan, lower di oven temperature by $10\sim15\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and check di browning early.

p-292.title: Bimetal dey control temperature of electric blanket
p-292.summary: Thin plate wey dem join two different metals together dey bend to one side wen e get heat and e dey open and close electric contact. Dis na simple thermostat wey dey cut electricity at fixed temperature.
p-292.principle: Linear expansion na $\Delta L=\alpha L\Delta T$, and di plate dey bend because of di difference in expansion coefficients of di two metals $\Delta\alpha$, and di displacement of di end point na $\delta=\frac{3\Delta\alpha\Delta T L^2}{4t}$ ($t$: total thickness).
p-292.example: If $L=50\ \mathrm{mm}$, $t=1\ \mathrm{mm}$, $\Delta\alpha=7\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{/K}$, $\Delta T=40\ \mathrm{K}$, e go move $\delta\approx0.5\ \mathrm{mm}$ and di contact go separate.
p-292.actionItem: Today, use electric blanket spread out, no fold or bunch am up, and set am to low level wen you dey sleep.

p-293.title: Heat source beside boiler thermostat dey deceive di heating
p-293.summary: Thermostat dey measure only di temperature for di place where e dey, and e dey turn di boiler on and off. If stove or sunlight dey beside am, di whole house go cold pass di setting, and if e dey beside cold wall, e go overheat.
p-293.principle: Thermostat dey work only wen di temperature $T_{\mathrm{sensor}}$ for sensor position lower than di set value $T_{\mathrm{set}}$, so di position error $T_{\mathrm{room}}=T_{\mathrm{sensor}}+\epsilon$ for di room average temperature $\epsilon$ na di heating error.
p-293.example: If heat source beside di sensor make am read $23\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, but di room average na $20\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, di boiler go off even for set $22\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and e go cold by $2\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. On di other hand, $2\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ overheating go increase heating cost by about $14\%$ (about $7\%$ per 1°C as estimate).
p-293.actionItem: Today, remove electric heater, TV, and heat sources and furniture wey dey near di thermostat, for di side wey get sunlight blind.

p-294.title: If polarity of one speaker reverse, bass go disappear
p-294.summary: If you swap + and − for one speaker, di two speakers go sound with opposite phase, and di long wavelength bass go cancel. If di sound thin and di space feeling strange, check polarity first.
p-294.principle: Two waves wey phase differ by $\pi$ dey do destructive interference wey di sum reduce. If wavelength $\lambda=\frac{v}{f}$ much longer than di spacing between speakers, e go cancel almost completely everywhere.
p-294.example: Wavelength of $100\ \mathrm{Hz}$ na $\lambda=343/100=3.4\ \mathrm{m}$, wey be longer than di speaker spacing $2\ \mathrm{m}$, so e reduce well near di centre. $5\ \mathrm{kHz}$ na $\lambda\approx6.9\ \mathrm{cm}$, so if you move even few cm, di intensity dey go up and down and e sound like only di bass don miss.
p-294.actionItem: Today, check say + (red) of speaker wire dey connected to + terminal and − (black) to − terminal di same way for both speakers.

p-295.title: Knee push-up dey reduce di body lever
p-295.summary: If you put your knees on di floor, di lever length go short and di load for your arms go reduce. If standard push-up hard, e good to start with knee push-up with correct form.
p-295.principle: If you see di body as lever, from torque balance $F_{\mathrm{hand}}\,L=mg\,d$ di force wey hand receive na $F_{\mathrm{hand}}=mg\frac{d}{L}$. Di support point move from toe to knee so $L$ and $d$ dey change and di load ratio dey reduce.
p-295.example: Studies report say di load wey hand receive na about $64\%$ for standard push-up and about $49\%$ for knee push-up. If body weight na $70\ \mathrm{kg}$, e be about $45\ \mathrm{kg}$ versus $34\ \mathrm{kg}$, so about $23\%$ lighter.
p-295.actionItem: Today, do 2 sets of 8 knee push-ups while you keep your body for one straight line (head-hip-knee). Stop if pain dey.

p-296.title: Find south with analogue watch and sun
p-296.summary: If you point di hour hand toward di sun, di direction halfway between di hour hand and 12 o'clock na roughly south. Na approximate method wey you fit use for Northern Hemisphere without compass.
p-296.principle: Sun dey move $\omega_\odot=15^\circ$ per hour and hour hand dey move $\omega_h=30^\circ$ per hour. So half of di hour hand angle $\frac{\omega_\odot}{\omega_h}=\frac12$ match di change of di sun's bearing and di bisector dey point south.
p-296.example: For 4 pm, if you point di hour hand ($120^\circ$ from 12) toward di sun, di direction wey be half of am, $2$ o'clock, na south. For Korea, di standard time meridian ($135^\circ$ east) and Seoul (about $127^\circ$) differ so e get about $30$ minutes difference from solar time, so di error na about $\pm15^\circ$.
p-296.actionItem: Today for clear day outside, use analogue watch to estimate south and compare with phone compass.

p-297.title: For magnifying glass, di higher di power (D), di shorter di focus
p-297.summary: Di power of magnifying glass na di reciprocal of focal length, so if di number big, di focus short and di magnification big. Di higher di magnification, di narrower di field of view and you must put di lens close to your eye and di object.
p-297.principle: Lens refractive power na $D=\frac{1}{f}$ ($f$ unit m, $D$ unit diopter), and angular magnification for di eye near point $25\ \mathrm{cm}$ na $M\approx\frac{25\ \mathrm{cm}}{f}=\frac{D}{4}$.
p-297.example: $5\ \mathrm{D}$ na $f=20\ \mathrm{cm}$ e be about $1.25$ times, $10\ \mathrm{D}$ na $f=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ e be about $2.5$ times, $20\ \mathrm{D}$ na $f=5\ \mathrm{cm}$ e be about $5$ times.
p-297.actionItem: Today wen you dey buy magnifying glass, choose di power wey fit di use, and no put am for place wey sun dey shine because e fit gather sunlight and start fire.

p-298.title: Energy recovery ventilation dey recover di heat wey dey go out
p-298.summary: Na device wey dey pass di indoor heat wey dem for waste during ventilation to di cold air wey dey enter. E dey change di air but e dey keep much of di heating heat.
p-298.principle: Heat recovery efficiency na $\eta=\frac{T_{\mathrm{supply}}-T_{\mathrm{out}}}{T_{\mathrm{in}}-T_{\mathrm{out}}}$, and ventilation heat loss na $P=\rho c\,\dot V\,\Delta T$ ($\rho c\approx1200\ \mathrm{J/(m^3\cdot K)}$).
p-298.example: If indoor na $22\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, outdoor na $0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and ventilation rate na $150\ \mathrm{m^3/h}$, di loss na $1200\times\frac{150}{3600}\times22\approx1100\ \mathrm{W}$. If $\eta=70\%$, e reduce to about $330\ \mathrm{W}$ and di supply air go be about $15.4\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
p-298.actionItem: Today, if you get energy recovery ventilator (ventilation unit), clean di filter according to di period for di manual.

p-299.title: One floor rug dey add one more layer of thermal resistance
p-299.summary: Rug dey add one more insulation layer between di floor and your feet. But for floor heating, thick rug go block di heat wey suppose come into di room, so use thin one.
p-299.principle: If di layers dey in series, di thermal resistance na $R=\sum\frac{L_i}{k_i}$ and di heat flow na $q=\frac{\Delta T}{R}$. If you add one more layer, $R$ increase and $q$ reduce.
p-299.example: Rug wey get thickness $1\ \mathrm{cm}$ and $k\approx0.05\ \mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$ na $R=0.2\ \mathrm{m^2K/W}$. If di floor na $R=0.5$ and $\Delta T=10\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, e be $q=20\to14.3\ \mathrm{W/m^2}$ and e reduce by about $29\%$.
p-299.actionItem: Today, spread rug for di cold floor spot wey you dey sit or stand often, and if di room get floor heating, choose thin rug.

p-300.title: If door sag, tighten di upper hinge screw first
p-300.summary: Di weight of di door dey pull di upper hinge and press di lower hinge, so di upper screw dey loosen first. Many times, if you tighten only di upper hinge screw, di sag go fix.
p-300.principle: Door wey dey still dey for torque balance $\sum\tau=0$. If weight $W$ act for di centre of di door ($\frac{w}{2}$ from di hinge), di horizontal force for hinge spacing $h$ na $F=\frac{W\,w/2}{h}$.
p-300.example: If door mass na $20\ \mathrm{kg}$ ($W\approx196\ \mathrm{N}$), width na $0.9\ \mathrm{m}$ and hinge spacing na $1.6\ \mathrm{m}$, $F=\frac{196\times0.45}{1.6}\approx55\ \mathrm{N}$ dey pull di upper hinge and press di lower one.
p-300.actionItem: Today, wit di door open, use Phillips screwdriver tighten di upper hinge screw, and if di hole dey spin freely, fill am with toothpick and wood glue and tighten again.

p-301.title: Lean your upper body forward first wen you dey stand up from chair
p-301.summary: For sitting position, di centre of gravity dey behind di feet, so you must lean your upper body forward to move di centre of gravity over di feet so you go stand up with less effort and more stably.
p-301.principle: For person to stand, di vertical projection of di centre of mass (COM) must dey inside di support area wey di feet make. If di centre dey $x$ horizontally from di feet, di torque wey gravity create na $\tau=mg\,x$.
p-301.example: If di COM for sitting position dey about $15\ \mathrm{cm}$ behind di feet, if you lean your upper body forward about $30^\circ$, di COM go come about $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ forward and most of di $x$ go disappear (approximate value).
p-301.actionItem: Today wen you dey stand up from chair, lean your nose toward di direction of your toes, pull your feet close to di chair, and then stand up. If dizziness dey repeat, talk to professional.

p-302.title: For winter night, di altitude of Polaris equal your latitude
p-302.summary: Polaris dey near di north celestial pole so im height dey almost equal di latitude of di observer. With one star you fit estimate di latitude of your position.
p-302.principle: Di altitude angle of di north celestial pole equal di observer latitude $\varphi$, and Polaris dey about $0.7^\circ$ from di pole so $h_{\mathrm{Polaris}}\approx\varphi$.
p-302.example: For Seoul (about $37.5^\circ$ N), Polaris dey about $37.5^\circ$ above di horizon, and for Jeju (about $33.5^\circ$ N) e dey about $33.5^\circ$. One fist with arm stretched na about $10^\circ$, so for Seoul e be about 3.75 fists high.
p-302.actionItem: Today for clear night, find Polaris with Big Dipper or di W of Cassiopeia and measure di height with your fist.

p-303.title: Why anti-reflective coating for glasses get bluish colour
p-303.summary: Anti-reflective coating na very thin film wey make di light wey reflect from di film cancel each other. E dey tuned to di middle green wavelength, so small blue and red side remain and give reflected colour.
p-303.principle: If film thickness $d$ na $\frac{\lambda}{4n}$, di path difference of di reflected waves from top and bottom surface go be $\frac{\lambda}{2}$ and dem go interfere destructively. Di ideal film refractive index na $n_c=\sqrt{n_s}$.
p-303.example: $\mathrm{MgF_2}$ ($n=1.38$) film for $\lambda=550\ \mathrm{nm}$ na $d=\frac{550}{4\times1.38}\approx100\ \mathrm{nm}$. Uncoated glass dey reflect about $4\%$ per surface, but if coated e go reduce to $1\%$ or below.
p-303.actionItem: Today, clean your glasses lenses with special cleaner and microfibre cloth, and avoid rubbing with dry cloth or using hot water.

p-304.title: If charging cable thin, charging go slow
p-304.summary: Thin wire get high resistance so voltage dey drop for di cable and dey leak as heat. Even for di same charger, thick cable dey carry more current.
p-304.principle: Voltage drop na $V=IR$, and di wire resistance na $R=\frac{\rho L}{A}$. Di power wey dey disappear as heat for di cable na $P=I^2R$.
p-304.example: If you use $2\ \mathrm{A}$ copper wire ($2\ \mathrm{m}$) for round trip for $\rho=1.7\times10^{-8}\ \Omega\mathrm{m}$ charging, cross-section $0.08\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ (28 AWG) na $R\approx0.42\ \Omega$ so $0.84\ \mathrm{V}$, $1.7\ \mathrm{W}$ loss. $0.2\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ (24 AWG) na $0.17\ \Omega$ so $0.34\ \mathrm{V}$, $0.7\ \mathrm{W}$.
p-304.actionItem: Today, if charging dey slow or di cable dey hot, change di thin cable to thick cable wey get rated current written on am.

p-305.title: Chest-type kimchi fridge dey lose less cold air wen you open di door
p-305.summary: Cold air dense so e dey sink down and gather. For chest-type wey you open from di top, di cold air dey stay inside di box so less dey escape even wen you open di door.
p-305.principle: Air density na $\rho=\frac{p}{R_sT}$ wey bigger as di temperature dey lower. Buoyancy wey density difference create na $\Delta\rho\,g\,V$, and cold air dey gather stably for di bottom.
p-305.example: $4\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ air na about $1.27\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$ and $25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ air na about $1.18\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, wey be about $7\%$ heavier. For side-door fridge, dis heavy cold air dey pour out through di open door.
p-305.actionItem: Today, decide before time wetin you wan take from kimchi fridge and open di lid short, one time.

p-306.title: Put wooden chopstick across pot wey dey boil over
p-306.summary: If di bubbles touch di chopstick and burst, di boil-over dey often delay. But na not complete solution, so to reduce di fire and dey watch am na di basic thing.
p-306.principle: Pressure difference of one bubble film na Laplace equation $\Delta p=\frac{2\gamma}{r}$ ($\gamma$: surface tension, $r$: radius of curvature). When di bubble film touch rough wooden surface, e go thin and burst easily.
p-306.example: For water wey get $100\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ $\gamma\approx0.059\ \mathrm{N/m}$, if bubble radius na $1\ \mathrm{mm}$, e be $\Delta p=\frac{2\times0.059}{0.001}\approx118\ \mathrm{Pa}$. Noodle and pasta water wey get plenty starch get tough bubble film.
p-306.actionItem: Today, when you dey boil noodles, put dry wooden chopstick across di pot mouth and use medium-low fire. Make sure say di chopstick no touch di fire.

p-307.title: Every 1m/s wey wind increase, di feels-like temperature dey drop about 1°C
p-307.summary: When wind blow, di warm air layer wey dey near your skin go comot, so e go feel colder even for di same air temperature. For winter, look wind together with temperature before you choose clothes.
p-307.principle: Heat loss from forced convection na $q=h(v)\,A\,(T_{\mathrm{skin}}-T_{\mathrm{air}})$ and as wind speed $v$ dey bigger, $h$ dey bigger. Wind chill index na $T_{wc}=13.12+0.6215T-11.37v^{0.16}+0.3965Tv^{0.16}$ ($v$: $\mathrm{km/h}$).
p-307.example: For air temperature $0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, wind speed $1.4\ \mathrm{m/s}$ ($5\ \mathrm{km/h}$) na about $-1.6\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $5\ \mathrm{m/s}$ ($18\ \mathrm{km/h}$) na about $-4.9\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, so with about $3.6\ \mathrm{m/s}$ increase in wind speed, e drop about $3.3\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
p-307.actionItem: Today, for windy day, cover your exposed skin with windbreaker outer wear and neck gaiter.

p-308.title: Halo around moon fit be sign of rain
p-308.summary: Moon halo na ring wey ice crystals for high cloud dey form by bending moonlight. Dis kind cloud dey show often when front dey come, so di chance of rain dey high, but e no sure.
p-308.principle: Minimum deviation angle of prism for hexagonal ice crystal na $D_{\min}=2\arcsin\left(n\sin30^\circ\right)-60^\circ$. If ice $n\approx1.31$ be $D_{\min}\approx22^\circ$, ring of $22^\circ$ go form round di moon.
p-308.example: For $n=1.31$, $\arcsin(0.655)\approx40.9^\circ$, so e be $D_{\min}\approx2\times40.9-60\approx21.8^\circ$. Di width of one hand span wey you stretch out arm na about $20^\circ$, so di ring from di moon na about one hand span.
p-308.actionItem: Tonight, if you see moon halo, check tomorrow weather forecast and carry umbrella.

p-309.title: 9H for tempered glass film na pencil hardness
p-309.summary: 9H mean say even if you scratch am with di hardest pencil, no mark go show, e no mean Mohs hardness 9. Sand dust inside pocket dey harder, so e fit scratch am.
p-309.principle: For surface to scratch, di particle must dey harder pass di surface $H_{\mathrm{particle}}>H_{\mathrm{surface}}$. Pencil hardness scale and Mohs hardness na different scales.
p-309.example: Quartz (main part of sand) get Mohs hardness $7$ and e dey harder pass glass (about $5.5\sim6$). Even if na 9H film, if e low pass Mohs hardness 7, sand dust fit scratch am.
p-309.actionItem: Today, keep your phone for different pocket from keys and coins, and shake out sand dust from your pocket.

p-310.title: For winter, open south-facing window curtain for day make sun come in
p-310.summary: For winter, even if sun low, south-facing window dey receive sunlight almost head-on and e dey gain plenty heat. To open curtain for day and close am when sun set na free heating.
p-310.principle: Solar heat gain of window na $Q=A\,I\,\mathrm{SHGC}\cos\theta$ ($I$: solar intensity, SHGC: solar heat gain coefficient, $\theta$: incidence angle). For winter, south-facing vertical window get small incidence angle, so transmission big.
p-310.example: For window $2\ \mathrm{m^2}$, vertical surface solar radiation $I\approx500\ \mathrm{W/m^2}$ for noon for clear day, if $\mathrm{SHGC}=0.6$, e be $600\ \mathrm{W}$. If you assume average $400\ \mathrm{W}$ for 4 hours, you go gain about $1.6\ \mathrm{kWh}$ (assumed value) of heat.
p-310.actionItem: Today, for clear day, open curtain and blinds for south-facing window, and close dem before sun set to reduce night heat loss.

p-311.title: Inner porch door na wind-blocking buffer space
p-311.summary: Di small space between front door and inner door dey act as buffer wey go stop cold air from entering house direct. Di key na say make you no open di two doors at di same time.
p-311.principle: Air exchange through open door dey happen by convection and heat loss na $Q=\rho cV\Delta T$ ($V$: volume of air wey dey exchange). Inner door dey limit di exchange volume to about di porch space.
p-311.example: If porch $3\ \mathrm{m^3}$ exchange with $20\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ difference, e be $Q=1.2\times1005\times3\times20\approx72\ \mathrm{kJ}\approx0.02\ \mathrm{kWh}$. If no inner door, $60\ \mathrm{m^3}$ living room go even dey affected, and di maximum na about $0.4\ \mathrm{kWh}$.
p-311.actionItem: Today, when you reach home, close di front door before you open di inner door, and when you dey go out, close di inner door before you open di front door.

p-312.title: If only di top of oven dey burn, na rack position cause am
p-312.summary: Di closer you dey to di top heater, di more di radiant heat dey increase sharply, so di top go burn first. If you lower di rack one level, di top and bottom go cook evenly.
p-312.principle: For point-source approximation, radiation intensity na $I=\frac{P}{4\pi r^2}$, wey dey inversely proportional to di square of distance. Real heater na surface source, so di change dey gentler than dis, but di closer, di stronger.
p-312.example: If simplified, rack wey be $5\ \mathrm{cm}$ distance from heater get radiation $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ times of $(10/5)^2=4$ rack. For real life, because na surface heater, e be about 2 to 3 times.
p-312.actionItem: Today, if di top dey burn first, lower di rack one level, and if need dey, loosely cover di top with foil.

p-313.title: Wearing two layers of socks reduce blister
p-313.summary: Blisters dey form from friction wey pull skin against sock, but with two layers, di friction dey happen between di sock layers so di skin dey pull less. If shoe tight, e go be di opposite effect, so leave room.
p-313.principle: Friction force na $F=\mu N$ and shear stress wey skin dey receive na $\tau=\frac{F}{A}$. If friction coefficient between layers small pass between skin and sock, sliding go happen between layers and skin stress go reduce.
p-313.example: If you assume say for one foot when you dey walk na $N\approx700\ \mathrm{N}$, contact area $A\approx100\ \mathrm{cm^2}$, when $\mu=0.5$, na $\tau\approx35\ \mathrm{kPa}$, and if between layers na $\mu=0.3$, e be $\tau\approx21\ \mathrm{kPa}$, reduction of about $40\%$ (assumed value).
p-313.actionItem: Today, if you go walk long, wear one extra layer on top thin sweat-wicking sock, and check say your shoe no tight.

p-314.title: Why snow photos dey come out grey and dark
p-314.summary: Camera auto exposure dey set di average of di scene to middle grey, so white snow dey come out grey. If you increase exposure, di snow go come out white.
p-314.principle: Auto exposure dey set average reflectance to $18\%$ grey. If snow reflectance na $\rho$, di correction wey you need na $\Delta\mathrm{EV}=\log_2\frac{\rho}{0.18}$.
p-314.example: If snow reflectance na $\rho\approx0.8$, e be $\Delta\mathrm{EV}=\log_2\frac{0.8}{0.18}\approx2.1$. So normally you dey apply $+1\sim+2\ \mathrm{EV}$ correction.
p-314.actionItem: Today, when you dey shoot snow scenery, tap di snow part for di screen and raise di brightness slider to $+1\sim+2$.

p-315.title: Choose folding umbrella wey get wind vent
p-315.summary: When wind push di umbrella surface hard, if di top fabric get vent for air to escape, pressure difference go reduce and e go flip less. No use any umbrella for strong wind.
p-315.principle: Drag na $F_D=\frac12\rho C_DAv^2$ and e dey proportional to square of wind speed. Vent structure dey reduce pressure difference so $C_D$ go low and di force go reduce by di same ratio.
p-315.example: If wind speed $15\ \mathrm{m/s}$, diameter $100\ \mathrm{cm}$ ($A\approx0.79\ \mathrm{m^2}$), $C_D=1.2$, e be $F_D\approx127\ \mathrm{N}$ (about $13\ \mathrm{kgf}$). If $C_D$ go down to $0.9$, e be about $95\ \mathrm{N}$ and $25\%$ reduce (assumed value).
p-315.actionItem: Today, when you dey choose umbrella, check for double canopy or vent structure and whether e get fibreglass ribs.

p-316.title: 1kW electric heater dey heat 1kW
p-316.summary: Electric heater dey change almost all di electricity wey e use to heat. So di electricity wey you need to get di same heat na just heat capacity multiplied by time.
p-316.principle: Efficiency of resistance heating na $100\%$ and energy consumed na $E=Pt$. Heat pump (air conditioner heating) get coefficient of performance $\mathrm{COP}=\frac{Q}{W}$ of about 3, so e dey make di same heat with $\frac13$ of electricity.
p-316.example: If you use $1\ \mathrm{kW}$ heater for 3 hours, e be $3\ \mathrm{kWh}$, and if you assume electricity price na $200$ won/kWh, e be $600$ won (about USD 0.45). Heat pump wey get $\mathrm{COP}=3$ for di same heat na $1\ \mathrm{kWh}$, about $200$ won.
p-316.actionItem: Today, when you dey use heater, check di rated capacity (W) and set timer to on am only for di time wey you need.

p-317.title: Lap blanket fit replace 1 to 2°C of heating temperature
p-317.summary: Felt temperature dey rise by di amount wey heat loss from di body reduce, so one lap blanket dey give di effect of raising room temperature by 1 to 2°C. Even if you lower heating small, you fit stay warm.
p-317.principle: Heat loss na $q=\frac{T_{\mathrm{skin}}-T_{\mathrm{air}}}{R_{\mathrm{clo}}+R_{\mathrm{air}}}$ and for sitting activity, clothing $1\ \mathrm{clo}$ ($0.155\ \mathrm{m^2K/W}$) dey lower comfortable temperature by about $5.5\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
p-317.example: If lap blanket na about $0.3\ \mathrm{clo}$, e dey lower comfort temperature by about $1.7\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. If you lower heating by $1\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, di estimate na say you go reduce heating bill by about $7\%$, so for $1.5\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ e be about $10\%$.
p-317.actionItem: Today, lower your living room heating setting by 1°C and put lap blanket for sofa.

p-318.title: Foil spark for microwave dey start from sharp tip
p-318.summary: For sharp corner of metal, electric field dey concentrate for one place and air dey break down and spark dey jump. No put foil, gold-rimmed bowl or metal decoration inside.
p-318.principle: For tip wey get small radius of curvature, electric field dey big as $E\approx\frac{V}{r}$. Air dey lose insulation at about $E_b\approx3\ \mathrm{MV/m}$ and corona or spark discharge go happen.
p-318.example: If you assume say foil corner tip radius $r=0.1\ \mathrm{mm}$ and induced voltage $V=300\ \mathrm{V}$, e be $E=\frac{300}{10^{-4}}=3\ \mathrm{MV/m}$, wey be insulation breakdown level (assumed value). Big flat foil dey less than tip but e still dangerous.
p-318.actionItem: Today, no put metal container, foil or gold-rimmed bowl inside microwave. If spark jump, stop am immediately and take am out after e cool.

p-319.title: Why you dey feel colder pass room temperature when you sit near cold window
p-319.summary: Body dey lose heat to surrounding cold surfaces through radiation, not just air. For window area, even if air be di same, di surface cold so e dey feel colder.
p-319.principle: Net radiant heat loss na $q=\varepsilon\sigma\left(T_{\mathrm{skin}}^4-T_s^4\right)\approx h_r\left(T_{\mathrm{skin}}-T_s\right)$ and near room temperature, $h_r\approx5\ \mathrm{W/(m^2\cdot K)}$.
p-319.example: If clothing surface $28\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, window surface $8\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, e be $q\approx5\times20=100\ \mathrm{W/m^2}$, and for wall wey surface na $18\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, e be $50\ \mathrm{W/m^2}$. If facing area na $0.5\ \mathrm{m^2}$, di difference na about $25\ \mathrm{W}$ (assumed value).
p-319.actionItem: Today, if you dey cold for window seat, move your chair about 1m from di window, or put curtain or insulating sheet.

p-320.title: For winter camping, pitch tent for ridge mid-slope instead of valley
p-320.summary: For clear and windless night, cold air dey sink and gather for valley and hollow places. Ridge top get strong wind, so flat mid-slope with less wind better.
p-320.principle: Cold air dey dense so e dey flow go low places with buoyancy acceleration $a\approx g\frac{\Delta T}{T}$ and form cold air pool. As altitude rise, temperature dey drop by average of $0.65\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}/100\ \mathrm{m}$, but for night inversion e go be di opposite.
p-320.example: If $\Delta T=5\ \mathrm{K}$, $T=278\ \mathrm{K}$, e be $a\approx9.8\times\frac{5}{278}\approx0.18\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. For clear, low-wind winter night, valley bottom fit be several $^\circ\mathrm{C}$ colder pass mid-slope.
p-320.actionItem: Today, if you get camping plan, avoid hollows inside designated campsite and choose flat place wey get less wind.

p-321.title: Radiant and convection electric heaters different
p-321.summary: Radiant heater dey directly warm people and objects so e warm immediately, while convection heater dey warm di air and slowly warm di whole room. Choose according to di space wey you dey use.
p-321.principle: Radiation dey transfer heat to surfaces through $q=\varepsilon\sigma(T_h^4-T_s^4)A$ without passing through air, and convection dey move heat through warmed air circulation by $q=hA\,\Delta T$.
p-321.example: 1kW radiant heater go warm skin 1m in front as soon as you on am, but convection heater need $Q=mc\Delta T\approx0.18\ \mathrm{MJ}$ just to raise di air for 30m³ room (about 36kg of air) by 5°C, and e go take much longer to warm walls and furniture.
p-321.actionItem: Today, if you plan to buy heater, decide di use first: radiant for one spot like desk, convection for di whole room.

p-322.title: For electric car in winter, use heated seat instead of air heating
p-322.summary: Heater wey warm cabin air dey use battery well for electric car, so if you use heated seat and steering wheel to warm your body direct and lower cabin setting, you fit protect your range.
p-322.principle: If you heat by contact with di body direct, di heat wey you need to warm dey much smaller. Heating air na $Q=mc\Delta T$ and you must continue to replace di loss wey dey leak through di body and glass.
p-322.example: If you lower setting and use about 60W heated seat instead of about 3kW cabin heater, you fit save about 1.4kWh per hour, and for 6km/kWh car, na about 8km range.
p-322.actionItem: Today, when you dey drive, on di heated seat and steering wheel first and lower di cabin temperature setting by 1 to 2°C.

p-323.title: Winter heater na engine waste heat so e almost free
p-323.summary: Heater for combustion engine car dey use engine waste heat wey gather for coolant, so even if you on am, fuel no go increase much. Na di air conditioner (A/C) compressor dey use fuel.
p-323.principle: About 60% of fuel energy dey waste as heat ($Q_\mathrm{waste}\approx 0.6\,Q_\mathrm{fuel}$), and di heater core dey send part of am inside di cabin. A/C compressor dey take extra work $W$ from di engine.
p-323.example: Di heat wey heater dey use na about 2 to 4kW, wey be small part of engine waste heat while cruising, but A/C compressor dey take about 1 to 3kW more from engine output.
p-323.actionItem: If no fogging dey, today during winter driving, off di A/C button and use only di heater.

p-324.title: Ketchup bottle: no shake am, hit am upside down hard
p-324.summary: Ketchup dey hold like solid when you leave am still, but e dey suddenly thin when force dey apply. Hold di bottle upside down and hit di bottom once hard to apply sudden force.
p-324.principle: Ketchup na shear-thinning non-Newtonian fluid. As shear rate $\dot\gamma$ dey increase, apparent viscosity $\eta=\tau/\dot\gamma$ dey reduce and e go flow when e pass yield stress.
p-324.example: For still state, viscosity na about 50Pa·s or more, but under strong shear e fit drop many tens of times or more. E still dey much thicker than water (about 0.001Pa·s).
p-324.actionItem: Today, hold ketchup bottle upside down and hit di bottom near di neck once hard with your palm.

p-325.title: Set treadmill incline to 1% to match outdoor
p-325.summary: Treadmill no get air resistance, so even for di same speed, e dey easier pass outdoors. If you raise di incline to 1%, dis difference dey mostly compensate.
p-325.principle: Di work wey air resistance dey do, e dey replace am with potential energy of incline: $P=mgv\sin\theta\approx mgv\times(\text{slope})$.
p-325.example: For 70kg body weight wey dey run 10km/h (about 2.78m/s), 1% incline na extra power of $70\times9.81\times2.78\times0.01\approx19\ \mathrm{W}$.
p-325.actionItem: Today, if you dey use treadmill, set di incline to 1% and run.

p-326.title: For photos through bus or train window, press lens against glass
p-326.summary: Reflection of indoor light for car window wey show for photo go reduce well if you put di lens close to di glass. E go better if you cover di area round di lens with hand or hood.
p-326.principle: Glass surface reflection na Fresnel reflection of about 4% for one surface ($R=\left(\frac{n-1}{n+1}\right)^2,\ n\approx1.5$), and if you press di lens against am, di angle wey reflected light dey enter di lens go reduce.
p-326.example: Because about 4% dey reflect from each of di two glass surfaces, total about 8% of indoor light dey show for di window. For day wey outside dark, dis ratio dey much more noticeable for di photo.
p-326.actionItem: Today, when you dey shoot outside di window, lightly touch di lens to di glass and block surrounding light with one hand. But no press hard for place wey get big vibration.

p-327.title: Check earphone impedance (Ω) for compatibility with phone
p-327.summary: For device wey get low output voltage like smartphone, low-impedance earphone dey louder. High-impedance one get small output for di same voltage.
p-327.principle: Power wey earphone receive na $P=\frac{V^2}{R}$, so for di same voltage $V$, di bigger di impedance $R$, di smaller di $P$.
p-327.example: For voltage 0.5V (rms), 16Ω earphone na about 15.6mW, 300Ω earphone na about 0.83mW, so di difference na about 19 times.
p-327.actionItem: Today, check impedance for earphone spec table, and if you go plug am direct inside phone, choose 16 to 32Ω product.

p-328.title: 1kWh na 3.6MJ, about 860kcal
p-328.summary: kWh for electricity bill, kcal for food, and joule (J) for science na all energy units and dem dey convert exactly to each other.
p-328.example: 2,000kcal per day na about 8.4MJ, wey be about 2.3kWh, and average na about 97W. 1kWh fit make 100W bulb dey on for 10 hours.
p-328.actionItem: Today, check how much (kWh) you use dis month for your electricity bill or app.

p-329.title: Every time you open oven door, temperature dey drop 25°C
p-329.summary: When you open oven door once, hot air dey comot and cold air dey enter, so di inside temperature go drop noticeably, and energy go need to raise am again.
p-329.principle: When you open di door, air dey exchange through convection from temperature difference, and heat of $Q=C\Delta T$ must enter again to recover. Di walls dey hold heat, so di size of di drop dey different for each oven.
p-329.example: E dey commonly known say 180°C oven fit drop about 20 to 30°C when you open di door once, and recovery dey take few minutes. Cooking time go extend and e go use more electricity.
p-329.actionItem: Today, during oven cooking, no open di door, check di state through di oven window and light.

p-330.title: Spin am to know raw egg from boiled egg
p-330.summary: If you spin egg for table, boiled egg go spin smoothly for long time, and raw egg go wobble and stop quickly.
p-330.principle: Boiled egg na one rigid body, so e dey spin steadily with $L=I\omega$. For raw egg, di liquid inside dey move separately from di shell so energy dey scatter, and even after e stop, di liquid still dey turn so e go spin small again.
p-330.example: When you spin egg wey weigh about 60g, boiled egg go spin steadily for few seconds, and raw egg usually go stop noticeably earlier. If you stop am with hand for a moment and release, only raw egg go move small again.
p-330.actionItem: Today, spin two eggs from fridge for table and check which one dey spin smoothly.

p-331.title: Cough into sleeve or elbow, droplets fit fly many metres
p-331.summary: Cough and sneeze dey make fast air flow wey dey send droplets many metres. If you cover with di inside of elbow or sleeve, di distance wey dem go spread go reduce well.
p-331.principle: Di jet wey dey comot from di mouth get momentum $p=mv$ and e dey spread forward, speed dey slow down gradually, and e go diffuse inside di air.
p-331.example: Di initial speed of cough airflow dem report say e be about 10m per second, and small particles fit float for air and affect up to many metres.
p-331.actionItem: Today, if you cough, cover your mouth and nose with di inside of your elbow or sleeve instead of your hand.

p-332.title: Choose ski goggle lens colour according to weather
p-332.summary: For clear day, use dark lens to reduce glare, and for cloudy or snowy day, use yellow or orange lens to improve contrast of bumps.
p-332.principle: Lens get different transmittance by wavelength and brightness dey decided by visible light transmittance $\mathrm{VLT}=I/I_0$. Yellow and orange dey filter blue light and increase contrast for cloudy day.
p-332.example: For clear day, dark grey or mirror lens wey get VLT about 10 to 20% dey common choice, and for cloudy day, yellow or rose lens wey get VLT about 40 to 60%.
p-332.actionItem: Today, when you dey pack ski goggles, look weather forecast and decide lens colour (or replacement lens).

p-333.title: Put speaker at least 20cm from wall
p-333.summary: If you put speaker too close to wall, bass go swell and some sounds go disappear, so di sound go dull and blur.
p-333.principle: Near wall, bass dey louder because of boundary effect (about 3 to 6dB), and sound dey reduce for frequency $f=\frac{c}{4d}$ wey wall reflection dey opposite phase from direct sound.
p-333.example: If di distance from wall na 20cm, about $f=\frac{343}{4\times0.2}\approx430\ \mathrm{Hz}$ go reduce, and if 50cm, about 170Hz go reduce, so di bass range dey change. E depend on di room.
p-333.actionItem: Today, move your speaker at least 20cm from di wall and listen to di same song again.

p-334.title: Car inverter dey get big current for 12V
p-334.summary: If you connect high-power device like laptop charger to inverter for car, di current for 12V side go big well, and di socket fuse fit blow.
p-334.principle: Power na $P=VI$, so for di same power, di lower di voltage, di bigger di current $I=P/V$.
p-334.example: 150W device na $150/12=12.5\ \mathrm{A}$ in theory, and if you consider 90% inverter efficiency, e be about 13.9A, wey near di limit of common 10 to 15A socket fuse.
p-334.actionItem: Today, check di car socket fuse capacity (A) and divide di power consumption of di device wey you wan connect by 12V.

p-335.title: Oven preheat energy na fixed cost, so bake everything together
p-335.summary: Every time you on oven, di energy wey preheat dey use na di same no matter how much you bake. If you bake many things at once, di number of preheats go reduce.
p-335.principle: Heat wey preheat dey use dey decided by di oven heat capacity and temperature rise: $Q=C_\mathrm{oven}\Delta T$. E no depend on di amount of food.
p-335.example: To preheat electric oven to 180°C need about 0.3 to 0.4kWh, and if you bake once instead of twice, you fit save about 70 won (about 0.05 dollar).
p-335.actionItem: Today, if you go use oven, gather everything wey you wan bake together and bake dem together for two racks.

p-336.title: Find stud for wall by knocking sound
p-336.summary: If you knock plasterboard wall with finger, hollow place go give low resonant sound, and on top stud (frame) e go give hard and high sound.
p-336.principle: Di knocked surface dey vibrate and e dey give resonance frequency $f\propto\sqrt{k/m}$, but on top frame, stiffness $k$ dey big so di sound dey higher and shorter.
p-336.example: Studs dey normally 400 to 600mm apart, so if you move along di wall about 10cm at a time and knock, di positions wey sound change go appear regularly.
p-336.actionItem: Today, before you hammer nail, knock di wall to find stud, and check whether wiring or pipes dey pass.

p-337.title: Sauna 80°C you fit endure, but 80°C water you no fit
