c-361.summary: If you use very small baking soda for tough meat, di pH go rise and e go hold water better so e go soften.
c-361.principle: Muscle fibre protein dey hold water least near isoelectric point (pH about 5 to 5.5). If you raise di meat pH (about 5.5 to 5.7) with baking soda, di negative charge of di protein go increase and dem go repel each other and hold more water. $\mathrm{NaHCO_3 \rightleftharpoons Na^+ + HCO_3^-}$
c-361.example: Mix about 2.5g (0.5%) baking soda with 450g sliced meat for 15 minutes and rinse am. If you use plenty, e go taste like soap and di tissue go turn soft.
c-361.actionItem: Today if di meat for stir-fry tough, coat am with 0.5% or less baking soda for only 15 minutes, rinse am clean and cook am.

c-362.title: Sometimes milk dey curdle when you put am inside hot coffee
c-362.summary: Milk dey curdle for coffee because acid and heat dey make di protein clump, and if di milk fresh e normally no dey harmful.
c-362.principle: Isoelectric point of milk casein na about pH 4.6, so as pH come close to dis, di charge go reduce and dem go clump together. Heat dey make dis clumping faster.
c-362.example: Milk pH na about 6.7 and coffee na about 4.8 to 5.1. Old milk dey already get lower pH so e dey clump more easily, and if e smell sour, no drink am, throw am away.
c-362.actionItem: Today for coffee with milk, pour milk first for di cup or use warmed milk, and if e smell sour, throw am away.

c-363.title: E dey dangerous to breathe helium balloon gas
c-363.summary: If you breathe helium, your voice go change but e dey push oxygen out and you fit suffocate, so e dey dangerous.
c-363.principle: Oxygen partial pressure for di air wey you dey breathe na $P_{\mathrm{O_2}} = F_{\mathrm{O_2}} \times P$. Pure helium get $F_{\mathrm{O_2}} = 0$ so e dey push oxygen out of di lungs. Speed of sound na $v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma RT}{M}}$, and for helium e dey much faster so your voice go high.
c-363.example: Oxygen for air na 20.9% but helium 100% get 0%. Speed of sound for helium na about 1,007m/s, about 3 times of air (about 343m/s), and if you breathe am directly from compressed tank, lung damage fit happen.
c-363.actionItem: Today when you dey blow balloons, no breathe helium, and ventilate for closed room.

c-364.title: No give high-speed film to airport X-ray for film camera
c-364.summary: Airport X-ray fit make foggy blur for film, so for high-speed film e safer to ask for hand inspection.
c-364.principle: When silver halide crystal receive light or X-ray photon, silver atoms go form as latent image. $\mathrm{AgBr + h\nu \to Ag + Br}$ Exposure dey accumulate.
c-364.example: Film wey get speed of ISO 800 or more fit blur if e pass through many scans, and X-ray for checked baggage strong pass. Exposure dey add up so e good to reduce di number of scans during travel.
c-364.actionItem: Today, put di film inside transparent bag separately and ask for manual inspection for security check, and no put am inside checked baggage.

c-365.title: Use EDP and EDT concentration to judge perfume lasting time and price
c-365.summary: For perfume, look di fragrance concentration (%) instead of di name to judge how long e go last and di price.
c-365.principle: Di higher di fragrance concentration, di slower e dey evaporate and di longer e dey remain. Eau de parfum (EDP) na about 15 to 20%, eau de toilette (EDT) about 5 to 15%, and eau de cologne (EDC) about 2 to 4%.
c-365.example: For 50mL bottle, EDP 15% get about 7.5mL fragrance and EDT 8% get about 4mL, so EDP usually cost more. Lasting time na usually about 3 to 4 hours for EDT and about 5 to 8 hours for EDP.
c-365.actionItem: Before you buy perfume, spray am for di inside of your arm instead of wrist and check di smell even after 4 hours.

c-366.title: Aerogel for winter insoles and gloves na silica wey be almost air
c-366.summary: Aerogel for winter gear na silica structure wey almost all na air, so even if e thin, e dey block heat well.
c-366.principle: Nano-size holes small pass di mean free path of air molecules (about 68nm) so heat transfer dey block. $\lambda = \frac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2}\,\pi d^2 P}$ Heat flow na $Q = \frac{kA\,\Delta T}{L}$.
c-366.example: Thermal conductivity of silica aerogel na about 0.015 to 0.02W/m·K, lower than still air (about 0.026). For area 0.02m², thickness 3mm and temperature difference 20K, if $k = 0.02$, heat loss na about 2.7W.
c-366.actionItem: Today, check di real aerogel content and thickness of your winter insoles and gloves, and use dem dry because if dem wet, insulation go drop.

20261119-math-g03-1.title: Different Ways to Share 72 Candies Equally Between Plates
20261119-math-g03-1.summary: You wan put 72 candies on plates and share dem equally with nothing left. The number of candies on each plate change depending on how many plates you use.
20261119-math-g03-1.principle: You fit share the candies equally with nothing left only when number of plates times number of candies on one plate equal 72. 4×18, 6×12, and 9×8 na 72, and no number wey you multiply by 5 or 7 go make 72.
20261119-math-g03-1.example: For each number of plates, divide 72 by that number and check whether remainder dey.
20261119-math-g03-1.actionItem: Find several ways wey meet the conditions together (the range for number of plates and candies on each plate), and explain how number of plates and candies on one plate pair together.

20261119-math-g07-1.title: Does higher frequency mean dem do better?
20261119-math-g07-1.summary:
Class 1 (20 students) and Class 2 (50 students) sit same math test. Frequency table group scores into 3 ranges, like this:
Interval / Class 1 (20 students) / Class 2 (50 students)
Below 60 points / 2 students / 10 students
60 points or more but below 80 points / 10 students / 25 students
80 points or more / 8 students / 15 students
Minji talk, "More students get 80 points or more in Class 2, na 15, so Class 2 do better for the test."
20261119-math-g07-1.principle: By proportion, for 80 points or more, Class 1 get 8/20=40% and Class 2 get 15/50=30%, so Class 1 higher; for below 60, Class 1 get 2/20=10%, Class 2 get 10/50=20%, so Class 2 rate 2 times Class 1. You no fit know mean from grouped table, and conclusion comparing only student counts no get strong support.
20261119-math-g07-1.example: For each class, divide student number in each range by total students in that class.
20261119-math-g07-1.actionItem: Learn problem with comparing raw frequencies when two classes get different student counts, and separate wetin table tell you for sure from wetin e no tell.

20261125-physics-g11-2.title: Newton's laws of motion and special relativity
20261125-physics-g11-2.summary: For horizontal surface wey no get friction, dem put object A wey get mass 3 kg and object B wey get mass 2 kg touch each other, and dem push am with horizontal force of 20 N for di A side. Wetin be di acceleration of di two objects and di size of di force wey A dey push B with?
20261125-physics-g11-2.principle: Di acceleration of di whole system na $a = \frac{F}{m_A + m_B} = \frac{20\text{ N}}{5\text{ kg}} = 4\text{ m/s}^2$. Di net force wey dey accelerate object B na only di contact force wey A dey push B with, so e be $F_{AB} = m_B \cdot a = 2\text{ kg} \times 4\text{ m/s}^2 = 8\text{ N}$.
20261125-physics-g11-2.example: Whole system (A+B): F = (m<sub>A</sub> + m<sub>B</sub>) a → 20 = (3 + 2) a

20261125-physics-g12-1.principle: Wave theory predict say energy go accumulate over time, but for photoelectric effect, one single photon wey get frequency above di threshold frequency dey collide with electron immediately and transfer energy, so electron dey release immediately without time delay.

20261123-chemistry-g11-1.title: Mole

20261123-chemistry-g11-2.title: Mole

20261123-chemistry-g12-2.title: Reaction rate, Le Chatelier's principle and chemical cells
20261123-chemistry-g12-2.summary: For di reaction 2NO(g) + O₂(g) → 2NO₂(g), dem do initial rate method. Wen dem keep [O₂] constant and double [NO], di rate become 4 times, and wen dem keep [NO] constant and double [O₂], di rate become 2 times. Wetin be di rate law and di overall reaction order of dis reaction?
20261123-chemistry-g12-2.principle: Because $[\text{NO}]$ become $2$ times and di rate become $4$ times, $m=2$, and because $[\text{O}_2]$ become $2$ times and di rate become $2$ times, $n=1$. Di rate law na $v = k[\text{NO}]^2[\text{O}_2]$, and di overall reaction order na $2 + 1 = 3$.

20261124-chemistry-g11-1.title: Mole
20261124-chemistry-g11-1.summary: For 0℃ and 1 atm, wetin be di number of moles of methane molecules and di total number of moles of hydrogen (H) atoms inside 11.2 L of methane gas (CH₄, molecular mass 16)?
20261124-chemistry-g11-1.principle: Di number of moles of methane na $n = \frac{11.2\text{ L}}{22.4\text{ L/mol}} = 0.5\text{ mol}$. Because each $1$ methane molecule get $4$ hydrogen atoms, di total moles of hydrogen atoms na $0.5 \times 4 = 2.0\text{ mol}$.
20261124-chemistry-g11-1.example: For 0℃ and 1 atm, 1 mol of gas = 22.4 L.
20261124-chemistry-g11-1.actionItem: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.

20261124-chemistry-g11-2.title: Mole
20261124-chemistry-g11-2.summary: If you wan prepare 500 mL of 0.1 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH, formula mass 40) standard solution, wetin be di mass of pure solid NaOH wey you need?
20261124-chemistry-g11-2.principle: Di number of moles of $\text{NaOH}$ wey dem need na $n = M \times V = 0.1\text{ mol/L} \times 0.5\text{ L} = 0.05\text{ mol}$. Di mass wey dem need na $w = n \times M_w = 0.05\text{ mol} \times 40\text{ g/mol} = 2.0\text{ g}$.
20261124-chemistry-g11-2.example: Molarity M = number of moles (mol) / volume of solution (L)
20261124-chemistry-g11-2.actionItem: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.

20261124-chemistry-g12-1.summary: Which one be di correct description of di change wey happen wen dem add 'positive catalyst' to chemical reaction?

20261124-chemistry-g12-2.title: Reaction rate, Le Chatelier's principle and chemical cells

20261125-chemistry-g07-2.principle: According to Boyle's law, for constant temperature, $P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$ dey hold. $1\text{ atm} \times 60\text{ mL} = 3\text{ atm} \times V_2 \implies V_2 = 20\text{ mL}$ .

20261122-english-g04-1.title: Mama note and Jisu playtime

3:30 p.m. Come home.
4:00 p.m. Piano class (30 minutes).
5:00 p.m. Throw away di trash.
6:30 p.m. Dinner with Mama and Papa.

20261122-english-g04-1.principle: Piano class na 4:00-4:30, so 4:15-4:30 overlap, and throwing away trash for 5:00 fall inside 4:15-5:15. Coming home for 3:30 and dinner for 6:30 dey outside di park time.

20261122-english-g04-2.title: Decide dog-walking and homework times

- Do your homework for 60 minutes.

- No do both at di same time.

20261122-english-g05-2.title: 'Most popular'—text get evidence for am?
20261122-english-g05-2.summary:

Mina talk, 'Animal books na the most popular for our class.'

20261122-english-g09-1.title: The hidden assumption inside 'we sold 200 fewer lunches'

"This month, the cafeteria sold 200 fewer lunches than last month. So students did not like the new menu."

20261122-english-g10-1.title: How we go report 2 conflicting school newsletter announcements?
20261122-english-g10-1.summary:
You dey school English newsletter editorial team. Two festival notices disagree.

School notice: 'Festival: Friday, 4 p.m., in gym. Free for all students.'
Student council poster: 'Festival: Friday, 5 p.m., in gym. Tickets: 1,000 won.'

You never confirm which one correct.
20261122-english-g10-1.principle: If no confirm yet, fairly state wetin both sources say and say dem still dey check. Choosing one side as fact or telling people no come without information go mislead.
20261122-english-g10-1.example: Compare information each announcement give and wetin e leave out.
20261122-english-g10-1.actionItem: Write for student readers fair account of 2 different notices; say wetin not confirmed and wetin readers should do.

20261122-english-g10-2.title: One case enough to claim 'always'?
20261122-english-g10-2.summary:
This na part of text from school newspaper (line numbers start at 1).
1) Our school suppose ban phones from building.
2) Last month, Mina get new phone, and her math score drop from 90 to 75.
3) So phone clearly make every student's grade worse.
4) Also phone dey make noise in hallway, and some students check answers during tests.
5) So school suppose ban dem for everybody.
20261122-english-g10-2.principle: Line 3 na problem. Saying grades 'surely' worsen for 'all students' from only one student's score drop (line 2) claim pass evidence. Score fit drop for other reason, like test difficulty or situation. Line 4 get separate reason (noise, cheating), so judge am separately. Line 5 'ban for everybody' depend on this too, but first problem show for line 3.
20261122-english-g10-2.example: For each line separate 'wetin report' from 'wetin conclude'.
20261122-english-g10-2.actionItem: For argumentative text, find line where evidence no support claim enough; rewrite it more carefully and decide what more evidence need.

20261122-english-g11-1.title: Unclear work instruction: wetin you ask first?

Hi Jiho,
Please send sales summary to client before meeting.
Thanks,
Ms. Han

Jiho knows: team calendar show Aurora Co. meeting Tuesday at 10:00 and Blue Pine Ltd. Thursday at 14:00. Shared folder has separate July, August and September sales files.

20261122-english-g11-1.example: Check whether 'to who', 'which file' and 'by when' each point to one clear thing in email.
20261122-english-g11-1.actionItem: From vague work email, choose info you must confirm before action; write question email easy to answer.

20261122-english-g11-2.title: Na reading club cause am? What info go show us?

20261122-english-g11-2.actionItem: Choose information needed to tell whether score gap between club members and nonmembers na club effect; write English question to get am.

20261122-english-g12-1.title: Students wey eat breakfast get higher grades: wetin else we need know?

This na claim in school article: 'Students wey eat breakfast get higher test scores, so school suppose provide free breakfast.' Evidence na survey of 200 students:

Group | Number of students | Average score
Students wey eat breakfast | 130 | 82
Students wey skip breakfast | 70 | 74
20261122-english-g12-1.principle: b check other causes (sleep, study time), c checks actual intervention result, e checks fairness of comparison. a and d no be evidence whether breakfast raise scores.

20261122-english-g12-2.actionItem: As details increase, revise judgment how headline tone and omissions tilt from facts; explain one thing in English.

20261123-english-g01-1.title: Find the actions wey no follow the pool notice rules.

Pool Rules
1. No running.
2. Swim caps on, please.
3. Under 8? Come with a grown-up.

(grown-up = adult)

Four people wan go pool.
Mina na 7. She come with her mama and get cap.
Jun na 10. E come alone and no get cap.
Tom na 6. E come with e brother. E brother na 9. Tom get cap.

20261123-english-g01-1.principle: Jun no get cap, so e break rule 2. Tom under 8, but e brother wey come with am na 9, so e no be 'grown-up', and Tom break rule 3. Mina come with her mama, and Sue na 11, so e okay for her to waka and come alone.

20261123-english-g10-1.title: How we go report 2 conflicting school newsletter announcements?
20261123-english-g10-1.summary:
You dey school English newsletter editorial team. Two festival notices disagree.

School notice: 'Festival: Friday, 4 p.m., in gym. Free for all students.'
Student council poster: 'Festival: Friday, 5 p.m., in gym. Tickets: 1,000 won.'

You never confirm which one correct.
20261123-english-g10-1.principle: If no confirm yet, fairly state wetin both sources say and say dem still dey check. Choosing one side as fact or telling people no come without information go mislead.
20261123-english-g10-1.example: Compare information each announcement give and wetin e leave out.
20261123-english-g10-1.actionItem: Write for student readers fair account of 2 different notices; say wetin not confirmed and wetin readers should do.

20261123-english-g10-2.title: One case enough to claim 'always'?
20261123-english-g10-2.summary:
This na part of text from school newspaper (line numbers start at 1).
1) Our school suppose ban phones from building.
2) Last month, Mina get new phone, and her math score drop from 90 to 75.
3) So phone clearly make every student's grade worse.
4) Also phone dey make noise in hallway, and some students check answers during tests.
5) So school suppose ban dem for everybody.
20261123-english-g10-2.principle: Line 3 na problem. Saying grades 'surely' worsen for 'all students' from only one student's score drop (line 2) claim pass evidence. Score fit drop for other reason, like test difficulty or situation. Line 4 get separate reason (noise, cheating), so judge am separately. Line 5 'ban for everybody' depend on this too, but first problem show for line 3.
20261123-english-g10-2.example: For each line separate 'wetin report' from 'wetin conclude'.
20261123-english-g10-2.actionItem: For argumentative text, find line where evidence no support claim enough; rewrite it more carefully and decide what more evidence need.

20261124-english-g03-2.title: Show 'worry' without saying am

3:30 p.m. Come home.

5:00 p.m. Throw away di trash.
6:30 p.m. Dinner with Mama and Papa.

20261124-english-g04-2.title: Decide dog-walking and homework times
20261124-english-g04-2.summary:
Note wey Dad leave (na text only, no picture):

Mina,
You dey come home for 4:00 p.m. I dey come home for 6:30 p.m.
- Walk di dog for 30 minutes. No do am before 5:00 p.m. E too hot.
- Do your homework for 60 minutes.

- Finish both before I come home.
- No do both at di same time.

20261125-english-g01-2.title: Correct the wrong line in copied lost-and-found notice
20261125-english-g01-2.summary:
Notice for school board (words only):

Lost and Found
Found: a blue water bottle, near Room 3.
Ask Ms. Park in Room 1 after school.

Your friend Jia see the notice because she dey find her water bottle, and send message to Hana. Hana wan compare am with the notice.
20261125-english-g01-2.principle: Line 4 wrong. The notice say Ms. Park dey Room 1, but the message say Room 3, so e wrong. Blue for line 2 match the notice, and Room 3 for line 3 na where dem find the bottle, so e correct.
20261125-english-g01-2.example: Point to the words in the notice (colour, room number, person's name) one by one and match dem with the message lines.
20261125-english-g01-2.actionItem: Compare the lost-and-found notice with the message wey friend copy am line by line, find the wrong line, and correct am.

20261125-english-g02-1.title: Where dem talk 'Two tickets, please.'? Judge whether information plenty
20261125-english-g02-1.summary:
You hear wetin one man and ticket seller talk. Dem no talk where dem dey.

Man: Two tickets, please.
Seller: Here you are. Di show start for 7:00.
20261125-english-g02-1.principle: Ticket and show na words wey dem use for many places, like cinema or concert hall. E hard to choose one from only two lines.
20261125-english-g02-1.example: Think of two or three places wey people fit talk these two lines.
20261125-english-g02-1.actionItem: Judge whether you fit know di place from only two lines wey you hear, and choose extra clue wey go separate di places.

20261125-english-g02-2.title: Which answer fit teacher greeting? Think about where politeness get limit
20261125-english-g02-2.summary:
Teacher talk for morning, "How are you today, Mina?"

Your friend Jin talk say, "For English, e always better to talk politely. You fit just talk that way to everybody."
20261125-english-g02-2.principle: b and d answer di greeting and ask di other person too, so dem fit teacher. a too casual and c sound rude.
20261125-english-g02-2.example: Check separately whether di answer match di question and whether e suit teacher.
20261125-english-g02-2.actionItem: Choose answer wey fit di teacher greeting, and talk about one case wey di claim 'polite talk always better' no work.

20261125-english-g03-1.title: Find reading time inside Mina Saturday schedule
20261125-english-g03-1.summary:
Mina Saturday schedule (text only, no picture):

10 a.m.: My free time fit start.
12 p.m. - 1 p.m.: Lunch
1 p.m. - 2 p.m.: Dance class
5 p.m.: Dinner. I must finish before dinner.

Mina want read book for 1 hour. She start on the hour and finish on the hour.
20261125-english-g03-1.principle: Free time start at 10 a.m.; from 12 to 14 lunch and dance class fill the time. Schedule get no activity from 15 to 16 or 16 to 17, and dem finish before dinner.
20261125-english-g03-1.example: Change schedule times to 24-hour numbers and draw time line.
20261125-english-g03-1.actionItem: Think of different reading start times wey meet all schedule conditions, and explain why other times no work.

20261125-english-g03-2.title: Show 'worry' without saying am
20261125-english-g03-2.summary: You go write scene where your friend Mina dey worry during test. Text wey directly name feeling and text wey show am through actions reach reader in different ways.
20261125-english-g03-2.principle: Cold hands and checking clock again and again make reader guess nervousness. Yawning while looking out window suggest boredom; smiling while writing fast suggest ease or confidence.
20261125-english-g03-2.example: From each text, pick and write Mina action or body change.
20261125-english-g03-2.actionItem: Write short text where reader fit guess feeling only from actions and body clues, without any feeling word.

20261125-english-g04-1.title: Mama note and Jisu playtime
20261125-english-g04-1.summary:
Note wey Mama leave for table (na text only, no picture):

Mina,
Today's plan:
3:30 p.m. Come home.
4:00 p.m. Piano class (30 minutes).
5:00 p.m. Throw away di trash.
6:30 p.m. Dinner with Mama and Papa.

Then her friend Jisu send message. "Make we play for park from 4:15 to 5:15 today!"
20261125-english-g04-1.principle: Piano class na 4:00-4:30, so 4:15-4:30 overlap, and throwing away trash for 5:00 fall inside 4:15-5:15. Coming home for 3:30 and dinner for 6:30 dey outside di park time.
20261125-english-g04-1.example: Put each line beside di park time '4:15-5:15' one by one, and check whether e finish before or start after.
20261125-english-g04-1.actionItem: Compare di different plans for Mama note with di time wey friend suggest, find where dem no fit together, then say no for English and suggest another time.

20261125-english-g04-2.title: Decide dog-walking and homework times
20261125-english-g04-2.summary:
Note wey Dad leave (na text only, no picture):

Mina,
You dey come home for 4:00 p.m. I dey come home for 6:30 p.m.
- Walk di dog for 30 minutes. No do am before 5:00 p.m. E too hot.
- Do your homework for 60 minutes.

- Finish both before I come home.
- No do both at di same time.
For down, write each time as 'how many minutes after 4:00 p.m.'. For example, if you start for 4:30, write 30, and if you start for 5:15, write 75.
20261125-english-g04-2.principle: Homework na 5:00-6:00 and di walk na 5:30-6:00, so both tasks overlap from 5:30 to 6:00. Di walk start after 5:00 and both finish before 6:30, so dem keep di other conditions.
20261125-english-g04-2.example: Add di time wey each task take (in minutes) to di task start time to find di finish time.
20261125-english-g04-2.actionItem: Make some different combinations of dog-walking time and homework time wey meet all di conditions for Dad note.

20261125-english-g05-1.title: Your thinking change as you read poster
20261125-english-g05-1.summary: Jun no be member of Green Library. Friend Ara na member. Both go read poster in front of library one line at a time.
20261125-english-g05-1.principle: Each time poster info appear step by step, update your judgment and make English question to check information wey poster no give.
20261125-english-g05-1.example: Check whether the new sentence change your earlier judgment.
20261125-english-g05-1.actionItem: Each time poster info appear step by step, update your judgment and make English question to check information wey poster no give.

20261125-english-g05-2.title: 'Most popular'—text get evidence for am?
20261125-english-g05-2.summary:
Mina class get reading corner with bookshelf.

Our class get reading corner. Shelf get 20 books. 12 na about animals. 4 na about space, and 4 na story books. Teacher no buy new books this year.

Mina talk, 'Animal books na the most popular for our class.'
20261125-english-g05-2.principle: Text only tell number of books on shelf (12 animal books etc.). E no tell which books students read or borrow most, so we no fit check claim 'most popular'.
20261125-english-g05-2.example: Think wetin Mina mean by 'popular', then find sentence for text wey tell you that.
20261125-english-g05-2.actionItem: Think whether number information support claim (popular), and make English question wey fit check the claim.

20261125-english-g06-1.title: Book club dey succeed? Change your judgment as evidence increase
20261125-english-g06-1.summary: New book club start for our school. Teacher talk say, "Di club dey succeed." Dem go give you evidence one part at a time, and you go think whether di statement correct.
20261125-english-g06-1.principle: As data dey come one part at a time, change your judgment about di claim 'di book club dey succeed', then finish for English with two pieces of evidence.
20261125-english-g06-1.example: Separate wetin di data wey you get now confirm from wetin you still no know.
20261125-english-g06-1.actionItem: As data dey come one part at a time, change your judgment about di claim 'di book club dey succeed', then finish for English with two pieces of evidence.

20261125-english-g06-2.title: Make tables to find cases where claim true
20261125-english-g06-2.summary: 20 students in one class each vote one time for after-snack activity: soccer, art or music. Votes call s (soccer), a (art), and m (music).
20261125-english-g06-2.principle: 8 votes pass art (6) and music (6), so e get most votes; e below 10, half of 20, so e no reach half. Therefore a correct.
20261125-english-g06-2.example: Add 8, 6 and 6; find half of 20 students and compare.
20261125-english-g06-2.actionItem: Make several vote tables yourself where English claim 'e get most votes but no reach half the class' true.

20261125-english-g07-1.title: Ben go come party? Check hidden meaning of his answers
20261125-english-g07-1.summary:
Conversation between Jisu and Ben (na text only, no pictures):

Jisu: You wan come my birthday party on Saturday?
Ben: Saturday? Hmm. I get soccer game for morning.
Jisu: Di party start for 4 p.m.
Ben: Oh, that might work. I go probably dey tired, though.
Jisu: So... you dey come?
Ben: Make I check with my mom first.
20261125-english-g07-1.principle: Football match na morning, party na 4 p.m., so times no overlap. Ben only talk say e might be tired, and go check with mom.
20261125-english-g07-1.example: Break Ben words into four parts: 'football match,' 'party time,' 'tired,' and 'mom.'
20261125-english-g07-1.actionItem: Break Ben answers into lines, separate wetin don settle from wetin remain, then judge whether e go come.

20261125-english-g07-2.title: Does 'That's fine.' really mean say e okay?
20261125-english-g07-2.summary: Sam and Dad talk about Friday plans. Conversation go show in three parts, as text only.
20261125-english-g07-2.principle: Read more of conversation little by little, judge speaker inner feelings and revise your view as clues show.
20261125-english-g07-2.example: Find one new tone sign or word for this part.
20261125-english-g07-2.actionItem: Read more of conversation little by little, judge speaker inner feelings and revise your view as clues show.

20261125-english-g08-1.title: Rewrite claim say going library often raise scores
20261125-english-g08-1.summary: Blog writer wan say: 'Library visits make students' scores go up.' Make we check di sentence step by step.
20261125-english-g08-1.principle: As new data show one by one, judge again how sure you fit be about di claim, and rewrite final statement to fit all di data.
20261125-english-g08-1.example: Check each time whether new information support your earlier judgment or weaken am.
20261125-english-g08-1.actionItem: As new data show one by one, judge again how sure you fit be about di claim, and rewrite final statement to fit all di data.

20261125-english-g08-2.title: Fix line with wrong number in beach cleanup blog
20261125-english-g08-2.summary: One student in a class write this school blog post. (Text only; each line numbered.)
20261125-english-g08-2.principle: Line 3 say 30 bags collected first hour, line 4 say total 18. Total no fit less than first-hour part. Post no show whether line 3 or 4 wrong, so choose either.
20261125-english-g08-2.example: Collect only lines with numbers and compare them.
20261125-english-g08-2.actionItem: Find two number sentences in post wey conflict, rewrite to fit confirmed information.

20261125-english-g09-1.title: The hidden assumption inside 'we sold 200 fewer lunches'
20261125-english-g09-1.summary:
Dem post this for the notice board in front of the school cafeteria.

"This month, the cafeteria sold 200 fewer lunches than last month. So students did not like the new menu."
20261125-english-g09-1.principle: To move from the fact say sales drop to 'the food no suit their taste', other things (number of students, number of school days, etc.) must stay the same. If students or school days reduce, sales go drop even if people still like the food.
20261125-english-g09-1.example: First, write in your own language wetin fit cause 'fewer lunches were sold'.
20261125-english-g09-1.actionItem: Find the unstated assumption wey must be true for a claim to hold, then write in English another explanation wey fit weaken that assumption.

20261125-english-g09-2.title: Change restaurant choice as reviews arrive one by one
20261125-english-g09-2.summary: Family choose restaurant for lunch before movie starts 3:00 p.m. Lunch one hour, starting 12:30. Review information come one part at a time.
20261125-english-g09-2.principle: Read reviews stepwise, update judgment and write in English what conditions make rating trustworthy.
20261125-english-g09-2.example: Find one word or number for the first time wey you see inside this part.
20261125-english-g09-2.actionItem: Read reviews stepwise, update judgment and write in English what conditions make rating trustworthy.

20261125-english-g10-1.title: How we go report 2 conflicting school newsletter announcements?
20261125-english-g10-1.summary:
You dey school English newsletter editorial team. Two festival notices disagree.

School notice: 'Festival: Friday, 4 p.m., in gym. Free for all students.'
Student council poster: 'Festival: Friday, 5 p.m., in gym. Tickets: 1,000 won.'

You never confirm which one correct.
20261125-english-g10-1.principle: If no confirm yet, fairly state wetin both sources say and say dem still dey check. Choosing one side as fact or telling people no come without information go mislead.
20261125-english-g10-1.example: Compare information each announcement give and wetin e leave out.
20261125-english-g10-1.actionItem: Write for student readers fair account of 2 different notices; say wetin not confirmed and wetin readers should do.

20261125-english-g10-2.title: One case enough to claim 'always'?
20261125-english-g10-2.summary:
This na part of text from school newspaper (line numbers start at 1).
1) Our school suppose ban phones from building.
2) Last month, Mina get new phone, and her math score drop from 90 to 75.
3) So phone clearly make every student's grade worse.
4) Also phone dey make noise in hallway, and some students check answers during tests.
5) So school suppose ban dem for everybody.
20261125-english-g10-2.principle: Line 3 na problem. Saying grades 'surely' worsen for 'all students' from only one student's score drop (line 2) claim pass evidence. Score fit drop for other reason, like test difficulty or situation. Line 4 get separate reason (noise, cheating), so judge am separately. Line 5 'ban for everybody' depend on this too, but first problem show for line 3.
20261125-english-g10-2.example: For each line separate 'wetin report' from 'wetin conclude'.
20261125-english-g10-2.actionItem: For argumentative text, find line where evidence no support claim enough; rewrite it more carefully and decide what more evidence need.

20261125-english-g11-1.title: Unclear work instruction: wetin you ask first?
20261125-english-g11-1.summary:
Email team leader Ms. Han send intern Jiho:

Hi Jiho,
Please send sales summary to client before meeting.
Thanks,
Ms. Han

Jiho knows: team calendar show Aurora Co. meeting Tuesday at 10:00 and Blue Pine Ltd. Thursday at 14:00. Shared folder has separate July, August and September sales files.
20261125-english-g11-1.principle: If client and period undecided, you fit send wrong file to wrong client. For format, choose default like PDF and tell her; her being at work no relate to task itself.
20261125-english-g11-1.example: Check whether 'to who', 'which file' and 'by when' each point to one clear thing in email.
20261125-english-g11-1.actionItem: From vague work email, choose info you must confirm before action; write question email easy to answer.

20261125-english-g11-2.title: Na reading club cause am? What info go show us?
20261125-english-g11-2.summary:
This na part of student council report.

'Students wey join school reading club get higher English test scores than students wey no join (average 82 vs 74). So reading club raise English scores.'

Student Mina want check whether conclusion correct. Students join club if dem choose to apply.
20261125-english-g11-2.principle: If you know scores from before joining, you fit check whether members already high or score rose after joining. Since students choose apply, more students already good at English fit join.
20261125-english-g11-2.example: Think how voluntary application fit affect starting difference between the two groups.
20261125-english-g11-2.actionItem: Choose information needed to tell whether score gap between club members and nonmembers na club effect; write English question to get am.

20261125-english-g12-1.title: Students wey eat breakfast get higher grades: wetin else we need know?
20261125-english-g12-1.summary:
This na claim in school article: 'Students wey eat breakfast get higher test scores, so school suppose provide free breakfast.' Evidence na survey of 200 students:

Group | Number of students | Average score
Students wey eat breakfast | 130 | 82
Students wey skip breakfast | 70 | 74
20261125-english-g12-1.principle: b check other causes (sleep, study time), c checks actual intervention result, e checks fairness of comparison. a and d no be evidence whether breakfast raise scores.
20261125-english-g12-1.example: Check whether each information answer 'Does breakfast-score connection mean cause?'
20261125-english-g12-1.actionItem: Judge whether survey result tell cause; choose extra info needed and propose English comparison method to check effect of free meals.

20261125-english-g12-2.title: Same event, different headlines: judgment change as information increase
20261125-english-g12-2.summary: Article about city council decision to raise parking fees near station go show in stages. See whether your judgment change as information increase.
20261125-english-g12-2.principle: As details increase, revise judgment how headline tone and omissions tilt from facts; explain one thing in English.
20261125-english-g12-2.example: Separate headline words wey state facts from words showing feeling.
20261125-english-g12-2.actionItem: As details increase, revise judgment how headline tone and omissions tilt from facts; explain one thing in English.

20261119-korean-l1-1.title: Which sign show di way to parking lot?
20261119-korean-l1-1.summary:
Visitor drive up to school and wan park car for one hour. Three signs dey there (no pictures; dem describe am with words).

Sign A: white letters ‘주차 금지’ on red board. Red circle with diagonal line cross small car picture. Dem fix am to school fence.
Sign B: blue board, white letters ‘방문자 주차장’ and arrow point right. E stand beside road.
Sign C: green board, white letters ‘주차장 출구’ and arrow point back toward road. E hang above narrow lane where cars dey drive out.

Words: 주차(장) = parking (lot); 방문자 = visitor; 입구 = entrance; 출구 = exit.
20261119-korean-l1-1.principle: Sign B na for visitors, e name parking lot and show direction. Sign A get same first word but symbol say no parking. Sign C name parking lot too, but 출구 mean exit, so e show where cars dey leave.
20261119-korean-l1-1.example: List wetin each sign talk with words, and wetin symbol or arrow add.
20261119-korean-l1-1.actionItem: Read three short road signs, join di words with arrow and symbol described, then judge which one really lead visitor to park; defend your answer when friend read only half.

20261119-korean-l1-2.title: Wetin time you fit enter library?
20261119-korean-l1-2.summary:
Sign for library door (one line each row):

도서관
오전 9시 ~ 오후 6시
낮 12시 ~ 1시 쉬어요
일요일 쉬어요

Words: 오전 = a.m.; 오후 = p.m.; 낮 = midday; 쉬어요 = (it) rests; ~ na ‘to’ (from ... to ...). You wan visit on Wednesday.
20261119-korean-l1-2.principle: Lines 2 and 3 apply to every normal day. Line 1 na di name and line 4 only talk about Sunday.
20261119-korean-l1-2.example: For each line, ask: e apply on Wednesday?
20261119-korean-l1-2.actionItem: Read sign wey get several lines, decide which lines matter for one day, then find different arrival times wey meet all of dem.

20261119-korean-l2-1.title: Who dey leave, who dey stay?
20261119-korean-l2-1.summary:
지우 na student and speak politely to adults. 지우 say goodbye three times. Check who walk away and who stay.

Scene 1: 지우 finish talking inside 선생님 room and walk out. 선생님 stay at desk.
Scene 2: 지우 and 선생님 leave school together. For gate dem walk different directions.
Scene 3: 지우 eat dinner at 할머니 house. Then 지우 go home. 할머니 stay home.
20261119-korean-l2-1.principle: Person wey leave say 안녕히 계세요 to person wey stay. 지우 walk out and 선생님 stay at desk.
20261119-korean-l2-1.example: Ask: who dey walk away, who stay inside room?
20261119-korean-l2-1.actionItem: Choose correct goodbye based on who dey leave and who dey stay, notice situation where both leave, and write polite goodbye with thanks.

korean-l2-1.title: Who dey leave, who dey stay?
korean-l2-1.summary:
지우 na student and speak politely to adults. 지우 say goodbye three times. Check who walk away and who stay.

Scene 2: 지우 and 선생님 leave school together. For gate dem walk different directions.
Scene 3: 지우 eat dinner at 할머니 house. Then 지우 go home. 할머니 stay home.

korean-l2-1.actionItem: Choose correct goodbye based on who dey leave and who dey stay, notice situation where both leave, and write polite goodbye with thanks.

20261119-korean-l2-2.title: Thank-you to friend, thank-you to teacher
20261119-korean-l2-2.summary: 서준 give book to classmate, and classmate write back: ‘책 줘서 고마워!’ Now 서준 teacher give 서준 book, and 서준 wan send almost same message to teacher.
20261119-korean-l2-2.principle: Both verb about wetin teacher do (줘서 change to 주셔서) and thank-you word (고마워 change to 고맙습니다 or 감사합니다) show relationship, and meaning must stay ‘thank you for giving me book.’
20261119-korean-l2-2.example: Check two things in each choice: verb for wetin teacher do and thank-you word.
20261119-korean-l2-2.actionItem: Choose thank-you wey fit teacher, then rewrite message with your own words.

korean-l2-2.title: Thank-you to friend, thank-you to teacher
korean-l2-2.summary: 서준 give book to classmate, and classmate write back: ‘책 줘서 고마워!’ Now 서준 teacher give 서준 book, and 서준 wan send almost same message to teacher.
korean-l2-2.principle: Both verb about wetin teacher do (줘서 change to 주셔서) and thank-you word (고마워 change to 고맙습니다 or 감사합니다) show relationship, and meaning must stay ‘thank you for giving me book.’
korean-l2-2.example: Check two things in each choice: verb for wetin teacher do and thank-you word.
korean-l2-2.actionItem: Choose thank-you wey fit teacher, then rewrite message with your own words.

20261119-korean-l3-1.title: Who give pocket money?
20261119-korean-l3-1.summary:
Two classmates, 지우 and 하나, dey chat using polite -요 speech. Korean often leave out subject (person doing action). (댁 = respectful word for somebody house.)

지우: 어제 뭐 했어요?
하나: 할머니 댁에 갔어요. 맛있는 밥을 먹었어요. 용돈도 주셨어요.
지우: 좋았겠어요!
20261119-korean-l3-1.principle: Text no name subject, but verb form show giver na person wey deserve respect, and only that person in story na 할머니, whose house 하나 visit. ‘Probably’ fit because text no state am directly.

korean-l3-1.title: Who give pocket money?
korean-l3-1.summary:
Two classmates, 지우 and 하나, dey chat using polite -요 speech. Korean often leave out subject (person doing action). (댁 = respectful word for somebody house.)

지우: 어제 뭐 했어요?

지우: 좋았겠어요!

20261119-korean-l6-2.title: Which draft senior go say yes to?
20261119-korean-l6-2.summary:
You first-year university student. 민준 선배 club senior, 3 years older; you talk only twice. He take good notes last week. Exam tomorrow afternoon and you wan see notes today. Four drafts:

A: 선배, 지난주 필기 보내 줘요. 내일 시험이에요.
B: 선배님, 혹시 지난주 필기를 사진으로 보내 주실 수 있을까요? 내일 시험이라서요.
C: 선배님, 바쁘시겠지만 시간 되실 때 아무 때나 지난주 필기를 보여 주시면 정말 감사하겠습니다.
D: 선배님, 필기 보내 주세요. 안 보내 주시면 저 시험 망해요.
20261119-korean-l6-2.principle: Draft B ask whether possible (혹시 + -(으)ㄹ 수 있을까요), give reason, and reason show deadline. Draft C very respectful but never say it needed tomorrow, so senior fit reply next week. Draft A no enough respect for distant senior; D pressure am.
20261119-korean-l6-2.example: Compare who each draft sound like it dey address.
20261119-korean-l6-2.actionItem: Judge four draft requests by wording and explain what make request easy to accept and which polite-looking drafts still fail.

20261121-korean-l1-1.title: Which sign show di way to parking lot?
20261121-korean-l1-1.summary:
Visitor drive up to school and wan park car for one hour. Three signs dey there (no pictures; dem describe am with words).

Sign A: white letters ‘주차 금지’ on red board. Red circle with diagonal line cross small car picture. Dem fix am to school fence.
Sign B: blue board, white letters ‘방문자 주차장’ and arrow point right. E stand beside road.
Sign C: green board, white letters ‘주차장 출구’ and arrow point back toward road. E hang above narrow lane where cars dey drive out.

Words: 주차(장) = parking (lot); 방문자 = visitor; 입구 = entrance; 출구 = exit.
20261121-korean-l1-1.principle: Sign B na for visitors, e name parking lot and show direction. Sign A get same first word but symbol say no parking. Sign C name parking lot too, but 출구 mean exit, so e show where cars dey leave.
20261121-korean-l1-1.example: List wetin each sign talk with words, and wetin symbol or arrow add.
20261121-korean-l1-1.actionItem: Read three short road signs, join di words with arrow and symbol described, then judge which one really lead visitor to park; defend your answer when friend read only half.

20261121-korean-l1-2.title: Wetin time you fit enter library?
20261121-korean-l1-2.summary:
Sign for library door (one line each row):

도서관
오전 9시 ~ 오후 6시
낮 12시 ~ 1시 쉬어요
일요일 쉬어요

Words: 오전 = a.m.; 오후 = p.m.; 낮 = midday; 쉬어요 = (it) rests; ~ na ‘to’ (from ... to ...). You wan visit on Wednesday.
20261121-korean-l1-2.principle: Lines 2 and 3 apply to every normal day. Line 1 na di name and line 4 only talk about Sunday.
20261121-korean-l1-2.example: For each line, ask: e apply on Wednesday?
20261121-korean-l1-2.actionItem: Read sign wey get several lines, decide which lines matter for one day, then find different arrival times wey meet all of dem.

20261121-korean-l2-1.title: Who dey leave, who dey stay?
20261121-korean-l2-1.summary:
지우 na student and speak politely to adults. 지우 say goodbye three times. Check who walk away and who stay.

Scene 1: 지우 finish talking inside 선생님 room and walk out. 선생님 stay at desk.
Scene 2: 지우 and 선생님 leave school together. For gate dem walk different directions.
Scene 3: 지우 eat dinner at 할머니 house. Then 지우 go home. 할머니 stay home.
20261121-korean-l2-1.principle: Person wey leave say 안녕히 계세요 to person wey stay. 지우 walk out and 선생님 stay at desk.
20261121-korean-l2-1.example: Ask: who dey walk away, who stay inside room?
20261121-korean-l2-1.actionItem: Choose correct goodbye based on who dey leave and who dey stay, notice situation where both leave, and write polite goodbye with thanks.

20261121-korean-l2-2.title: Thank-you to friend, thank-you to teacher
20261121-korean-l2-2.summary: 서준 give book to classmate, and classmate write back: ‘책 줘서 고마워!’ Now 서준 teacher give 서준 book, and 서준 wan send almost same message to teacher.
20261121-korean-l2-2.principle: Both verb about wetin teacher do (줘서 change to 주셔서) and thank-you word (고마워 change to 고맙습니다 or 감사합니다) show relationship, and meaning must stay ‘thank you for giving me book.’
20261121-korean-l2-2.example: Check two things in each choice: verb for wetin teacher do and thank-you word.
20261121-korean-l2-2.actionItem: Choose thank-you wey fit teacher, then rewrite message with your own words.

20261118-life-all.title: Leave the Microwave Center Empty
20261118-life-all.summary: Arranging food in a ring on the plate makes a microwave heat more evenly.
20261118-life-all.principle: Microwaves at 2.45GHz form standing waves with wavelength λ = c/f ≈ 12.2cm, creating hot and cold spots.
20261118-life-all.example: The plate center often gets less energy and stays cold. A ring layout plus one stir midway can cut temperature differences by 20°C or more.
20261118-life-all.actionItem: Today arrange food in a ring with the middle empty and stir halfway through.

20261119-life-all-2.title: Bubble Wrap Window Insulation
20261119-life-all-2.summary: Sticking bubble wrap to a window traps still air that cuts heat loss sharply.
20261119-life-all-2.principle: Still air conducts only about 0.026W/m · K, 1/40 of glass (1.0). In Q = UAΔT the coefficient U falls.
20261119-life-all-2.example: A 2m² single pane with a 20°C indoor-outdoor gap and U ≈ 5.8 loses 232W. Bubble wrap lowering U to about 3.5 gives 140W, saving roughly 90W.
20261119-life-all-2.actionItem: Today spray water on a window and press bubble wrap, flat side to the glass.

20261126-english-g03-1.principle: Free time start at 10 a.m.; from 12 to 14 lunch and dance class fill the time. Schedule get no activity from 15 to 16 or 16 to 17, and dem finish before dinner.
20261126-english-g03-1.example: Change schedule times to 24-hour numbers and draw time line.
20261126-english-g03-1.actionItem: Think of different reading start times wey meet all schedule conditions, and explain why other times no work.

20261126-english-g04-1.title: Mama note and Jisu playtime
20261126-english-g04-1.summary:
Note wey Mama leave for table (na text only, no picture):

Mina,
Today's plan:
3:30 p.m. Come home.
4:00 p.m. Piano class (30 minutes).
5:00 p.m. Throw away di trash.
6:30 p.m. Dinner with Mama and Papa.

Then her friend Jisu send message. "Make we play for park from 4:15 to 5:15 today!"
20261126-english-g04-1.principle: Piano class na 4:00-4:30, so 4:15-4:30 overlap, and throwing away trash for 5:00 fall inside 4:15-5:15. Coming home for 3:30 and dinner for 6:30 dey outside di park time.
20261126-english-g04-1.example: Put each line beside di park time '4:15-5:15' one by one, and check whether e finish before or start after.
20261126-english-g04-1.actionItem: Compare di different plans for Mama note with di time wey friend suggest, find where dem no fit together, then say no for English and suggest another time.

20261126-english-g05-1.title: Your thinking change as you read poster
20261126-english-g05-1.summary: Jun no be member of Green Library. Friend Ara na member. Both go read poster in front of library one line at a time.
20261126-english-g05-1.principle: Each time poster info appear step by step, update your judgment and make English question to check information wey poster no give.
20261126-english-g05-1.example: Check whether the new sentence change your earlier judgment.
20261126-english-g05-1.actionItem: Each time poster info appear step by step, update your judgment and make English question to check information wey poster no give.

20261126-english-g06-1.title: Book club dey succeed? Change your judgment as evidence increase
20261126-english-g06-1.summary: New book club start for our school. Teacher talk say, "Di club dey succeed." Dem go give you evidence one part at a time, and you go think whether di statement correct.
20261126-english-g06-1.principle: As data dey come one part at a time, change your judgment about di claim 'di book club dey succeed', then finish for English with two pieces of evidence.
20261126-english-g06-1.example: Separate wetin di data wey you get now confirm from wetin you still no know.
20261126-english-g06-1.actionItem: As data dey come one part at a time, change your judgment about di claim 'di book club dey succeed', then finish for English with two pieces of evidence.

20261126-english-g07-1.title: Ben go come party? Check hidden meaning of his answers
20261126-english-g07-1.summary:
Conversation between Jisu and Ben (na text only, no pictures):

Jisu: You wan come my birthday party on Saturday?
Ben: Saturday? Hmm. I get soccer game for morning.
Jisu: Di party start for 4 p.m.
Ben: Oh, that might work. I go probably dey tired, though.
Jisu: So... you dey come?
Ben: Make I check with my mom first.
20261126-english-g07-1.principle: Football match na morning, party na 4 p.m., so times no overlap. Ben only talk say e might be tired, and go check with mom.
20261126-english-g07-1.example: Break Ben words into four parts: 'football match,' 'party time,' 'tired,' and 'mom.'
20261126-english-g07-1.actionItem: Break Ben answers into lines, separate wetin don settle from wetin remain, then judge whether e go come.

20261126-english-g08-1.title: Rewrite claim say going library often raise scores
20261126-english-g08-1.summary: Blog writer wan say: 'Library visits make students' scores go up.' Make we check di sentence step by step.
20261126-english-g08-1.principle: As new data show one by one, judge again how sure you fit be about di claim, and rewrite final statement to fit all di data.
20261126-english-g08-1.example: Check each time whether new information support your earlier judgment or weaken am.
20261126-english-g08-1.actionItem: As new data show one by one, judge again how sure you fit be about di claim, and rewrite final statement to fit all di data.

20261126-english-g09-1.title: The hidden assumption inside 'we sold 200 fewer lunches'
20261126-english-g09-1.summary:
Dem post this for the notice board in front of the school cafeteria.

"This month, the cafeteria sold 200 fewer lunches than last month. So students did not like the new menu."
20261126-english-g09-1.principle: To move from the fact say sales drop to 'the food no suit their taste', other things (number of students, number of school days, etc.) must stay the same. If students or school days reduce, sales go drop even if people still like the food.
20261126-english-g09-1.example: First, write in your own language wetin fit cause 'fewer lunches were sold'.
20261126-english-g09-1.actionItem: Find the unstated assumption wey must be true for a claim to hold, then write in English another explanation wey fit weaken that assumption.

20261126-english-g10-1.title: How we go report 2 conflicting school newsletter announcements?
20261126-english-g10-1.summary:
You dey school English newsletter editorial team. Two festival notices disagree.

School notice: 'Festival: Friday, 4 p.m., in gym. Free for all students.'
Student council poster: 'Festival: Friday, 5 p.m., in gym. Tickets: 1,000 won.'

You never confirm which one correct.
20261126-english-g10-1.principle: If no confirm yet, fairly state wetin both sources say and say dem still dey check. Choosing one side as fact or telling people no come without information go mislead.
20261126-english-g10-1.example: Compare information each announcement give and wetin e leave out.
20261126-english-g10-1.actionItem: Write for student readers fair account of 2 different notices; say wetin not confirmed and wetin readers should do.

20261126-english-g11-1.title: Unclear work instruction: wetin you ask first?
20261126-english-g11-1.summary:
Email team leader Ms. Han send intern Jiho:

Hi Jiho,
Please send sales summary to client before meeting.
Thanks,
Ms. Han

Jiho knows: team calendar show Aurora Co. meeting Tuesday at 10:00 and Blue Pine Ltd. Thursday at 14:00. Shared folder has separate July, August and September sales files.
20261126-english-g11-1.principle: If client and period undecided, you fit send wrong file to wrong client. For format, choose default like PDF and tell her; her being at work no relate to task itself.
20261126-english-g11-1.example: Check whether 'to who', 'which file' and 'by when' each point to one clear thing in email.
20261126-english-g11-1.actionItem: From vague work email, choose info you must confirm before action; write question email easy to answer.

20261126-english-g12-1.title: Students wey eat breakfast get higher grades: wetin else we need know?
20261126-english-g12-1.summary:
This na claim in school article: 'Students wey eat breakfast get higher test scores, so school suppose provide free breakfast.' Evidence na survey of 200 students:

Group | Number of students | Average score
Students wey eat breakfast | 130 | 82
Students wey skip breakfast | 70 | 74
20261126-english-g12-1.principle: b check other causes (sleep, study time), c checks actual intervention result, e checks fairness of comparison. a and d no be evidence whether breakfast raise scores.
20261126-english-g12-1.example: Check whether each information answer 'Does breakfast-score connection mean cause?'
20261126-english-g12-1.actionItem: Judge whether survey result tell cause; choose extra info needed and propose English comparison method to check effect of free meals.

20261126-korean-l1-1.title: Which sign show di way to parking lot?
20261126-korean-l1-1.summary:
Visitor drive up to school and wan park car for one hour. Three signs dey there (no pictures; dem describe am with words).

Sign A: white letters ‘주차 금지’ on red board. Red circle with diagonal line cross small car picture. Dem fix am to school fence.
Sign B: blue board, white letters ‘방문자 주차장’ and arrow point right. E stand beside road.
Sign C: green board, white letters ‘주차장 출구’ and arrow point back toward road. E hang above narrow lane where cars dey drive out.

Words: 주차(장) = parking (lot); 방문자 = visitor; 입구 = entrance; 출구 = exit.
20261126-korean-l1-1.principle: Sign B na for visitors, e name parking lot and show direction. Sign A get same first word but symbol say no parking. Sign C name parking lot too, but 출구 mean exit, so e show where cars dey leave.
20261126-korean-l1-1.example: List wetin each sign talk with words, and wetin symbol or arrow add.
20261126-korean-l1-1.actionItem: Read three short road signs, join di words with arrow and symbol described, then judge which one really lead visitor to park; defend your answer when friend read only half.

20261126-korean-l2-1.title: Who dey leave, who dey stay?
20261126-korean-l2-1.summary:
지우 na student and speak politely to adults. 지우 say goodbye three times. Check who walk away and who stay.

Scene 1: 지우 finish talking inside 선생님 room and walk out. 선생님 stay at desk.
Scene 2: 지우 and 선생님 leave school together. For gate dem walk different directions.
Scene 3: 지우 eat dinner at 할머니 house. Then 지우 go home. 할머니 stay home.
20261126-korean-l2-1.principle: Person wey leave say 안녕히 계세요 to person wey stay. 지우 walk out and 선생님 stay at desk.
20261126-korean-l2-1.example: Ask: who dey walk away, who stay inside room?
20261126-korean-l2-1.actionItem: Choose correct goodbye based on who dey leave and who dey stay, notice situation where both leave, and write polite goodbye with thanks.

20261126-korean-l3-1.title: Who give pocket money?
20261126-korean-l3-1.summary:
Two classmates, 지우 and 하나, dey chat using polite -요 speech. Korean often leave out subject (person doing action). (댁 = respectful word for somebody house.)

지우: 어제 뭐 했어요?
하나: 할머니 댁에 갔어요. 맛있는 밥을 먹었어요. 용돈도 주셨어요.
지우: 좋았겠어요!
20261126-korean-l3-1.principle: Text no name subject, but verb form show giver na person wey deserve respect, and only that person in story na 할머니, whose house 하나 visit. ‘Probably’ fit because text no state am directly.
20261126-korean-l3-1.example: Check ending of 주셨어요 and compare with 먹었어요 in line before.
20261126-korean-l3-1.actionItem: Guess who omitted subject refer to, point to text clues and explain how guess change if one clue disappear.

20261126-korean-l4-1.title: Book the room
20261126-korean-l4-1.summary:
Your team wan use after-school room. Read notice and message from teammate 서준.

[방과 후 교실 이용 안내]
- 이용 시간: 오후 1시 ~ 6시
- 한 번에 1시간이나 2시간 쓸 수 있어요.
- 오후 3시 ~ 4시는 청소 시간이라 쓸 수 없어요.

서준: 저는 수업이 2시에 끝나서 2시 전에는 갈 수 없어요. 시작 시간은 정각으로 해 주세요.
20261126-korean-l4-1.principle: 2시 ~ 4시 include 3시 ~ 4시, when room dey cleaned. Check full time of every plan, no be only start.
20261126-korean-l4-1.example: Write start hour and end hour of plan.
20261126-korean-l4-1.actionItem: Join room rules from notice with teammate message and find different booking plans wey meet all conditions.

20261126-korean-l5-1.title: School trip notice with time problem
20261126-korean-l5-1.summary: Your class get this notice from teacher by message.
20261126-korean-l5-1.principle: Lines 3 and 4 clash: class arrive park at 11:30, but lunch ‘after arriving’ dey 11:00. Lines 1, 2 and 5 fit together.
20261126-korean-l5-1.example: Put times from lines in order and compare dem.
20261126-korean-l5-1.actionItem: Find clash in trip notice, decide wetin you can conclude, and ask polite question to clear am up.

20261126-korean-l6-1.title: Where do I apply?
20261126-korean-l6-1.summary: E be 4:20 p.m. You dey counter at neighborhood 주민센터. You wan apply for passport. You no sure if passport photo dey your bag.
20261126-korean-l6-1.principle: Change how you understand official reply as more of exchange show, then ask sensible follow-up.
20261126-korean-l6-1.example: Decide using only wetin you don read so far.
20261126-korean-l6-1.actionItem: Change how you understand official reply as more of exchange show, then ask sensible follow-up.

20261126-life-all-1.title: Leave the Microwave Center Empty
20261126-life-all-1.summary: Arranging food in a ring on the plate makes a microwave heat more evenly.
20261126-life-all-1.principle: Microwaves at 2.45GHz form standing waves with wavelength λ = c/f ≈ 12.2cm, creating hot and cold spots.
20261126-life-all-1.example: The plate center often gets less energy and stays cold. A ring layout plus one stir midway can cut temperature differences by 20°C or more.
20261126-life-all-1.actionItem: Today arrange food in a ring with the middle empty and stir halfway through.
